So the old woman went to the Wicked Witch of the East, and promised her two sheep and a cow if she would prevent the marriage. Thereupon the Wicked Witch enchanted my axe, and when I was chopping away at my best one day, for I was anxious to get the new house and my wife as soon as possible, the axe slipped all at once and cut off my left leg.
passages.vernacular: 「有一個芒奇金姑娘,咁美麗,我好快就全心全意愛上咗佢。佢呢,答應等我賺夠錢畀佢蓋一所更好嘅房子就嫁畀我;所以我比以前更努力工作。但嗰姑娘同一個老太太住喺一起,老太太唔想佢嫁畀任何人,因為佢太懶,希望女孩留喺佢身邊,為佢做飯、做家務。所以老太太去找東方惡女巫,答應畀佢兩隻羊同一頭牛,只要佢阻止呢場婚事。於是惡女巫畀我嘅斧頭施咗魔法,有一天我正拚命砍住,因為我急著想盡快得到新房子同妻子,斧頭突然一滑,砍掉咗我嘅左腿。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有一個芒奇金姑娘,那麼美麗,我很快就全心全意愛上了她。她呢,答應等我賺夠錢給她蓋一所更好的房子就嫁給我;所以我比以前更努力工作。但那姑娘同一個老太太住在一起,老太太不想她嫁給任何人,因為她太懶,希望女孩留在她身邊,為她做飯、做家務。所以老太太去找東方惡女巫,答應給她兩隻羊和一頭牛,只要她阻止這場婚事。於是惡女巫給我的斧頭施了魔法,有一天我正拚命砍著,因為我急著想盡快得到新房子和妻子,斧頭突然一滑,砍掉了我的左腿。

passages.original: “This at first seemed a great misfortune, for I knew a one-legged man could not do very well as a wood-chopper. So I went to a tinsmith and had him make me a new leg out of tin. The leg worked very well, once I was used to it. But my action angered the Wicked Witch of the East, for she had promised the old woman I should not marry the pretty Munchkin girl. When I began chopping again, my axe slipped and cut off my right leg. Again I went to the tinsmith, and again he made me a leg out of tin. After this the enchanted axe cut off my arms, one after the other; but, nothing daunted, I had them replaced with tin ones. The Wicked Witch then made the axe slip and cut off my head, and at first I thought that was the end of me. But the tinsmith happened to come along, and he made me a new head out of tin.
passages.vernacular: 「起初呢似乎係個好大嘅不幸,因為我知道一個獨腿嘅人做伐木工幹不好。所以我去找一個錫匠,請佢用錫畀我做一條新腿。呢條腿一旦習慣喇,用起嚟好好。但我嘅行動激怒咗東方惡女巫,因為佢向老太太保證我唔會娶嗰個漂亮嘅芒奇金姑娘。我又開始砍樹時,斧頭滑喇,砍掉咗我嘅右腿。我又去找錫匠,佢又畀我做咗一條錫腿。此後嗰把被施咗魔法嘅斧頭一個接一個地砍掉咗我嘅手臂;但我毫不氣餒,換上咗錫嘅。然後惡女巫讓斧頭滑落,砍掉咗我嘅頭,起初我以為我完喇。但錫匠碰巧經過,佢用錫畀我做咗一個新頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「起初這似乎是個很大的不幸,因為我知道一個獨腿的人做伐木工幹不好。所以我去找一個錫匠,請他用錫給我做一條新腿。這條腿一旦習慣了,用起來很好。但我的行動激怒了東方惡女巫,因為她向老太太保證我不會娶那個漂亮的芒奇金姑娘。我又開始砍樹時,斧頭滑了,砍掉了我的右腿。我又去找錫匠,他又給我做了一條錫腿。此後那把被施了魔法的斧頭一個接一個地砍掉了我的手臂;但我毫不氣餒,換上了錫的。然後惡女巫讓斧頭滑落,砍掉了我的頭,起初我以為我完了。但錫匠碰巧經過,他用錫給我做了一個新頭。

passages.original: “I thought I had beaten the Wicked Witch then, and I worked harder than ever; but I little knew how cruel my enemy could be. She thought of a new way to kill my love for the beautiful Munchkin maiden, and made my axe slip again, so that it cut right through my body, splitting me into two halves. Once more the tinsmith came to my help and made me a body of tin, fastening my tin arms and legs and head to it, by means of joints, so that I could move around as well as ever. But, alas! I had now no heart, so that I lost all my love for the Munchkin girl, and did not care whether I married her or not. I suppose she is still living with the old woman, waiting for me to come after her.
passages.vernacular: 「我以為嗰時我已戰勝咗惡女巫,我比以前更努力工作;但我好少知道我嘅敵人可以幾咁殘忍。佢想出咗一個新辦法殺死我對美麗芒奇金少女嘅愛,又讓我嘅斧頭滑落,直接砍穿我嘅身體,把我劈成咗兩半。錫匠再一次嚟幫我,畀我做咗一個錫身體,用關節把我嘅錫手臂、錫腿同頭連喺上面,使我能像以前一樣活動。但係,唉!我而家冇心,所以我對芒奇金姑娘嘅愛全部消失喇,我不在乎係咪娶佢。我想佢仍同老太太住喺一起,等住我去找佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我以為那時我已戰勝了惡女巫,我比以前更努力工作;但我很少知道我的敵人可以多麼殘忍。她想出了一個新辦法殺死我對美麗芒奇金少女的愛,又讓我的斧頭滑落,直接砍穿我的身體,把我劈成了兩半。錫匠再一次來幫我,給我做了一個錫身體,用關節把我的錫手臂、錫腿和頭連在上面,使我能像以前一樣活動。但是,唉!我現在沒有心,所以我對芒奇金姑娘的愛全部消失了,我不在乎是否娶她。我想她仍同老太太住在一起,等著我去找她。

passages.original: “My body shone so brightly in the sun that I felt very proud of it and it did not matter now if my axe slipped, for it could not cut me. There was only one danger—that my joints would rust; but I kept an oil-can in my cottage and took care to oil myself whenever I needed it. However, there came a day when I forgot to do this, and, being caught in a rainstorm, before I thought of the danger my joints had rusted, and I was left to stand in the woods until you came to help me. It was a terrible thing to undergo, but during the year I stood there I had time to think that the greatest loss I had known was the loss of my heart. While I was in love I was the happiest man on earth; but no one can love who has not a heart, and so I am resolved to ask Oz to give me one. If he does, I will go back to the Munchkin maiden and marry her.”
passages.vernacular: 「我嘅身體喺陽光下閃閃發亮,我為此感到好自豪,而家斧頭滑落都冇關係,因為佢砍唔到我。只有一種危險——我嘅關節會生鏽;但我喺小屋裡放咗一個油壺,小心地喺需要時畀自己上油。然而,有一天我忘咗咁樣做,被一場暴雨淋到,我仲冇想到危險,我嘅關節就生鏽喇,我被留喺樹林裡站住,直到你哋嚟幫我。呢個係一件好可怕嘅經歷,但喺我站喺嗰度嘅一年中,我有時間去想,我所知嘅最大損失係失去我嘅心。我戀愛時,我係世上最快樂嘅人;但冇心嘅人唔能夠愛,所以我決心請奧茲畀我一顆。如果佢畀,我就回到芒奇金少女嗰度,同佢結婚。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我的身體在陽光下閃閃發亮,我為此感到非常自豪,現在斧頭滑落也沒關係,因為它砍不到我。只有一種危險——我的關節會生鏽;但我在小屋裡放了一個油壺,小心地在需要時給自己上油。然而,有一天我忘了這樣做,被一場暴雨淋到,我還沒想到危險,我的關節就生鏽了,我被留在樹林裡站著,直到你們來幫我。這是一件很可怕的經歷,但在我站在那裡的一年中,我有時間去想,我所知的最大損失是失去我的心。我戀愛時,我是世上最快樂的人;但沒有心的人不能愛,所以我決心請奧茲給我一顆。如果他給,我就回到芒奇金少女那裡,與她結婚。」

passages.original: Both Dorothy and the Scarecrow had been greatly interested in the story of the Tin Woodman, and now they knew why he was so anxious to get a new heart.
passages.vernacular: 桃樂絲同稻草人都對鐵皮樵夫嘅故事好感興趣,而家佢哋知道佢點解咁急於得到一顆新嘅心喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 桃樂絲和稻草人都對鐵皮樵夫的故事很感興趣,現在他們知道他為什麼那麼急於得到一顆新的心了。

passages.original: “All the same,” said the Scarecrow, “I shall ask for brains instead of a heart; for a fool would not know what to do with a heart if he had one.”
passages.vernacular: 「儘管如此,」稻草人講,「我定係要求腦子而唔係心;因為一個傻瓜即使有一顆心,都唔知道點算。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「儘管如此,」稻草人說,「我還是要求腦子而不是心;因為一個傻瓜即使有一顆心,也不知道怎麼辦。」

passages.original: “I shall take the heart,” returned the Tin Woodman; “for brains do not make one happy, and happiness is the best thing in the world.”
passages.vernacular: 「我要心,」鐵皮樵夫回答;「因為腦子唔能夠使人快樂,而快樂係世上最好嘅嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我要心,」鐵皮樵夫回答;「因為腦子不能使人快樂,而快樂是世上最好的東西。」

passages.original: Dorothy did not say anything, for she was puzzled to know which of her two friends was right, and she decided if she could only get back to Kansas and Aunt Em, it did not matter so much whether the Woodman had no brains and the Scarecrow no heart, or each got what he wanted.
passages.vernacular: 桃樂絲乜嘢都冇講,因為佢唔知道佢嘅兩個朋友邊個對,佢決定,只要佢能回到堪薩斯同艾姆嬸嬸身邊,樵夫冇腦子、稻草人冇心,或每人得到自己想要嘅,都冇咁重要。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 桃樂絲什麼也沒說,因為她不知道她的兩個朋友誰對,她決定,只要她能回到堪薩斯和艾姆嬸嬸身邊,樵夫沒有腦子、稻草人沒有心,或每人得到自己想要的,都沒有那麼重要。

passages.original: What worried her most was that the bread was nearly gone, and another meal for herself and Toto would empty the basket. To be sure, neither the Woodman nor the Scarecrow ever ate anything, but she was not made of tin nor straw, and could not live unless she was fed.
passages.vernacular: 最令佢擔心嘅係麵包快食完喇,佢自己同托托再食一頓就會把籃子食空。的確,樵夫同稻草人都從不食嘢,但佢唔係錫做嘅,都唔係稻草做嘅,不食嘢就唔能夠活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最令她擔心的是麵包快吃完了,她自己和托托再吃一頓就會把籃子吃空。的確,樵夫和稻草人都從不吃東西,但她不是錫做的,也不是稻草做的,不吃東西就不能活。

chapters.title: Chapter VI: The Cowardly Lion 第六章:膽小的獅子

passages.original: All this time Dorothy and her companions had been walking through the thick woods. The road was still paved with yellow brick, but these were much covered by dried branches and dead leaves from the trees, and the walking was not at all good.
passages.vernacular: 呢段時間,桃樂絲同佢嘅同伴哋一直喺走過茂密嘅樹林。路仍然係用黃磚鋪嘅,但呢啲磚大部分被樹上掉下嚟嘅乾樹枝同枯葉蓋住,走起嚟啲都不好走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這段時間,桃樂絲和她的同伴們一直在走過茂密的樹林。路仍然是用黃磚鋪的,但這些磚大部分被樹上掉下來的乾樹枝和枯葉蓋住,走起來一點也不好走。

passages.original: There were few birds in this part of the forest, for birds love the open country where there is plenty of sunshine. But now and then there came a deep growl from some wild animal hidden among the trees. These sounds made the little girl’s heart beat fast, for she did not know what made them; but Toto knew, and he walked close to Dorothy’s side, and did not even bark in return.
passages.vernacular: 森林嘅呢部分鳥好少,因為鳥愛有充足陽光嘅開闊鄉野。但時不時有從藏喺樹木間嘅某隻野獸發出嘅低沉咆哮。呢啲聲音使小女孩嘅心跳得好快,因為佢唔知道係乜嘢發出嘅;但托托知道,佢走喺桃樂絲身邊好近嘅地方,甚至不回吠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 森林的這部分鳥很少,因為鳥愛有充足陽光的開闊鄉野。但時不時有從藏在樹木間的某隻野獸發出的低沉咆哮。這些聲音使小女孩的心跳得很快,因為她不知道是什麼發出的;但托托知道,他走在桃樂絲身邊很近的地方,甚至不回吠。

passages.original: “How long will it be,” the child asked of the Tin Woodman, “before we are out of the forest?”
passages.vernacular: 「仲要多久,」細路問鐵皮樵夫,「我哋才能走出森林?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「還要多久,」孩子問鐵皮樵夫,「我們才能走出森林?」

passages.original: “I cannot tell,” was the answer, “for I have never been to the Emerald City. But my father went there once, when I was a boy, and he said it was a long journey through a dangerous country, although nearer to the city where Oz dwells the country is beautiful. But I am not afraid so long as I have my oil-can, and nothing can hurt the Scarecrow, while you bear upon your forehead the mark of the Good Witch’s kiss, and that will protect you from harm.”
passages.vernacular: 「我講不準,」回答係,「因為我從冇去過翡翠城。但我父親去過一次,嗰時我定係個男孩,佢講嗰個係穿過一個危險國家嘅長途旅程,雖然靠近奧茲居住嘅城市,鄉野係美麗嘅。但只要我有油壺,我就不怕,而且冇乜嘢能傷害稻草人,而你額頭上有好女巫嘅吻嘅印記,嗰會保護你不受傷害。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我說不準,」回答是,「因為我從沒去過翡翠城。但我父親去過一次,那時我還是個男孩,他說那是穿過一個危險國家的長途旅程,雖然靠近奧茲居住的城市,鄉野是美麗的。但只要我有油壺,我就不怕,而且沒有什麼能傷害稻草人,而你額頭上有好女巫的吻的印記,那會保護你不受傷害。」

passages.original: “But Toto!” said the girl anxiously. “What will protect him?”
passages.vernacular: 「但托托呢!」女孩焦急地講。「乜嘢嚟保護佢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但托托呢!」女孩焦急地說。「什麼來保護他?」

passages.original: “We must protect him ourselves if he is in danger,” replied the Tin Woodman.
passages.vernacular: 「如果佢有危險,我哋必須自己保護佢,」鐵皮樵夫回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果他有危險,我們必須自己保護他,」鐵皮樵夫回答。

passages.original: Just as he spoke there came from the forest a terrible roar, and the next moment a great Lion bounded into the road. With one blow of his paw he sent the Scarecrow spinning over and over to the edge of the road, and then he struck at the Tin Woodman with his sharp claws. But, to the Lion’s surprise, he could make no impression on the tin, although the Woodman fell over in the road and lay still.
passages.vernacular: 佢剛講完,森林裡就傳嚟一聲可怕嘅吼叫,下一刻一頭大獅子躍上咗路。佢一爪就把稻草人打得翻滾住到路邊,然後用鋒利嘅爪子打向鐵皮樵夫。但令獅子驚訝嘅係,佢對錫冇留下任何印象,雖然樵夫倒喺路上,躺住不動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他剛說完,森林裡就傳來一聲可怕的吼叫,下一刻一頭大獅子躍上了路。他一爪就把稻草人打得翻滾著到路邊,然後用鋒利的爪子打向鐵皮樵夫。但令獅子驚訝的是,他對錫沒有留下任何印象,雖然樵夫倒在路上,躺著不動。

passages.original: Little Toto, now that he had an enemy to face, ran barking toward the Lion, and the great beast had opened his mouth to bite the dog, when Dorothy, fearing Toto would be killed, and heedless of danger, rushed forward and slapped the Lion upon his nose as hard as she could, while she cried out:
passages.vernacular: 小托托而家有咗一個要面對嘅敵人,吠叫住跑向獅子,大野獸張開嘴要咬狗,呢陣桃樂絲怕托托被殺,不顧危險衝上前,盡全力打喺獅子嘅鼻子上,同時喊道:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小托托現在有了一個要面對的敵人,吠叫著跑向獅子,大野獸張開嘴要咬狗,這時桃樂絲怕托托被殺,不顧危險衝上前,盡全力打在獅子的鼻子上,同時喊道:

passages.original: “Don’t you dare to bite Toto! You ought to be ashamed of yourself, a big beast like you, to bite a poor little dog!”
passages.vernacular: 「你敢咬托托!你應該為自己感到羞恥,像你咁樣大嘅野獸,去咬一隻可憐嘅小狗!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你敢咬托托!你應該為自己感到羞恥,像你這樣大的野獸,去咬一隻可憐的小狗!」

passages.original: “I didn’t bite him,” said the Lion, as he rubbed his nose with his paw where Dorothy had hit it.
passages.vernacular: 「我冇咬佢,」獅子講,用爪子揉被桃樂絲打過嘅鼻子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我沒有咬他,」獅子說,用爪子揉被桃樂絲打過的鼻子。

passages.original: “No, but you tried to,” she retorted. “You are nothing but a big coward.”
passages.vernacular: 「冇,但你想咬,」佢反駁講。「你只不過係個大膽小鬼。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有,但你想咬,」她反駁說。「你只不過是個大膽小鬼。」

passages.original: “I know it,” said the Lion, hanging his head in shame. “I’ve always known it. But how can I help it?”
passages.vernacular: 「我知道,」獅子羞愧地垂下頭講。「我一直都知道。但我有乜嘢辦法呢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我知道,」獅子羞愧地垂下頭說。「我一直都知道。但我有什麼辦法呢?」

passages.original: “I don’t know, I’m sure. To think of your striking a stuffed man, like the poor Scarecrow!”
passages.vernacular: 「我確實唔知道。想想你竟然打一個塞滿嘢嘅人,像可憐嘅稻草人!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我確實不知道。想想你竟然打一個塞滿東西的人,像可憐的稻草人!」

passages.original: “Is he stuffed?” asked the Lion in surprise, as he watched her pick up the Scarecrow and set him upon his feet, while she patted him into shape again.
passages.vernacular: 「佢係塞嘅嗎?」獅子驚訝地問,睇住佢把稻草人撿起嚟讓佢站好,同時拍打佢恢復形狀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他是塞的嗎?」獅子驚訝地問,看著她把稻草人撿起來讓他站好,同時拍打他恢復形狀。

passages.original: “Of course he’s stuffed,” replied Dorothy, who was still angry.
passages.vernacular: 「當然佢係塞嘅,」桃樂絲回答,佢仍然生氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然他是塞的,」桃樂絲回答,她仍然生氣。

passages.original: “That’s why he went over so easily,” remarked the Lion. “It astonished me to see him whirl around so. Is the other one stuffed also?”
passages.vernacular: 「所以佢一碰就翻,」獅子講。「睇佢嗰樣旋轉,我好食驚。另一個都係塞嘅嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「所以他一碰就翻,」獅子說。「看他那樣旋轉,我很吃驚。另一個也是塞的嗎?」

passages.original: “No,” said Dorothy, “he’s made of tin.” And she helped the Woodman up again.
passages.vernacular: 「唔係,」桃樂絲講,「佢係錫做嘅。」佢又扶起樵夫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不是,」桃樂絲說,「他是錫做的。」她又扶起樵夫。

passages.original: “That’s why he nearly blunted my claws,” said the Lion. “When they scratched against the tin it made a cold shiver run down my back. What is that little animal you are so tender of?”
passages.vernacular: 「所以佢幾乎把我嘅爪子弄鈍喇,」獅子講。「爪子抓喺錫上時,使我背上一陣發冷。你咁疼愛嘅嗰隻小動物係乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「所以他幾乎把我的爪子弄鈍了,」獅子說。「爪子抓在錫上時,使我背上一陣發冷。你這麼疼愛的那隻小動物是什麼?」

passages.original: “He is my dog, Toto,” answered Dorothy.
passages.vernacular: 「佢係我嘅狗,托托,」桃樂絲回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他是我的狗,托托,」桃樂絲回答。

passages.original: “Is he made of tin, or stuffed?” asked the Lion.
passages.vernacular: 「佢係錫做嘅,定係塞嘅?」獅子問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他是錫做的,還是塞的?」獅子問。

passages.original: “Neither. He’s a—a—a meat dog,” said the girl.
passages.vernacular: 「都唔係。佢係一隻——一隻——一隻肉狗,」女孩講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「都不是。他是一隻——一隻——一隻肉狗,」女孩說。

passages.original: “Oh! He’s a curious animal and seems remarkably small, now that I look at him. No one would think of biting such a little thing, except a coward like me,” continued the Lion sadly.
passages.vernacular: 「哦!佢係一隻奇特嘅動物,而家我睇佢,似乎異常嘅小。冇人會想咬咁小嘅嘢,除咗像我咁樣嘅膽小鬼,」獅子悲傷地繼續講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦!他是一隻奇特的動物,現在我看他,似乎異常的小。沒有人會想咬這麼小的東西,除了像我這樣的膽小鬼,」獅子悲傷地繼續說。

passages.original: “What makes you a coward?” asked Dorothy, looking at the great beast in wonder, for he was as big as a small horse.
passages.vernacular: 「係乜嘢使你成為膽小鬼?」桃樂絲問,驚奇地睇住呢頭大野獸,因為佢像一匹小馬咁大。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是什麼使你成為膽小鬼?」桃樂絲問,驚奇地看著這頭大野獸,因為他像一匹小馬那麼大。

passages.original: “It’s a mystery,” replied the Lion. “I suppose I was born that way. All the other animals in the forest naturally expect me to be brave, for the Lion is everywhere thought to be the King of Beasts. I learned that if I roared very loudly every living thing was frightened and got out of my way. Whenever I’ve met a man I’ve been awfully scared; but I just roared at him, and he has always run away as fast as he could go. If the elephants and the tigers and the bears had ever tried to fight me, I should have run myself—I’m such a coward; but just as soon as they hear me roar they all try to get away from me, and of course I let them go.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係個謎,」獅子回答。「我想我生來就係咁樣。森林裡所有其他動物自然期望我勇敢,因為獅子到處被認為係百獸之王。我發現只要我大聲吼叫,每一個活嘅嘢都會害怕,為我讓路。每當我遇到人,我就好害怕;但我只係對佢吼,佢總是盡佢所能快地跑掉。如果大象、老虎同熊曾經試圖同我打,我自己會跑——我係咁樣嘅膽小鬼;但牠哋一聽到我吼叫,都試圖躲開我,當然我就讓牠哋走。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是個謎,」獅子回答。「我想我生來就是這樣。森林裡所有其他動物自然期望我勇敢,因為獅子到處被認為是百獸之王。我發現只要我大聲吼叫,每一個活的東西都會害怕,為我讓路。每當我遇到人,我就非常害怕;但我只是對他吼,他總是盡他所能快地跑掉。如果大象、老虎和熊曾經試圖同我打,我自己會跑——我是這樣的膽小鬼;但牠們一聽到我吼叫,都試圖躲開我,當然我就讓牠們走。」

passages.original: “But that isn’t right. The King of Beasts shouldn’t be a coward,” said the Scarecrow.
passages.vernacular: 「但呢不對。百獸之王不該係個膽小鬼,」稻草人講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但這不對。百獸之王不該是個膽小鬼,」稻草人說。

passages.original: “I know it,” returned the Lion, wiping a tear from his eye with the tip of his tail. “It is my great sorrow, and makes my life very unhappy. But whenever there is danger, my heart begins to beat fast.”
passages.vernacular: 「我知道,」獅子回答,用尾巴尖擦掉眼角嘅一滴淚。「呢個係我嘅大悲哀,使我嘅生活好不快樂。但每當有危險,我嘅心就開始跳得好快。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我知道,」獅子回答,用尾巴尖擦掉眼角的一滴淚。「這是我的大悲哀,使我的生活很不快樂。但每當有危險,我的心就開始跳得很快。」

passages.original: “Perhaps you have heart disease,” said the Tin Woodman.
passages.vernacular: 「或者你有心臟病,」鐵皮樵夫講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「也許你有心臟病,」鐵皮樵夫說。

passages.original: “It may be,” said the Lion.
passages.vernacular: 「可能,」獅子講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可能,」獅子說。

passages.original: “If you have,” continued the Tin Woodman, “you ought to be glad, for it proves you have a heart. For my part, I have no heart; so I cannot have heart disease.”
passages.vernacular: 「如果有,」鐵皮樵夫繼續講,「你應該高興,因為呢證明你有一顆心。至於我,我冇心;所以我唔可能有心臟病。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果有,」鐵皮樵夫繼續說,「你應該高興,因為這證明你有一顆心。至於我,我沒有心;所以我不可能有心臟病。」

passages.original: “Perhaps,” said the Lion thoughtfully, “if I had no heart I should not be a coward.”
passages.vernacular: 「或者,」獅子若有所思地講,「如果我冇心,我就唔會係膽小鬼。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「也許,」獅子若有所思地說,「如果我沒有心,我就不會是膽小鬼。」

passages.original: “Have you brains?” asked the Scarecrow.
passages.vernacular: 「你有腦子嗎?」稻草人問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你有腦子嗎?」稻草人問。

passages.original: “I suppose so. I’ve never looked to see,” replied the Lion.
passages.vernacular: 「我想有。我從冇睇過,」獅子回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想有。我從沒看過,」獅子回答。

passages.original: “I am going to the Great Oz to ask him to give me some,” remarked the Scarecrow, “for my head is stuffed with straw.”
passages.vernacular: 「我要去大奧茲嗰度請佢畀我啲,」稻草人講,「因為我嘅頭塞滿咗稻草。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我要去大奧茲那裡請他給我一些,」稻草人說,「因為我的頭塞滿了稻草。」

passages.original: “And I am going to ask him to give me a heart,” said the Woodman.
passages.vernacular: 「我要請佢畀我一顆心,」樵夫講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我要請他給我一顆心,」樵夫說。

passages.original: “And I am going to ask him to send Toto and me back to Kansas,” added Dorothy.
passages.vernacular: 「我要請佢送托托同我回堪薩斯,」桃樂絲補充講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我要請他送托托和我回堪薩斯,」桃樂絲補充說。

passages.original: “Do you think Oz could give me courage?” asked the Cowardly Lion.
passages.vernacular: 「你認為奧茲能畀我勇氣嗎?」膽小嘅獅子問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你認為奧茲能給我勇氣嗎?」膽小的獅子問。

passages.original: “Just as easily as he could give me brains,” said the Scarecrow.
passages.vernacular: 「就像佢能畀我腦子一樣容易,」稻草人講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「就像他能給我腦子一樣容易,」稻草人說。

passages.original: “Or give me a heart,” said the Tin Woodman.
passages.vernacular: 「或畀我一顆心,」鐵皮樵夫講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「或給我一顆心,」鐵皮樵夫說。

passages.original: “Or send me back to Kansas,” said Dorothy.
passages.vernacular: 「或送我回堪薩斯,」桃樂絲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「或送我回堪薩斯,」桃樂絲說。

passages.original: “Then, if you don’t mind, I’ll go with you,” said the Lion, “for my life is simply unbearable without a bit of courage.”
passages.vernacular: 「咁,如果你哋不介意,我同你哋去,」獅子講,「因為冇啲勇氣,我嘅生活簡直無法忍受。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼,如果你們不介意,我同你們去,」獅子說,「因為沒有一點勇氣,我的生活簡直無法忍受。」

passages.original: “You will be very welcome,” answered Dorothy, “for you will help to keep away the other wild beasts. It seems to me they must be more cowardly than you are if they allow you to scare them so easily.”
passages.vernacular: 「好歡迎,」桃樂絲回答,「因為你會幫助趕走其他野獸。喺我睇來,如果牠哋允許你咁容易嚇到牠哋,牠哋一定比你更膽小。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「非常歡迎,」桃樂絲回答,「因為你會幫助趕走其他野獸。在我看來,如果牠們允許你這麼容易嚇到牠們,牠們一定比你更膽小。」

passages.original: “They really are,” said the Lion, “but that doesn’t make me any braver, and as long as I know myself to be a coward I shall be unhappy.”
passages.vernacular: 「牠哋確實係,」獅子講,「但嗰唔能夠使我更勇敢,只要我知道自己係個膽小鬼,我就會不快樂。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「牠們確實是,」獅子說,「但那不能使我更勇敢,只要我知道自己是個膽小鬼,我就會不快樂。」

passages.original: So once more the little company set off upon the journey, the Lion walking with stately strides at Dorothy’s side. Toto did not approve of this new comrade at first, for he could not forget how nearly he had been crushed between the Lion’s great jaws. But after a time he became more at ease, and presently Toto and the Cowardly Lion had grown to be good friends.
passages.vernacular: 於是呢小隊伍又出發旅行,獅子以威嚴嘅步伐走喺桃樂絲身邊。托托起初不贊成呢個新夥伴,因為佢忘不咗自己差點被夾喺獅子大嘴之間壓碎。但過咗一段時間,佢放鬆喇,不久托托同膽小嘅獅子成咗好朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是這小隊伍又出發旅行,獅子以威嚴的步伐走在桃樂絲身邊。托托起初不贊成這個新夥伴,因為他忘不了自己差點被夾在獅子大嘴之間壓碎。但過了一段時間,他放鬆了,不久托托和膽小的獅子成了好朋友。

passages.original: During the rest of that day there was no other adventure to mar the peace of their journey. Once, indeed, the Tin Woodman stepped upon a beetle that was crawling along the road, and killed the poor little thing. This made the Tin Woodman very unhappy, for he was always careful not to hurt any living creature; and as he walked along he wept several tears of sorrow and regret. These tears ran slowly down his face and over the hinges of his jaw, and there they rusted. When Dorothy presently asked him a question the Tin Woodman could not open his mouth, for his jaws were tightly rusted together. He became greatly frightened at this and made many motions to Dorothy to relieve him, but she could not understand. The Lion was also puzzled to know what was wrong. But the Scarecrow seized the oil-can from Dorothy’s basket and oiled the Woodman’s jaws, so that after a few moments he could talk as well as before.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天剩下嘅時間,冇其他冒險破壞佢哋旅途嘅平靜。確實,有一次,鐵皮樵夫踩到一隻沿路爬行嘅甲蟲,把呢可憐嘅小嘢殺死喇。呢使鐵皮樵夫好不快樂,因為佢一向小心不傷害任何生物;佢邊走邊流咗幾滴悲傷同悔恨嘅眼淚。呢啲眼淚慢慢順住佢嘅臉同佢下顎嘅鉸鏈流下,喺嗰度生咗鏽。桃樂絲不久問佢一個問題時,鐵皮樵夫唔能夠張嘴,因為佢嘅下顎緊緊鏽喺一起。佢為此好害怕,向桃樂絲做咗許多動作請佢救佢,但佢不懂。獅子都納悶出咗乜嘢事。但稻草人從桃樂絲嘅籃子裡攞過油壺,畀樵夫嘅下顎上油,過咗一會兒,佢又能像以前一樣講話喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天剩下的時間,沒有其他冒險破壞他們旅途的平靜。確實,有一次,鐵皮樵夫踩到一隻沿路爬行的甲蟲,把這可憐的小東西殺死了。這使鐵皮樵夫非常不快樂,因為他一向小心不傷害任何生物;他邊走邊流了幾滴悲傷和悔恨的眼淚。這些眼淚慢慢順著他的臉和他下顎的鉸鏈流下,在那裡生了鏽。桃樂絲不久問他一個問題時,鐵皮樵夫不能張嘴,因為他的下顎緊緊鏽在一起。他為此非常害怕,向桃樂絲做了許多動作請她救他,但她不懂。獅子也納悶出了什麼事。但稻草人從桃樂絲的籃子裡拿過油壺,給樵夫的下顎上油,過了一會兒,他又能像以前一樣說話了。

passages.original: “This will serve me a lesson,” said he, “to look where I step. For if I should kill another bug or beetle I should surely cry again, and crying rusts my jaws so that I cannot speak.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢會畀我一個教訓,」佢講,「要睇住我踩喺邊度。因為如果我再殺死一隻蟲或甲蟲,我肯定又會哭,而哭會使我嘅下顎生鏽,使我講不咗話。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這會給我一個教訓,」他說,「要看著我踩在哪裡。因為如果我再殺死一隻蟲或甲蟲,我肯定又會哭,而哭會使我的下顎生鏽,使我說不了話。」

passages.original: Thereafter he walked very carefully, with his eyes on the road, and when he saw a tiny ant toiling by he would step over it, so as not to harm it. The Tin Woodman knew very well he had no heart, and therefore he took great care never to be cruel or unkind to anything.
passages.vernacular: 此後佢走得好小心,眼睛睇住路,睇到一隻小螞蟻辛苦經過,佢就跨過去,以免傷害佢。鐵皮樵夫好清楚自己冇心,因此佢好小心不對任何嘢殘忍或不友善。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 此後他走得非常小心,眼睛看著路,看到一隻小螞蟻辛苦經過,他就跨過去,以免傷害它。鐵皮樵夫很清楚自己沒有心,因此他非常小心不對任何東西殘忍或不友善。

passages.original: “You people with hearts,” he said, “have something to guide you, and need never do wrong; but I have no heart, and so I must be very careful. When Oz gives me a heart of course I needn’t mind so much.”
passages.vernacular: 「你哋有心嘅人,」佢講,「有嘢指導你哋,永遠唔使做錯事;但我冇心,所以我必須好小心。當奧茲畀我一顆心,當然我就唔使咁在意喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你們有心的人,」他說,「有東西指導你們,永遠不必做錯事;但我沒有心,所以我必須非常小心。當奧茲給我一顆心,當然我就不必這麼在意了。」

chapters.title: Chapter VII: The Journey to the Great Oz 第七章:前往大奧茲之旅

passages.original: They were obliged to camp out that night under a large tree in the forest, for there were no houses near. The tree made a good, thick covering to protect them from the dew, and the Tin Woodman chopped a great pile of wood with his axe and Dorothy built a splendid fire that warmed her and made her feel less lonely. She and Toto ate the last of their bread, and now she did not know what they would do for breakfast.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天晚上佢哋唔得不喺森林裡一棵大樹下露營,因為附近冇房子。嗰棵樹提供咗又好又厚嘅遮蓋,保護佢哋不受露水侵襲,鐵皮樵夫用斧頭砍咗一大堆木柴,桃樂絲生咗一堆好棒嘅火,使佢暖同,都讓佢覺得不咁孤單。佢同托托食完咗最後嘅麵包,而家佢唔知道早餐食乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天晚上他們不得不在森林裡一棵大樹下露營,因為附近沒有房子。那棵樹提供了又好又厚的遮蓋,保護他們不受露水侵襲,鐵皮樵夫用斧頭砍了一大堆木柴,桃樂絲生了一堆很棒的火,使她暖和,也讓她覺得不那麼孤單。她和托托吃完了最後的麵包,現在她不知道早餐吃什麼。

passages.original: “If you wish,” said the Lion, “I will go into the forest and kill a deer for you. You can roast it by the fire, since your tastes are so peculiar that you prefer cooked food, and then you will have a very good breakfast.”
passages.vernacular: 「如果你願意,」獅子講,「我去森林裡替你殺一隻鹿。你可以喺火上烤,因為你嘅口味咁特別,鍾意熟食,然後你就有一頓好好嘅早餐喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果你願意,」獅子說,「我去森林裡替你殺一隻鹿。你可以在火上烤,因為你的口味那麼特別,喜歡熟食,然後你就有一頓很好的早餐了。」

passages.original: “Don’t! Please don’t,” begged the Tin Woodman. “I should certainly weep if you killed a poor deer, and then my jaws would rust again.”
passages.vernacular: 「別!請別,」鐵皮樵夫懇求。「如果你殺死一隻可憐嘅鹿,我肯定會哭,然後我嘅下顎又要生鏽喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「別!請別,」鐵皮樵夫懇求。「如果你殺死一隻可憐的鹿,我肯定會哭,然後我的下顎又要生鏽了。」

passages.original: But the Lion went away into the forest and found his own supper, and no one ever knew what it was, for he didn’t mention it. And the Scarecrow found a tree full of nuts and filled Dorothy’s basket with them, so that she would not be hungry for a long time. She thought this was very kind and thoughtful of the Scarecrow, but she laughed heartily at the awkward way in which the poor creature picked up the nuts. His padded hands were so clumsy and the nuts were so small that he dropped almost as many as he put in the basket. But the Scarecrow did not mind how long it took him to fill the basket, for it enabled him to keep away from the fire, as he feared a spark might get into his straw and burn him up. So he kept a good distance away from the flames, and only came near to cover Dorothy with dry leaves when she lay down to sleep. These kept her very snug and warm, and she slept soundly until morning.
passages.vernacular: 但獅子定係走進森林,找到咗自己嘅晚飯,冇人知道係乜嘢,因為佢冇提。稻草人找到一棵結滿堅果嘅樹,用堅果把桃樂絲嘅籃子裝滿,咁樣佢好長時間都唔會餓。佢認為稻草人咁樣做好好心、體貼,但佢睇到嗰可憐嘅傢伙撿堅果嘅笨拙樣子,忍不住開懷大笑。佢墊住嘢嘅手咁笨拙,堅果咁小,佢掉嘅幾乎同放進籃子嘅一樣多。但稻草人不在乎裝滿籃子要花多久,因為呢使佢能遠離火,佢怕啲火星進到佢嘅稻草裡把佢燒掉。所以佢離火焰好遠,只喺桃樂絲躺下瞓覺時才靠近,用乾葉子蓋住佢。呢啲使佢好舒適溫暖,佢瞓得好沉,直到早晨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但獅子還是走進森林,找到了自己的晚飯,沒有人知道是什麼,因為他沒有提。稻草人找到一棵結滿堅果的樹,用堅果把桃樂絲的籃子裝滿,這樣她好長時間都不會餓。她認為稻草人這樣做非常好心、體貼,但她看到那可憐的傢伙撿堅果的笨拙樣子,忍不住開懷大笑。他墊著東西的手那麼笨拙,堅果那麼小,他掉的幾乎和放進籃子的一樣多。但稻草人不在乎裝滿籃子要花多久,因為這使他能遠離火,他怕一點火星進到他的稻草裡把他燒掉。所以他離火焰很遠,只在桃樂絲躺下睡覺時才靠近,用乾葉子蓋住她。這些使她非常舒適溫暖,她睡得很沉,直到早晨。

passages.original: When it was daylight, the girl bathed her face in a little rippling brook, and soon after they all started toward the Emerald City.
passages.vernacular: 天亮時,女孩喺一條小小嘅潺潺小溪裡洗咗臉,不久佢哋都朝翡翠城出發喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天亮時,女孩在一條小小的潺潺小溪裡洗了臉,不久他們都朝翡翠城出發了。

passages.original: This was to be an eventful day for the travelers. They had hardly been walking an hour when they saw before them a great ditch that crossed the road and divided the forest as far as they could see on either side. It was a very wide ditch, and when they crept up to the edge and looked into it they could see it was also very deep, and there were many big, jagged rocks at the bottom. The sides were so steep that none of them could climb down, and for a moment it seemed that their journey must end.
passages.vernacular: 呢一天對旅行者來講將係多事嘅一天。佢哋走咗幾乎唔到一小時,就睇到前面有一條大溝橫過路,把森林分成兩半,兩邊都睇唔到盡頭。嗰個係一條好寬嘅溝,佢哋爬到邊緣往裡睇時,睇到佢都好深,底部有許多參差不齊嘅大石頭。兩側咁陡,佢哋冇人能爬下去,有一刻似乎佢哋嘅旅程必須結束喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這一天對旅行者來說將是多事的一天。他們走了幾乎不到一小時,就看到前面有一條大溝橫過路,把森林分成兩半,兩邊都看不到盡頭。那是一條很寬的溝,他們爬到邊緣往裡看時,看到它也很深,底部有許多參差不齊的大石頭。兩側那麼陡,他們沒有人能爬下去,有一刻似乎他們的旅程必須結束了。

passages.original: “What shall we do?” asked Dorothy despairingly.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋點算?」桃樂絲絕望地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們怎麼辦?」桃樂絲絕望地問。

passages.original: “I haven’t the faintest idea,” said the Tin Woodman, and the Lion shook his shaggy mane and looked thoughtful.
passages.vernacular: 「我完全冇概念,」鐵皮樵夫講,獅子甩咗甩佢蓬鬆嘅鬃毛,若有所思。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我完全沒有概念,」鐵皮樵夫說,獅子甩了甩他蓬鬆的鬃毛,若有所思。

passages.original: But the Scarecrow said, “We cannot fly, that is certain. Neither can we climb down into this great ditch. Therefore, if we cannot jump over it, we must stop where we are.”
passages.vernacular: 但稻草人講:「我哋唔能夠飛,呢個係肯定嘅。我哋都唔能夠爬下呢條大溝。因此,如果我哋唔能夠跳過去,我哋就只能停喺呢度。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但稻草人說:「我們不能飛,這是肯定的。我們也不能爬下這條大溝。因此,如果我們不能跳過去,我們就只能停在這裡。」

passages.original: “I think I could jump over it,” said the Cowardly Lion, after measuring the distance carefully in his mind.
passages.vernacular: 「我想我能跳過去,」膽小嘅獅子喺腦中仔細測量咗距離後講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想我能跳過去,」膽小的獅子在腦中仔細測量了距離後說。

passages.original: “Then we are all right,” answered the Scarecrow, “for you can carry us all over on your back, one at a time.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰我哋就冇問題喇,」稻草人回答,「因為你可以背我哋一個一個地過去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那我們就沒問題了,」稻草人回答,「因為你可以背我們一個一個地過去。」

passages.original: “Well, I’ll try it,” said the Lion. “Who will go first?”
passages.vernacular: 「好,我試試,」獅子講。「邊個先去?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好,我試試,」獅子說。「誰先去?」

passages.original: “I will,” declared the Scarecrow, “for, if you found that you could not jump over the gulf, Dorothy would be killed, or the Tin Woodman badly dented on the rocks below. But if I am on your back it will not matter so much, for the fall would not hurt me at all.”
passages.vernacular: 「我,」稻草人宣布,「因為,如果你發現你跳不過呢個深淵,桃樂絲會被殺死,或鐵皮樵夫會喺下面嘅石頭上撞得好凹。但如果我喺你背上就冇咁要緊,因為摔下去完全唔會傷到我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我,」稻草人宣布,「因為,如果你發現你跳不過這個深淵,桃樂絲會被殺死,或鐵皮樵夫會在下面的石頭上撞得很凹。但如果我在你背上就沒有那麼要緊,因為摔下去完全不會傷到我。」

passages.original: “I am terribly afraid of falling, myself,” said the Cowardly Lion, “but I suppose there is nothing to do but try it. So get on my back and we will make the attempt.”
passages.vernacular: 「我自己好怕摔下去,」膽小嘅獅子講,「但我想只有試一試喇。所以爬到我背上,我哋嚟試試。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我自己非常怕摔下去,」膽小的獅子說,「但我想只有試一試了。所以爬到我背上,我們來試試。」

passages.original: The Scarecrow sat upon the Lion’s back, and the big beast walked to the edge of the gulf and crouched down.
passages.vernacular: 稻草人坐喺獅子背上,大野獸走到深淵邊緣,蹲下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 稻草人坐在獅子背上,大野獸走到深淵邊緣,蹲下。

passages.original: “Why don’t you run and jump?” asked the Scarecrow.
passages.vernacular: 「你點解不跑起嚟跳?」稻草人問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你為什麼不跑起來跳?」稻草人問。

passages.original: “Because that isn’t the way we Lions do these things,” he replied. Then giving a great spring, he shot through the air and landed safely on the other side. They were all greatly pleased to see how easily he did it, and after the Scarecrow had got down from his back the Lion sprang across the ditch again.
passages.vernacular: 「因為我哋獅子唔係咁樣做呢種事嘅,」佢回答。然後猛地一躍,佢喺空中射過去,安全落喺另一邊。佢哋都好高興睇到佢做得咁容易,稻草人從佢背上下嚟後,獅子又跳回溝呢邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「因為我們獅子不是這樣做這種事的,」他回答。然後猛地一躍,他在空中射過去,安全落在另一邊。他們都非常高興看到他做得那麼容易,稻草人從他背上下來後,獅子又跳回溝這邊。

passages.original: Dorothy thought she would go next; so she took Toto in her arms and climbed on the Lion’s back, holding tightly to his mane with one hand. The next moment it seemed as if she were flying through the air; and then, before she had time to think about it, she was safe on the other side. The Lion went back a third time and got the Tin Woodman, and then they all sat down for a few moments to give the beast a chance to rest, for his great leaps had made his breath short, and he panted like a big dog that has been running too long.
passages.vernacular: 桃樂絲想佢該下一個去;於是佢抱住托托,爬上獅子嘅背,一隻手緊緊抓住佢嘅鬃毛。下一刻似乎佢喺空中飛;然後,喺佢嚟得及想之前,佢已安全地喺另一邊。獅子第三次回去接鐵皮樵夫,然後佢哋都坐下幾分鐘,讓野獸休息,因為佢嘅大跳躍使佢氣短,佢像一條跑太久嘅大狗一樣喘氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 桃樂絲想她該下一個去;於是她抱著托托,爬上獅子的背,一隻手緊緊抓著他的鬃毛。下一刻似乎她在空中飛;然後,在她來得及想之前,她已安全地在另一邊。獅子第三次回去接鐵皮樵夫,然後他們都坐下幾分鐘,讓野獸休息,因為他的大跳躍使他氣短,他像一條跑太久的大狗一樣喘氣。

passages.original: They found the forest very thick on this side, and it looked dark and gloomy. After the Lion had rested they started along the road of yellow brick, silently wondering, each in his own mind, if ever they would come to the end of the woods and reach the bright sunshine again. To add to their discomfort, they soon heard strange noises in the depths of the forest, and the Lion whispered to them that it was in this part of the country that the Kalidahs lived.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋發現呢一邊嘅森林好密,睇起嚟黑暗陰沉。獅子休息過後,佢哋沿住黃磚路出發,默默地各自在心裡想,佢哋能唔能夠走到樹林嘅盡頭,再次回到明亮嘅陽光下。更添不適嘅係,佢哋不久就聽到森林深處有奇怪嘅聲音,獅子低聲告訴佢哋,卡里達就住喺呢一帶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們發現這一邊的森林很密,看起來黑暗陰沉。獅子休息過後,他們沿著黃磚路出發,默默地各自在心裡想,他們能不能走到樹林的盡頭,再次回到明亮的陽光下。更添不適的是,他們不久就聽到森林深處有奇怪的聲音,獅子低聲告訴他們,卡里達就住在這一帶。

passages.original: “What are the Kalidahs?” asked the girl.
passages.vernacular: 「卡里達係乜嘢?」女孩問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「卡里達是什麼?」女孩問。

passages.original: “They are monstrous beasts with bodies like bears and heads like tigers,” replied the Lion, “and with claws so long and sharp that they could tear me in two as easily as I could kill Toto. I’m terribly afraid of the Kalidahs.”
passages.vernacular: 「牠哋係怪獸,身體像熊,頭像老虎,」獅子回答,「爪子咁長咁鋒利,能輕易把我撕成兩半,就像我能殺死托托一樣容易。我好怕卡里達。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「牠們是怪獸,身體像熊,頭像老虎,」獅子回答,「爪子那麼長那麼鋒利,能輕易把我撕成兩半,就像我能殺死托托一樣容易。我非常怕卡里達。」

passages.original: “I’m not surprised that you are,” returned Dorothy. “They must be dreadful beasts.”
passages.vernacular: 「你怕我不奇怪,」桃樂絲回答。「牠哋一定係可怕嘅野獸。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你怕我不奇怪,」桃樂絲回答。「牠們一定是可怕的野獸。」

passages.original: The Lion was about to reply when suddenly they came to another gulf across the road. But this one was so broad and deep that the Lion knew at once he could not leap across it.
passages.vernacular: 獅子正要回答,突然佢哋嚟到路上嘅另一條深溝。但呢條咁寬咁深,獅子即刻知道佢跳不過去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 獅子正要回答,突然他們來到路上的另一條深溝。但這條那麼寬那麼深,獅子立刻知道他跳不過去。

passages.original: So they sat down to consider what they should do, and after serious thought the Scarecrow said:
passages.vernacular: 於是佢哋坐下嚟考慮該點算,經過認真思考,稻草人講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是他們坐下來考慮該怎麼辦,經過認真思考,稻草人說:

passages.original: “Here is a great tree, standing close to the ditch. If the Tin Woodman can chop it down, so that it will fall to the other side, we can walk across it easily.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢度有一棵大樹,靠近溝站住。如果鐵皮樵夫能把佢砍倒,使佢倒向另一邊,我哋就可以輕易地走過去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這裡有一棵大樹,靠近溝站著。如果鐵皮樵夫能把它砍倒,使它倒向另一邊,我們就可以輕易地走過去。」

passages.original: “That is a first-rate idea,” said the Lion. “One would almost suspect you had brains in your head, instead of straw.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係個第一流嘅主意,」獅子講。「人哋幾乎要懷疑你頭腦裡係腦子而唔係稻草。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是個第一流的主意,」獅子說。「人們幾乎要懷疑你頭腦裡是腦子而不是稻草。」

passages.original: The Woodman set to work at once, and so sharp was his axe that the tree was soon chopped nearly through. Then the Lion put his strong front legs against the tree and pushed with all his might, and slowly the big tree tipped and fell with a crash across the ditch, with its top branches on the other side.
passages.vernacular: 樵夫即刻動工,佢嘅斧頭咁鋒利,樹好快就被砍咗將近一半。然後獅子把佢強壯嘅前腿頂喺樹上,用盡全力推,慢慢地大樹傾斜,轟然倒下,橫跨溝壑,樹頂嘅樹枝喺另一邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 樵夫立刻動工,他的斧頭那麼鋒利,樹很快就被砍了將近一半。然後獅子把他強壯的前腿頂在樹上,用盡全力推,慢慢地大樹傾斜,轟然倒下,橫跨溝壑,樹頂的樹枝在另一邊。

passages.original: They had just started to cross this queer bridge when a sharp growl made them all look up, and to their horror they saw running toward them two great beasts with bodies like bears and heads like tigers.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋剛開始過呢座奇怪嘅橋,一聲尖銳嘅吼叫使佢哋都抬頭,令佢哋驚恐嘅係,佢哋睇到兩隻大野獸朝佢哋跑嚟,身體像熊,頭像老虎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們剛開始過這座奇怪的橋,一聲尖銳的吼叫使他們都抬頭,令他們驚恐的是,他們看到兩隻大野獸朝他們跑來,身體像熊,頭像老虎。

passages.original: “They are the Kalidahs!” said the Cowardly Lion, beginning to tremble.
passages.vernacular: 「牠哋係卡里達!」膽小嘅獅子講,開始發抖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「牠們是卡里達!」膽小的獅子說,開始發抖。

passages.original: “Quick!” cried the Scarecrow. “Let us cross over.”
passages.vernacular: 「快!」稻草人喊道。「我哋過去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「快!」稻草人喊道。「我們過去。」

passages.original: So Dorothy went first, holding Toto in her arms, the Tin Woodman followed, and the Scarecrow came next. The Lion, although he was certainly afraid, turned to face the Kalidahs, and then he gave so loud and terrible a roar that Dorothy screamed and the Scarecrow fell over backward, while even the fierce beasts stopped short and looked at him in surprise.
passages.vernacular: 於是桃樂絲先走,抱住托托,鐵皮樵夫跟住,稻草人接住。獅子雖然肯定害怕,卻轉身面對卡里達,然後發出咁響亮可怕嘅一聲吼,桃樂絲尖叫,稻草人向後倒下,連凶猛嘅野獸都猛然停住,驚訝地睇住佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是桃樂絲先走,抱著托托,鐵皮樵夫跟著,稻草人接著。獅子雖然肯定害怕,卻轉身面對卡里達,然後發出那麼響亮可怕的一聲吼,桃樂絲尖叫,稻草人向後倒下,連凶猛的野獸也猛然停住,驚訝地看著他。

passages.original: But, seeing they were bigger than the Lion, and remembering that there were two of them and only one of him, the Kalidahs again rushed forward, and the Lion crossed over the tree and turned to see what they would do next. Without stopping an instant the fierce beasts also began to cross the tree. And the Lion said to Dorothy:
passages.vernacular: 但睇到牠哋比獅子大,想起牠哋有兩隻而佢只有一隻,卡里達又衝上前,獅子過咗樹,轉身睇牠哋接下嚟做乜嘢。凶猛嘅野獸毫不停頓,都開始過樹。獅子對桃樂絲講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但看到牠們比獅子大,想起牠們有兩隻而他只有一隻,卡里達又衝上前,獅子過了樹,轉身看牠們接下來做什麼。凶猛的野獸毫不停頓,也開始過樹。獅子對桃樂絲說:

passages.original: “We are lost, for they will surely tear us to pieces with their sharp claws. But stand close behind me, and I will fight them as long as I am alive.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋完喇,因為牠哋肯定會用鋒利嘅爪子把我哋撕成碎片。但緊貼喺我後面站住,只要我活住,我就跟牠哋戰鬥。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們完了,因為牠們肯定會用鋒利的爪子把我們撕成碎片。但緊貼在我後面站著,只要我活著,我就跟牠們戰鬥。」

passages.original: “Wait a minute!” called the Scarecrow. He had been thinking what was best to be done, and now he asked the Woodman to chop away the end of the tree that rested on their side of the ditch. The Tin Woodman began to use his axe at once, and, just as the two Kalidahs were nearly across, the tree fell with a crash into the gulf, carrying the ugly, snarling brutes with it, and both were dashed to pieces on the sharp rocks at the bottom.
passages.vernacular: 「等一下!」稻草人喊道。佢一直喺想點做最好,而家佢請樵夫砍掉搭喺佢哋呢一邊溝上嘅樹端。鐵皮樵夫即刻用斧頭,就喺兩隻卡里達幾乎過完時,樹轟然倒進深淵,連同醜陋、咆哮嘅野獸一起,牠哋兩隻都喺底部鋒利嘅石頭上摔得粉碎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「等一下!」稻草人喊道。他一直在想怎麼做最好,現在他請樵夫砍掉搭在他們這一邊溝上的樹端。鐵皮樵夫立刻用斧頭,就在兩隻卡里達幾乎過完時,樹轟然倒進深淵,連同醜陋、咆哮的野獸一起,牠們兩隻都在底部鋒利的石頭上摔得粉碎。

passages.original: “Well,” said the Cowardly Lion, drawing a long breath of relief, “I see we are going to live a little while longer, and I am glad of it, for it must be a very uncomfortable thing not to be alive. Those creatures frightened me so badly that my heart is beating yet.”
passages.vernacular: 「好喇,」膽小嘅獅子講,鬆咗一口長氣,「我睇我哋仲能多活一會兒,我為此高興,因為不活住一定係好不舒服嘅事。嗰啲生物把我嚇得咁厲害,我嘅心仲喺跳。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了,」膽小的獅子說,鬆了一口長氣,「我看我們還能多活一會兒,我為此高興,因為不活著一定是很不舒服的事。那些生物把我嚇得那麼厲害,我的心還在跳。」

passages.original: “Ah,” said the Tin Woodman sadly, “I wish I had a heart to beat.”
passages.vernacular: 「啊,」鐵皮樵夫悲傷地講,「我希望我有顆心可以跳。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「啊,」鐵皮樵夫悲傷地說,「我希望我有顆心可以跳。」

passages.original: This adventure made the travelers more anxious than ever to get out of the forest, and they walked so fast that Dorothy became tired, and had to ride on the Lion’s back. To their great joy the trees became thinner the farther they advanced, and in the afternoon they suddenly came upon a broad river, flowing swiftly just before them. On the other side of the water they could see the road of yellow brick running through a beautiful country, with green meadows dotted with bright flowers and all the road bordered with trees hanging full of delicious fruits. They were greatly pleased to see this delightful country before them.
passages.vernacular: 呢次冒險使旅行者哋比以往更急於走出森林,佢哋走得咁快,桃樂絲累喇,唔得不騎喺獅子嘅背上。令佢哋好高興嘅係,佢哋越往前走,樹越稀,下午,佢哋突然嚟到一條寬闊嘅河,喺佢哋面前湍急地流住。喺水嘅另一邊,佢哋可以睇到黃磚路穿過一個美麗嘅國度,綠色嘅草地點綴住鮮豔嘅花朵,整條路兩旁嘅樹上掛滿咗美味嘅水果。睇到面前呢個令人愉快嘅國度,佢哋好高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這次冒險使旅行者們比以往更急於走出森林,他們走得那麼快,桃樂絲累了,不得不騎在獅子的背上。令他們非常高興的是,他們越往前走,樹越稀,下午,他們突然來到一條寬闊的河,在他們面前湍急地流著。在水的另一邊,他們可以看到黃磚路穿過一個美麗的國度,綠色的草地點綴著鮮豔的花朵,整條路兩旁的樹上掛滿了美味的水果。看到面前這個令人愉快的國度,他們非常高興。

passages.original: “How shall we cross the river?” asked Dorothy.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋點樣過河?」桃樂絲問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們怎樣過河?」桃樂絲問。

passages.original: “That is easily done,” replied the Scarecrow. “The Tin Woodman must build us a raft, so we can float to the other side.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢個好容易,」稻草人回答。「鐵皮樵夫必須為我哋造一個木筏,咁樣我哋就可以漂到另一邊。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這很容易,」稻草人回答。「鐵皮樵夫必須為我們造一個木筏,這樣我們就可以漂到另一邊。」

passages.original: So the Woodman took his axe and began to chop down small trees to make a raft, and while he was busy at this the Scarecrow found on the riverbank a tree full of fine fruit. This pleased Dorothy, who had eaten nothing but nuts all day, and she made a hearty meal of the ripe fruit.
passages.vernacular: 於是樵夫攞起斧頭,開始砍小樹做木筏,佢忙住做呢個時,稻草人喺河岸上發現一棵結滿好水果嘅樹。呢使桃樂絲高興,佢整天只食堅果,佢美美地食咗一頓熟水果。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是樵夫拿起斧頭,開始砍小樹做木筏,他忙著做這個時,稻草人在河岸上發現一棵結滿好水果的樹。這使桃樂絲高興,她整天只吃堅果,她美美地吃了一頓熟水果。

passages.original: But it takes time to make a raft, even when one is as industrious and untiring as the Tin Woodman, and when night came the work was not done. So they found a cozy place under the trees where they slept well until the morning; and Dorothy dreamed of the Emerald City, and of the good Wizard Oz, who would soon send her back to her own home again.
passages.vernacular: 但做木筏需要時間,即使係像鐵皮樵夫咁樣勤奮唔知疲倦嘅人,夜幕降臨時工作仲冇完成。於是佢哋喺樹下找到一個舒適嘅地方,瞓得好好,直到早晨;桃樂絲夢見咗翡翠城,同好巫師奧茲,佢好快就會送佢回到自己嘅家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但做木筏需要時間,即使是像鐵皮樵夫這樣勤奮不知疲倦的人,夜幕降臨時工作還沒完成。於是他們在樹下找到一個舒適的地方,睡得很好,直到早晨;桃樂絲夢見了翡翠城,和好巫師奧茲,他很快就會送她回到自己的家。

chapters.title: Chapter VIII: The Deadly Poppy Field 第八章:致命的罌粟花田

passages.original: Our little party of travelers awakened the next morning refreshed and full of hope, and Dorothy breakfasted like a princess off peaches and plums from the trees beside the river. Behind them was the dark forest they had passed safely through, although they had suffered many discouragements; but before them was a lovely, sunny country that seemed to beckon them on to the Emerald City.
passages.vernacular: 我哋嘅小旅行隊伍第二天早晨醒嚟,精神煥發,充滿希望,桃樂絲像公主一樣,食河邊樹上嘅桃子同李子當早餐。佢哋後面係佢哋安全穿過嘅黑暗森林,雖然佢哋受過許多挫折;但佢哋前面係一個可愛、陽光明媚嘅國度,似乎喺召喚佢哋前往翡翠城。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們的小旅行隊伍第二天早晨醒來,精神煥發,充滿希望,桃樂絲像公主一樣,吃河邊樹上的桃子和李子當早餐。他們後面是他們安全穿過的黑暗森林,雖然他們受過許多挫折;但他們前面是一個可愛、陽光明媚的國度,似乎在召喚他們前往翡翠城。

passages.original: To be sure, the broad river now cut them off from this beautiful land. But the raft was nearly done, and after the Tin Woodman had cut a few more logs and fastened them together with wooden pins, they were ready to start. Dorothy sat down in the middle of the raft and held Toto in her arms. When the Cowardly Lion stepped upon the raft it tipped badly, for he was big and heavy; but the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman stood upon the other end to steady it, and they had long poles in their hands to push the raft through the water.
passages.vernacular: 確實,寬闊嘅河而家把佢哋同呢片美麗嘅土地隔開。但木筏幾乎完成喇,鐵皮樵夫又砍咗幾根原木,用木釘把佢哋釘喺一起後,佢哋就準備好出發。桃樂絲坐喺木筏中間,抱住托托。膽小嘅獅子踏上木筏時,佢嚴重傾斜,因為佢又大又重;但稻草人同鐵皮樵夫站喺另一端穩住佢,佢哋手裡有長竿子嚟撐木筏過水。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 確實,寬闊的河現在把他們與這片美麗的土地隔開。但木筏幾乎完成了,鐵皮樵夫又砍了幾根原木,用木釘把它們釘在一起後,他們就準備好出發。桃樂絲坐在木筏中間,抱著托托。膽小的獅子踏上木筏時,它嚴重傾斜,因為他又大又重;但稻草人和鐵皮樵夫站在另一端穩住它,他們手裡有長竿子來撐木筏過水。

passages.original: They got along quite well at first, but when they reached the middle of the river the swift current swept the raft downstream, farther and farther away from the road of yellow brick. And the water grew so deep that the long poles would not touch the bottom.
passages.vernacular: 起初佢哋前進得相當好,但到河中間時,湍急嘅水流把木筏沖向下游,離黃磚路越嚟越遠。水變得咁深,長竿子碰唔到底。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 起初他們前進得相當好,但到河中間時,湍急的水流把木筏沖向下游,離黃磚路越來越遠。水變得那麼深,長竿子碰不到底。

passages.original: “This is bad,” said the Tin Woodman, “for if we cannot get to the land we shall be carried into the country of the Wicked Witch of the West, and she will enchant us and make us her slaves.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢不好,」鐵皮樵夫講,「因為如果我哋唔能夠上岸,我哋就會被沖進西方惡女巫嘅國家,佢會對我哋施魔法,使我哋成為佢嘅奴隸。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這不好,」鐵皮樵夫說,「因為如果我們不能上岸,我們就會被沖進西方惡女巫的國家,她會對我們施魔法,使我們成為她的奴隸。」

passages.original: “And then I should get no brains,” said the Scarecrow.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰我就得唔到腦子喇,」稻草人講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那我就得不到腦子了,」稻草人說。

passages.original: “And I should get no courage,” said the Cowardly Lion.
passages.vernacular: 「我就得唔到勇氣喇,」膽小嘅獅子講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我就得不到勇氣了,」膽小的獅子說。

passages.original: “And I should get no heart,” said the Tin Woodman.
passages.vernacular: 「我就得唔到心喇,」鐵皮樵夫講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我就得不到心了,」鐵皮樵夫說。

passages.original: “And I should never get back to Kansas,” said Dorothy.
passages.vernacular: 「我就永遠回不咗堪薩斯喇,」桃樂絲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我就永遠回不了堪薩斯了,」桃樂絲說。

passages.original: “We must certainly get to the Emerald City if we can,” the Scarecrow continued, and he pushed so hard on his long pole that it stuck fast in the mud at the bottom of the river. Then, before he could pull it out again—or let go—the raft was swept away, and the poor Scarecrow was left clinging to the pole in the middle of the river.
passages.vernacular: 「如果能,我哋一定要到翡翠城,」稻草人繼續講,佢用咁大嘅力氣撐佢嘅長竿子,以致佢牢牢卡喺河底嘅泥裡。然後,佢嚟不及把佢拔出嚟——或鬆手——木筏已被沖走,可憐嘅稻草人被留喺河中間,抱住竿子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果能,我們一定要到翡翠城,」稻草人繼續說,他用那麼大的力氣撐他的長竿子,以致它牢牢卡在河底的泥裡。然後,他來不及把它拔出來——或鬆手——木筏已被沖走,可憐的稻草人被留在河中間,抱著竿子。

passages.original: “Good-bye!” he called after them, and they were very sorry to leave him. Indeed, the Tin Woodman began to cry, but fortunately remembered that he might rust, and so dried his tears on Dorothy’s apron.
passages.vernacular: 「再見!」佢喺佢哋後面喊,佢哋好難過要離開佢。確實,鐵皮樵夫開始哭,但幸運地記起佢可能生鏽,於是喺桃樂絲嘅圍裙上擦乾眼淚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「再見!」他在他們後面喊,他們非常難過要離開他。確實,鐵皮樵夫開始哭,但幸運地記起他可能生鏽,於是在桃樂絲的圍裙上擦乾眼淚。

passages.original: Of course this was a bad thing for the Scarecrow.
passages.vernacular: 當然呢對稻草人係件壞事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然這對稻草人是件壞事。

passages.original: “I am now worse off than when I first met Dorothy,” he thought. “Then, I was stuck on a pole in a cornfield, where I could make-believe scare the crows, at any rate. But surely there is no use for a Scarecrow stuck on a pole in the middle of a river. I am afraid I shall never have any brains, after all!”
passages.vernacular: 「我而家比第一次遇見桃樂絲時更糟,」佢想。「嗰時,我被插喺玉米田嘅桿子上,至少我可以假裝嚇烏鴉。但係,一個插喺河中間桿子上嘅稻草人肯定冇用處。恐怕我畢竟永遠得唔到腦子喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我現在比第一次遇見桃樂絲時更糟,」他想。「那時,我被插在玉米田的桿子上,至少我可以假裝嚇烏鴉。但是,一個插在河中間桿子上的稻草人肯定沒有用處。恐怕我畢竟永遠得不到腦子了!」

passages.original: Down the stream the raft floated, and the poor Scarecrow was left far behind. Then the Lion said:
passages.vernacular: 木筏順流而下,可憐嘅稻草人被遠遠留喺後面。然後獅子講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 木筏順流而下,可憐的稻草人被遠遠留在後面。然後獅子說:

passages.original: “Something must be done to save us. I think I can swim to the shore and pull the raft after me, if you will only hold fast to the tip of my tail.”
passages.vernacular: 「必須做點乜嘢嚟救我哋。我想我可以游到岸邊,把木筏拖喺我後面,只要你哋緊抓我嘅尾巴尖。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「必須做點什麼來救我們。我想我可以游到岸邊,把木筏拖在我後面,只要你們緊抓我的尾巴尖。」

passages.original: So he sprang into the water, and the Tin Woodman caught fast hold of his tail. Then the Lion began to swim with all his might toward the shore. It was hard work, although he was so big; but by and by they were drawn out of the current, and then Dorothy took the Tin Woodman’s long pole and helped push the raft to the land.
passages.vernacular: 於是佢跳入水中,鐵皮樵夫緊緊抓住佢嘅尾巴。然後獅子開始用盡全力向岸邊游。雖然佢咁大,呢都係艱難嘅工作;但漸漸地佢哋被拉出咗水流,然後桃樂絲攞起鐵皮樵夫嘅長竿子,幫忙把木筏撐向陸地。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是他跳入水中,鐵皮樵夫緊緊抓住他的尾巴。然後獅子開始用盡全力向岸邊游。雖然他那麼大,這也是艱難的工作;但漸漸地他們被拉出了水流,然後桃樂絲拿起鐵皮樵夫的長竿子,幫忙把木筏撐向陸地。

passages.original: They were all tired out when they reached the shore at last and stepped off upon the pretty green grass, and they also knew that the stream had carried them a long way past the road of yellow brick that led to the Emerald City.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋終於到岸,踏上漂亮嘅綠草地時,都累壞喇,而且都知道河水把佢哋沖過通往翡翠城嘅黃磚路好遠喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們終於到岸,踏上漂亮的綠草地時,都累壞了,而且也知道河水把他們沖過通往翡翠城的黃磚路很遠了。

passages.original: “What shall we do now?” asked the Tin Woodman, as the Lion lay down on the grass to let the sun dry him.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋而家點算?」鐵皮樵夫問,呢陣獅子躺喺草地上讓太陽把佢曬乾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們現在怎麼辦?」鐵皮樵夫問,這時獅子躺在草地上讓太陽把他曬乾。

passages.original: “We must get back to the road, in some way,” said Dorothy.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋必須以某種方式回到路上,」桃樂絲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們必須以某種方式回到路上,」桃樂絲說。

passages.original: “The best plan will be to walk along the riverbank until we come to the road again,” remarked the Lion.
passages.vernacular: 「最好嘅計畫係沿河岸走,直到再回到路上,」獅子講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「最好的計畫是沿河岸走,直到再回到路上,」獅子說。

passages.original: So, when they were rested, Dorothy picked up her basket and they started along the grassy bank, to the road from which the river had carried them. It was a lovely country, with plenty of flowers and fruit trees and sunshine to cheer them, and had they not felt so sorry for the poor Scarecrow, they could have been very happy.
passages.vernacular: 於是,休息後,桃樂絲攞起籃子,佢哋沿住長滿草嘅河岸出發,往河水把佢哋沖離嘅路走。嗰個係一個可愛嘅國度,有許多花、果樹同陽光讓佢哋高興,如果佢哋唔係咁為可憐嘅稻草人難過,佢哋本可以好快樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是,休息後,桃樂絲拿起籃子,他們沿著長滿草的河岸出發,往河水把他們沖離的路走。那是一個可愛的國度,有許多花、果樹和陽光讓他們高興,如果他們不是那麼為可憐的稻草人難過,他們本可以很快樂。

passages.original: They walked along as fast as they could, Dorothy only stopping once to pick a beautiful flower; and after a time the Tin Woodman cried out: “Look!”
passages.vernacular: 佢哋盡快地走,桃樂絲只停下一次摘一朵漂亮嘅花;過咗一會兒鐵皮樵夫喊道:「睇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們盡快地走,桃樂絲只停下一次摘一朵漂亮的花;過了一會兒鐵皮樵夫喊道:「看!」

passages.original: Then they all looked at the river and saw the Scarecrow perched upon his pole in the middle of the water, looking very lonely and sad.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢哋都睇向河,睇到稻草人棲喺佢嘅桿子上,喺水嘅中間,睇起嚟好孤獨悲傷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他們都看向河,看到稻草人棲在他的桿子上,在水的中間,看起來非常孤獨悲傷。

passages.original: “What can we do to save him?” asked Dorothy.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋點樣才能救佢?」桃樂絲問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們怎樣才能救他?」桃樂絲問。

passages.original: The Lion and the Woodman both shook their heads, for they did not know. So they sat down upon the bank and gazed wistfully at the Scarecrow until a Stork flew by, who, upon seeing them, stopped to rest at the water’s edge.
passages.vernacular: 獅子同樵夫都搖咗搖頭,因為佢哋唔知道。於是佢哋坐喺岸邊,若有所思地凝視住稻草人,直到一隻鸛飛過,睇到佢哋,停喺水邊休息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 獅子和樵夫都搖了搖頭,因為他們不知道。於是他們坐在岸邊,若有所思地凝視著稻草人,直到一隻鸛飛過,看到他們,停在水邊休息。

passages.original: “Who are you and where are you going?” asked the Stork.
passages.vernacular: 「你哋係邊個,要去邊度?」鸛問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你們是誰,要去哪裡?」鸛問。

passages.original: “I am Dorothy,” answered the girl, “and these are my friends, the Tin Woodman and the Cowardly Lion; and we are going to the Emerald City.”
passages.vernacular: 「我係桃樂絲,」女孩回答,「呢啲係我嘅朋友,鐵皮樵夫同膽小嘅獅子;我哋要去翡翠城。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我是桃樂絲,」女孩回答,「這些是我的朋友,鐵皮樵夫和膽小的獅子;我們要去翡翠城。」

passages.original: “This isn’t the road,” said the Stork, as she twisted her long neck and looked sharply at the queer party.
passages.vernacular: 「呢唔係路,」鸛講,扭動佢嘅長脖子,銳利地睇住呢支奇怪嘅隊伍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這不是路,」鸛說,扭動她的長脖子,銳利地看著這支奇怪的隊伍。

passages.original: “I know it,” returned Dorothy, “but we have lost the Scarecrow, and are wondering how we shall get him again.”
passages.vernacular: 「我知道,」桃樂絲回答,「但我哋失去咗稻草人,喺想點樣才能把佢找回嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我知道,」桃樂絲回答,「但我們失去了稻草人,在想怎樣才能把他找回來。」

passages.original: “Where is he?” asked the Stork.
passages.vernacular: 「佢喺邊度?」鸛問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他在哪裡?」鸛問。

passages.original: “Over there in the river,” answered the little girl.
passages.vernacular: 「就喺嗰邊河裡,」小女孩回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「就在那邊河裡,」小女孩回答。

passages.original: “If he wasn’t so big and heavy I would get him for you,” remarked the Stork.
passages.vernacular: 「如果佢唔係咁大咁重,我會替你把佢弄嚟,」鸛講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果他不是那麼大那麼重,我會替你把他弄來,」鸛說。

passages.original: “He isn’t heavy a bit,” said Dorothy eagerly, “for he is stuffed with straw; and if you will bring him back to us, we shall thank you ever and ever so much.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢啲都不重,」桃樂絲急切地講,「因為佢塞嘅係稻草;如果你把佢帶回畀我哋,我哋會好好感謝你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他一點也不重,」桃樂絲急切地說,「因為他塞的是稻草;如果你把他帶回給我們,我們會非常非常感謝你。」

passages.original: “Well, I’ll try,” said the Stork, “but if I find he is too heavy to carry I shall have to drop him in the river again.”
passages.vernacular: 「好,我試試,」鸛講,「但如果我發現佢太重攞不動,我就得再把佢扔回河裡。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好,我試試,」鸛說,「但如果我發現他太重拿不動,我就得再把他扔回河裡。」

passages.original: So the big bird flew into the air and over the water till she came to where the Scarecrow was perched upon his pole. Then the Stork with her great claws grabbed the Scarecrow by the arm and carried him up into the air and back to the bank, where Dorothy and the Lion and the Tin Woodman and Toto were sitting.
passages.vernacular: 於是大鳥飛到空中,越過水,飛到稻草人棲喺桿子上嘅地方。然後鸛用佢巨大嘅爪子抓住稻草人嘅手臂,把佢帶到空中,回到岸邊,桃樂絲、獅子、鐵皮樵夫同托托正坐喺嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是大鳥飛到空中,越過水,飛到稻草人棲在桿子上的地方。然後鸛用她巨大的爪子抓住稻草人的手臂,把他帶到空中,回到岸邊,桃樂絲、獅子、鐵皮樵夫和托托正坐在那裡。

passages.original: When the Scarecrow found himself among his friends again, he was so happy that he hugged them all, even the Lion and Toto; and as they walked along he sang “Tol-de-ri-de-oh!” at every step, he felt so gay.
passages.vernacular: 稻草人發現自己又同朋友哋喺一起時,高興得抱住佢哋所有人,連獅子同托托都抱喇;佢哋走路時,佢每走一步都唱住「托爾德里德哦!」佢咁快活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 稻草人發現自己又和朋友們在一起時,高興得抱住他們所有人,連獅子和托托也抱了;他們走路時,他每走一步都唱著「托爾德里德哦!」他那麼快活。

passages.original: “I was afraid I should have to stay in the river forever,” he said, “but the kind Stork saved me, and if I ever get any brains I shall find the Stork again and do her some kindness in return.”
passages.vernacular: 「我怕我得永遠留喺河裡,」佢講,「但好心嘅鸛救咗我,如果我有咗腦子,我要再找到鸛,做些好事報答佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我怕我得永遠留在河裡,」他說,「但好心的鸛救了我,如果我有了腦子,我要再找到鸛,做些好事報答她。」

passages.original: “That’s all right,” said the Stork, who was flying along beside them. “I always like to help anyone in trouble. But I must go now, for my babies are waiting in the nest for me. I hope you will find the Emerald City and that Oz will help you.”
passages.vernacular: 「冇關係,」鸛講,佢喺佢哋旁邊飛。「我總鍾意幫助任何有困難嘅人。但我而家必須走喇,因為我嘅細路哋喺巢裡等我。我希望你哋找到翡翠城,奧茲能幫助你哋。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒關係,」鸛說,她在他們旁邊飛。「我總喜歡幫助任何有困難的人。但我現在必須走了,因為我的孩子們在巢裡等我。我希望你們找到翡翠城,奧茲能幫助你們。」

passages.original: “Thank you,” replied Dorothy, and then the kind Stork flew into the air and was soon out of sight.
passages.vernacular: 「謝謝你,」桃樂絲回答,然後好心嘅鸛飛向空中,不久就消失喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「謝謝你,」桃樂絲回答,然後好心的鸛飛向空中,不久就消失了。

passages.original: They walked along listening to the singing of the brightly colored birds and looking at the lovely flowers which now became so thick that the ground was carpeted with them. There were big yellow and white and blue and purple blossoms, besides great clusters of scarlet poppies, which were so brilliant in color they almost dazzled Dorothy’s eyes.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋邊走邊聽顏色鮮豔嘅鳥歌唱,睇住而家長得咁密、把地面鋪成地毯嘅可愛花朵。有大朵嘅黃色、白色、藍色同紫色嘅花,仲有成簇嘅猩紅色罌粟花,顏色咁鮮豔,幾乎使桃樂絲眼花繚亂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們邊走邊聽顏色鮮豔的鳥歌唱,看著現在長得那麼密、把地面鋪成地毯的可愛花朵。有大朵的黃色、白色、藍色和紫色的花,還有成簇的猩紅色罌粟花,顏色那麼鮮豔,幾乎使桃樂絲眼花繚亂。

passages.original: “Aren’t they beautiful?” the girl asked, as she breathed in the spicy scent of the bright flowers.
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋不美嗎?」女孩問,吸住鮮豔花朵嘅辛香氣味。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「它們不美嗎?」女孩問,吸著鮮豔花朵的辛香氣味。

passages.original: “I suppose so,” answered the Scarecrow. “When I have brains, I shall probably like them better.”
passages.vernacular: 「我想係嘅,」稻草人回答。「等我有咗腦子,我大概會更鍾意佢哋。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想是的,」稻草人回答。「等我有了腦子,我大概會更喜歡它們。」

passages.original: “If I only had a heart, I should love them,” added the Tin Woodman.
passages.vernacular: 「如果我有心,我會愛佢哋,」鐵皮樵夫補充講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果我有心,我會愛它們,」鐵皮樵夫補充說。

passages.original: “I always did like flowers,” said the Lion. “They seem so helpless and frail. But there are none in the forest so bright as these.”
passages.vernacular: 「我一向鍾意花,」獅子講。「佢哋睇起嚟咁無助、脆弱。但森林裡冇像呢啲咁鮮豔嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我一向喜歡花,」獅子說。「它們看起來那麼無助、脆弱。但森林裡沒有像這些這麼鮮豔的。」

passages.original: They now came upon more and more of the big scarlet poppies, and fewer and fewer of the other flowers; and soon they found themselves in the midst of a great meadow of poppies. Now it is well known that when there are many of these flowers together their odor is so powerful that anyone who breathes it falls asleep, and if the sleeper is not carried away from the scent of the flowers, he sleeps on and on forever. But Dorothy did not know this, nor could she get away from the bright red flowers that were everywhere about; so presently her eyes grew heavy and she felt she must sit down to rest and to sleep.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋而家遇到越嚟越多嘅大猩紅罌粟花,越嚟越少其他嘅花;不久佢哋發現自己置身於一大片罌粟花草地中央。而家眾所周知,當許多咁樣嘅花喺一起時,佢哋嘅氣味咁強烈,任何呼吸佢嘅人都會瞓住,如果瞓住嘅人不被帶離花嘅氣味,佢就會一直瞓下去,直到永遠。但桃樂絲唔知道呢個,佢都無法離開四周到處都係嘅鮮紅花朵;所以不久佢嘅眼睛變沉,覺得必須坐下休息、瞓覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們現在遇到越來越多的大猩紅罌粟花,越來越少其他的花;不久他們發現自己置身於一大片罌粟花草地中央。現在眾所周知,當許多這樣的花在一起時,它們的氣味那麼強烈,任何呼吸它的人都會睡著,如果睡著的人不被帶離花的氣味,他就會一直睡下去,直到永遠。但桃樂絲不知道這個,她也無法離開四周到處都是的鮮紅花朵;所以不久她的眼睛變沉,覺得必須坐下休息、睡覺。

passages.original: But the Tin Woodman would not let her do this.
passages.vernacular: 但鐵皮樵夫不讓佢咁樣做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但鐵皮樵夫不讓她這樣做。

passages.original: “We must hurry and get back to the road of yellow brick before dark,” he said; and the Scarecrow agreed with him. So they kept walking until Dorothy could stand no longer. Her eyes closed in spite of herself and she forgot where she was and fell among the poppies, fast asleep.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋必須趕快,天黑前回到黃磚路,」佢講;稻草人同意佢。所以佢哋繼續走,直到桃樂絲再都站不住喇。佢嘅眼睛不由自主地閉上,佢忘咗自己喺邊度,倒喺罌粟花中,沉沉瞓去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們必須趕快,天黑前回到黃磚路,」他說;稻草人同意他。所以他們繼續走,直到桃樂絲再也站不住了。她的眼睛不由自主地閉上,她忘了自己在哪裡,倒在罌粟花中,沉沉睡去。

passages.original: “What shall we do?” asked the Tin Woodman.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋點算?」鐵皮樵夫問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們怎麼辦?」鐵皮樵夫問。

passages.original: “If we leave her here she will die,” said the Lion. “The smell of the flowers is killing us all. I myself can scarcely keep my eyes open, and the dog is asleep already.”
passages.vernacular: 「如果我哋把佢留喺呢度,佢會死,」獅子講。「花嘅氣味正在殺死我哋所有人。我自己幾乎睜不開眼睛,狗已經瞓住喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果我們把她留在這裡,她會死,」獅子說。「花的氣味正在殺死我們所有人。我自己幾乎睜不開眼睛,狗已經睡著了。」

passages.original: It was true; Toto had fallen down beside his little mistress. But the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman, not being made of flesh, were not troubled by the scent of the flowers.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係真嘅;托托已倒喺佢小主人旁邊。但稻草人同鐵皮樵夫唔係血肉做嘅,不受花香嘅困擾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是真的;托托已倒在他小主人旁邊。但稻草人和鐵皮樵夫不是血肉做的,不受花香的困擾。

passages.original: “Run fast,” said the Scarecrow to the Lion, “and get out of this deadly flower bed as soon as you can. We will bring the little girl with us, but if you should fall asleep you are too big to be carried.”
passages.vernacular: 「快跑,」稻草人對獅子講,「盡快離開呢片致命嘅花床。我哋會把小女孩帶住,但如果你瞓住喇,你太大,抬不動。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「快跑,」稻草人對獅子說,「盡快離開這片致命的花床。我們會把小女孩帶著,但如果你睡著了,你太大,抬不動。」

passages.original: So the Lion aroused himself and bounded forward as fast as he could go. In a moment he was out of sight.
passages.vernacular: 於是獅子振作起嚟,盡佢所能快地向前跳去。轉眼間佢已睇唔見喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是獅子振作起來,盡他所能快地向前跳去。轉眼間他已看不見了。

passages.original: “Let us make a chair with our hands and carry her,” said the Scarecrow. So they picked up Toto and put the dog in Dorothy’s lap, and then they made a chair with their hands for the seat and their arms for the arms and carried the sleeping girl between them through the flowers.
passages.vernacular: 「讓我哋用手做一把椅子抬佢,」稻草人講。於是佢哋攞起托托,把狗放喺桃樂絲嘅腿上,然後用手做椅座、用手臂做扶手,抬住瞓住嘅女孩穿過花叢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「讓我們用手做一把椅子抬她,」稻草人說。於是他們拿起托托,把狗放在桃樂絲的腿上,然後用手做椅座、用手臂做扶手,抬著睡著的女孩穿過花叢。

passages.original: On and on they walked, and it seemed that the great carpet of deadly flowers that surrounded them would never end. They followed the bend of the river, and at last came upon their friend the Lion, lying fast asleep among the poppies. The flowers had been too strong for the huge beast and he had given up at last, and fallen only a short distance from the end of the poppy bed, where the sweet grass spread in beautiful green fields before them.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋走啊走,似乎圍住佢哋嘅致命花朵嘅大地毯永遠唔會結束。佢哋沿住河嘅彎道走,最後遇到咗佢哋嘅朋友獅子,佢躺喺罌粟花中沉瞓。花對呢頭巨獸太強喇,佢終於放棄喇,倒喺離罌粟花床盡頭只有一小段距離嘅地方,嗰度甜美嘅青草喺佢哋面前鋪成美麗嘅綠野。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們走啊走,似乎圍著他們的致命花朵的大地毯永遠不會結束。他們沿著河的彎道走,最後遇到了他們的朋友獅子,他躺在罌粟花中沉睡。花對這頭巨獸太強了,他終於放棄了,倒在離罌粟花床盡頭只有一小段距離的地方,那裡甜美的青草在他們面前鋪成美麗的綠野。

passages.original: “We can do nothing for him,” said the Tin Woodman, sadly; “for he is much too heavy to lift. We must leave him here to sleep on forever, and perhaps he will dream that he has found courage at last.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋對佢無能為力,」鐵皮樵夫悲傷地講;「因為佢太重,抬不動。我哋必須把佢留喺呢度永遠瞓下去,或者佢會夢見佢終於找到咗勇氣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們對他無能為力,」鐵皮樵夫悲傷地說;「因為他太重,抬不動。我們必須把他留在這裡永遠睡下去,也許他會夢見他終於找到了勇氣。」

passages.original: “I’m sorry,” said the Scarecrow. “The Lion was a very good comrade for one so cowardly. But let us go on.”
passages.vernacular: 「我好抱歉,」稻草人講。「對咁膽小嘅人來講,獅子係個好好嘅同伴。但我哋繼續走吧。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我很抱歉,」稻草人說。「對這麼膽小的人來說,獅子是個很好的同伴。但我們繼續走吧。」

passages.original: They carried the sleeping girl to a pretty spot beside the river, far enough from the poppy field to prevent her breathing any more of the poison of the flowers, and here they laid her gently on the soft grass and waited for the fresh breeze to waken her.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋把瞓住嘅女孩抬到河邊一個漂亮嘅地方,離罌粟花田夠遠,不讓佢再吸入更多花嘅毒氣,喺呢度佢哋輕輕地把佢放喺柔軟嘅草地上,等清新嘅微風叫醒佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們把睡著的女孩抬到河邊一個漂亮的地方,離罌粟花田夠遠,不讓她再吸入更多花的毒氣,在這裡他們輕輕地把她放在柔軟的草地上,等清新的微風叫醒她。

chapters.title: Chapter IX: The Queen of the Field Mice 第九章:田鼠女王

passages.original: “We cannot be far from the road of yellow brick, now,” remarked the Scarecrow, as he stood beside the girl, “for we have come nearly as far as the river carried us away.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋而家離黃磚路唔會遠喇,」稻草人站喺女孩旁邊講,「因為我哋差不多走回咗河水把我哋沖離嘅距離。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們現在離黃磚路不會遠了,」稻草人站在女孩旁邊說,「因為我們差不多走回了河水把我們沖離的距離。」

passages.original: The Tin Woodman was about to reply when he heard a low growl, and turning his head (which worked beautifully on hinges) he saw a strange beast come bounding over the grass toward them. It was, indeed, a great yellow Wildcat, and the Woodman thought it must be chasing something, for its ears were lying close to its head and its mouth was wide open, showing two rows of ugly teeth, while its red eyes glowed like balls of fire. As it came nearer the Tin Woodman saw that running before the beast was a little gray field mouse, and although he had no heart he knew it was wrong for the Wildcat to try to kill such a pretty, harmless creature.
passages.vernacular: 鐵皮樵夫正要回答,呢陣聽到一聲低沉嘅咆哮,轉過頭(佢嘅頭喺鉸鏈上轉得好靈活),佢睇到一頭奇怪嘅野獸蹦跳住穿過草地向佢哋跑嚟。嗰確實係一隻大黃色山貓,樵夫認為牠一定喺追趕乜嘢,因為牠嘅耳朵貼近頭部,嘴巴大張,露出兩排醜陋嘅牙齒,紅眼睛像火球一樣發光。佢走近時,鐵皮樵夫睇到喺野獸前面跑住一隻灰色嘅小田鼠,雖然佢冇心,佢知道山貓試圖殺死咁漂亮、無害嘅生物係不對嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鐵皮樵夫正要回答,這時聽到一聲低沉的咆哮,轉過頭(他的頭在鉸鏈上轉得很靈活),他看到一頭奇怪的野獸蹦跳著穿過草地向他們跑來。那確實是一隻大黃色山貓,樵夫認為牠一定在追趕什麼,因為牠的耳朵貼近頭部,嘴巴大張,露出兩排醜陋的牙齒,紅眼睛像火球一樣發光。它走近時,鐵皮樵夫看到在野獸前面跑著一隻灰色的小田鼠,雖然他沒有心,他知道山貓試圖殺死這麼漂亮、無害的生物是不對的。

passages.original: So the Woodman raised his axe, and as the Wildcat ran by he gave it a quick blow that cut the beast’s head clean off from its body, and it rolled over at his feet in two pieces.
passages.vernacular: 於是樵夫舉起斧頭,山貓跑過時,佢迅速一擊,把野獸嘅頭乾淨地從身體上砍下,佢喺佢腳邊滾成兩截。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是樵夫舉起斧頭,山貓跑過時,他迅速一擊,把野獸的頭乾淨地從身體上砍下,它在他腳邊滾成兩截。

passages.original: The field mouse, now that it was freed from its enemy, stopped short; and coming slowly up to the Woodman it said, in a squeaky little voice:
passages.vernacular: 田鼠而家擺脫咗敵人,猛地停住;慢慢走近樵夫,用尖細嘅小聲音講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 田鼠現在擺脫了敵人,猛地停住;慢慢走近樵夫,用尖細的小聲音說:

passages.original: “Oh, thank you! Thank you ever so much for saving my life.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,謝謝你!好好感謝你救咗我嘅命。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,謝謝你!非常非常感謝你救了我的命。」

passages.original: “Don’t speak of it, I beg of you,” replied the Woodman. “I have no heart, you know, so I am careful to help all those who may need a friend, even if it happens to be only a mouse.”
passages.vernacular: 「求你別提,」樵夫回答。「你知道,我冇心,所以我小心地幫助所有可能需要朋友嘅人,即使碰巧只係一隻老鼠。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「求你別提,」樵夫回答。「你知道,我沒有心,所以我小心地幫助所有可能需要朋友的人,即使碰巧只是一隻老鼠。」

passages.original: “Only a mouse!” cried the little animal, indignantly. “Why, I am a Queen—the Queen of all the Field Mice!”
passages.vernacular: 「只係一隻老鼠!」小動物憤慨地喊道。「哎呀,我係女王——所有田鼠嘅女王!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「只是一隻老鼠!」小動物憤慨地喊道。「哎呀,我是女王——所有田鼠的女王!」

passages.original: “Oh, indeed,” said the Woodman, making a bow.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,真嘅,」樵夫鞠躬講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,真的,」樵夫鞠躬說。

passages.original: “Therefore you have done a great deed, as well as a brave one, in saving my life,” added the Queen.
passages.vernacular: 「因此你救咗我嘅命,係一件偉大嘅事,都係勇敢嘅事,」女王補充講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「因此你救了我的命,是一件偉大的事,也是勇敢的事,」女王補充說。

passages.original: At that moment several mice were seen running up as fast as their little legs could carry them, and when they saw their Queen they exclaimed:
passages.vernacular: 呢陣睇到幾隻老鼠用牠哋小腿能跑嘅最快速度跑嚟,睇到牠哋嘅女王時,牠哋喊道:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時看到幾隻老鼠用牠們小腿能跑的最快速度跑來,看到牠們的女王時,牠們喊道:

passages.original: “Oh, your Majesty, we thought you would be killed! How did you manage to escape the great Wildcat?” They all bowed so low to the little Queen that they almost stood upon their heads.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,陛下,我哋以為您會被殺!您係點樣逃過嗰隻大山貓嘅?」牠哋都向小女王鞠躬咁低,幾乎頭住地站。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,陛下,我們以為您會被殺!您是怎樣逃過那隻大山貓的?」牠們都向小女王鞠躬那麼低,幾乎頭著地站。

passages.original: “This funny tin man,” she answered, “killed the Wildcat and saved my life. So hereafter you must all serve him, and obey his slightest wish.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢個滑稽嘅錫人,」佢回答,「殺咗山貓,救咗我嘅命。所以今後你哋都必須為佢服務,服從佢最輕微嘅願望。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這個滑稽的錫人,」她回答,「殺了山貓,救了我的命。所以今後你們都必須為他服務,服從他最輕微的願望。」

passages.original: “We will!” cried all the mice, in a shrill chorus. And then they scampered in all directions, for Toto had awakened from his sleep, and seeing all these mice around him he gave one bark of delight and jumped right into the middle of the group. Toto had always loved to chase mice when he lived in Kansas, and he saw no harm in it.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋會嘅!」所有老鼠用尖銳嘅齊聲喊道。然後牠哋向四面八方逃散,因為托托已從瞓夢中醒嚟,睇到周圍咁多老鼠,高興地叫咗一聲,直跳進呢群中間。托托喺堪薩斯時一向鍾意追老鼠,佢睇不出有乜嘢害處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們會的!」所有老鼠用尖銳的齊聲喊道。然後牠們向四面八方逃散,因為托托已從睡夢中醒來,看到周圍這麼多老鼠,高興地叫了一聲,直跳進這群中間。托托在堪薩斯時一向喜歡追老鼠,他看不出有什麼害處。

passages.original: But the Tin Woodman caught the dog in his arms and held him tight, while he called to the mice, “Come back! Come back! Toto shall not hurt you.”
passages.vernacular: 但鐵皮樵夫把狗抱喺懷裡抱緊,同時對老鼠喊道:「回嚟!回嚟!托托唔會傷害你哋。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但鐵皮樵夫把狗抱在懷裡抱緊,同時對老鼠喊道:「回來!回來!托托不會傷害你們。」

passages.original: At this the Queen of the Mice stuck her head out from underneath a clump of grass and asked, in a timid voice, “Are you sure he will not bite us?”
passages.vernacular: 聽到呢個,老鼠女王從一叢草下面探出頭嚟,用膽怯嘅聲音問:「你確定佢唔會咬我哋嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽到這個,老鼠女王從一叢草下面探出頭來,用膽怯的聲音問:「你確定他不會咬我們嗎?」

passages.original: “I will not let him,” said the Woodman; “so do not be afraid.”
passages.vernacular: 「我唔會讓佢,」樵夫講;「所以唔好害怕。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不會讓他,」樵夫說;「所以不要害怕。」

passages.original: One by one the mice came creeping back, and Toto did not bark again, although he tried to get out of the Woodman’s arms, and would have bitten him had he not known very well he was made of tin. Finally one of the biggest mice spoke.
passages.vernacular: 老鼠一隻一隻悄悄爬回嚟,托托冇再叫,雖然佢試圖掙脫樵夫嘅懷抱,如果佢唔係好清楚佢係錫做嘅,佢會咬佢喇。最後一隻最大嘅老鼠講話喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老鼠一隻一隻悄悄爬回來,托托沒有再叫,雖然他試圖掙脫樵夫的懷抱,如果他不是很清楚他是錫做的,他會咬他了。最後一隻最大的老鼠說話了。

passages.original: “Is there anything we can do,” it asked, “to repay you for saving the life of our Queen?”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋有乜嘢可以做嘅,」牠問,「嚟報答您救咗我哋女王嘅命?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們有什麼可以做的,」牠問,「來報答您救了我們女王的命?」

passages.original: “Nothing that I know of,” answered the Woodman; but the Scarecrow, who had been trying to think, but could not because his head was stuffed with straw, said, quickly, “Oh, yes; you can save our friend, the Cowardly Lion, who is asleep in the poppy bed.”
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道有乜嘢,」樵夫回答;但稻草人一直喺試著想,卻因為頭塞滿稻草想不出嚟,佢好快地講:「哦,係嘅;你哋可以救我哋嘅朋友,膽小嘅獅子,佢瞓喺罌粟花床裡。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道有什麼,」樵夫回答;但稻草人一直在試著想,卻因為頭塞滿稻草想不出來,他很快地說:「哦,是的;你們可以救我們的朋友,膽小的獅子,他睡在罌粟花床裡。」

passages.original: “A Lion!” cried the little Queen. “Why, he would eat us all up.”
passages.vernacular: 「一頭獅子!」小女王喊道。「哎呀,佢會把我哋全食喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一頭獅子!」小女王喊道。「哎呀,他會把我們全吃了。」

passages.original: “Oh, no,” declared the Scarecrow; “this Lion is a coward.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,唔會,」稻草人宣稱;「呢頭獅子係個膽小鬼。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,不會,」稻草人宣稱;「這頭獅子是個膽小鬼。」

passages.original: “Really?” asked the Mouse.
passages.vernacular: 「真嘅?」老鼠問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真的?」老鼠問。

passages.original: “He says so himself,” answered the Scarecrow, “and he would never hurt anyone who is our friend. If you will help us to save him I promise that he shall treat you all with kindness.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢自己咁樣講,」稻草人回答,「佢絕唔會傷害我哋嘅任何朋友。如果你哋幫我哋救佢,我保證佢會友善地對待你哋所有人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他自己這樣說,」稻草人回答,「他絕不會傷害我們的任何朋友。如果你們幫我們救他,我保證他會友善地對待你們所有人。」

passages.original: “Very well,” said the Queen, “we trust you. But what shall we do?”
passages.vernacular: 「好好,」女王講,「我哋信任你。但我哋該點做?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很好,」女王說,「我們信任你。但我們該怎麼做?」

passages.original: “Are there many of these mice which call you Queen and are willing to obey you?”
passages.vernacular: 「有好多叫你女王並願意服從你嘅老鼠嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有很多叫你女王並願意服從你的老鼠嗎?」

passages.original: “Oh, yes; there are thousands,” she replied.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,有,有幾千隻,」佢回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,有,有幾千隻,」她回答。

passages.original: “Then send for them all to come here as soon as possible, and let each one bring a long piece of string.”
passages.vernacular: 「咁派人叫牠哋全都盡快到呢度嚟,每隻帶一根長繩子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼派人叫牠們全都盡快到這裡來,每隻帶一根長繩子。」

passages.original: The Queen turned to the mice that attended her and told them to go at once and get all her people. As soon as they heard her orders they ran away in every direction as fast as possible.
passages.vernacular: 女王轉向侍從嘅老鼠,告訴牠哋即刻去叫佢所有嘅子民。牠哋一聽到佢嘅命令,就以最快嘅速度向各個方向跑去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 女王轉向侍從的老鼠,告訴牠們立刻去叫她所有的子民。牠們一聽到她的命令,就以最快的速度向各個方向跑去。

passages.original: “Now,” said the Scarecrow to the Tin Woodman, “you must go to those trees by the riverside and make a truck that will carry the Lion.”
passages.vernacular: 「而家,」稻草人對鐵皮樵夫講,「你必須到河邊嗰啲樹嗰度,做一輛能運獅子嘅板車。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在,」稻草人對鐵皮樵夫說,「你必須到河邊那些樹那裡,做一輛能運獅子的板車。」

passages.original: So the Woodman went at once to the trees and began to work; and he soon made a truck out of the limbs of trees, from which he chopped away all the leaves and branches. He fastened it together with wooden pegs and made the four wheels out of short pieces of a big tree trunk. So fast and so well did he work that by the time the mice began to arrive the truck was all ready for them.
passages.vernacular: 於是樵夫即刻去樹嗰度開始工作;不久佢用樹枝做成咗一輛板車,砍掉所有葉子同小枝。佢用木釘把佢釘喺一起,用一根大樹幹嘅短段做四個輪子。佢工作得咁快咁好,老鼠開始到達時板車已為牠哋準備好喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是樵夫立刻去樹那裡開始工作;不久他用樹枝做成了一輛板車,砍掉所有葉子和小枝。他用木釘把它釘在一起,用一根大樹幹的短段做四個輪子。他工作得那麼快那麼好,老鼠開始到達時板車已為牠們準備好了。

passages.original: They came from all directions, and there were thousands of them: big mice and little mice and middle-sized mice; and each one brought a piece of string in his mouth. It was about this time that Dorothy woke from her long sleep and opened her eyes. She was greatly astonished to find herself lying upon the grass, with thousands of mice standing around and looking at her timidly. But the Scarecrow told her about everything, and turning to the dignified little Mouse, he said:
passages.vernacular: 牠哋從四面八方嚟,有成千上萬隻:大老鼠、小老鼠同中等大小嘅老鼠;每隻嘴裡叼住一根繩子。大約呢陣桃樂絲從長長嘅瞓眠中醒嚟,睜開眼睛。佢好驚訝地發現自己躺喺草地上,有成千上萬隻老鼠站喺周圍,膽怯地睇住佢。但稻草人把一切告訴咗佢,轉向嗰隻威嚴嘅小老鼠,佢講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 牠們從四面八方來,有成千上萬隻:大老鼠、小老鼠和中等大小的老鼠;每隻嘴裡叼著一根繩子。大約這時桃樂絲從長長的睡眠中醒來,睜開眼睛。她非常驚訝地發現自己躺在草地上,有成千上萬隻老鼠站在周圍,膽怯地看著她。但稻草人把一切告訴了她,轉向那隻威嚴的小老鼠,他說:

passages.original: “Permit me to introduce to you her Majesty, the Queen.”
passages.vernacular: 「請允許我向您介紹女王陛下。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「請允許我向您介紹女王陛下。」

passages.original: Dorothy nodded gravely and the Queen made a curtsy, after which she became quite friendly with the little girl.
passages.vernacular: 桃樂絲嚴肅地點咗點頭,女王行咗個屈膝禮,之後佢同小女孩變得相當友好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 桃樂絲嚴肅地點了點頭,女王行了個屈膝禮,之後她同小女孩變得相當友好。

passages.original: The Scarecrow and the Woodman now began to fasten the mice to the truck, using the strings they had brought. One end of a string was tied around the neck of each mouse and the other end to the truck. Of course the truck was a thousand times bigger than any of the mice who were to draw it; but when all the mice had been harnessed, they were able to pull it quite easily. Even the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman could sit on it, and were drawn swiftly by their queer little horses to the place where the Lion lay asleep.
passages.vernacular: 稻草人同樵夫而家開始用牠哋帶嚟嘅繩子把老鼠繫喺板車上。每根繩子嘅一端繫喺一隻老鼠嘅脖子上,另一端繫喺板車上。當然板車比拉佢嘅任何一隻老鼠大一千倍;但當所有老鼠都套上咗韁繩,牠哋能相當輕易地拉動佢。連稻草人同鐵皮樵夫都能坐喺上面,被佢哋嘅奇特小馬迅速拉到獅子瞓覺嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 稻草人和樵夫現在開始用牠們帶來的繩子把老鼠繫在板車上。每根繩子的一端繫在一隻老鼠的脖子上,另一端繫在板車上。當然板車比拉它的任何一隻老鼠大一千倍;但當所有老鼠都套上了韁繩,牠們能相當輕易地拉動它。連稻草人和鐵皮樵夫也能坐在上面,被他們的奇特小馬迅速拉到獅子睡覺的地方。

passages.original: After a great deal of hard work, for the Lion was heavy, they managed to get him up on the truck. Then the Queen hurriedly gave her people the order to start, for she feared if the mice stayed among the poppies too long they also would fall asleep.
passages.vernacular: 經過大量艱苦嘅工作,因為獅子好重,佢哋設法把佢弄上咗板車。然後女王急忙下令讓佢嘅子民出發,因為佢怕老鼠喺罌粟花中待太久,牠哋都會瞓住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 經過大量艱苦的工作,因為獅子很重,他們設法把他弄上了板車。然後女王急忙下令讓她的子民出發,因為她怕老鼠在罌粟花中待太久,牠們也會睡著。

passages.original: At first the little creatures, many though they were, could hardly stir the heavily loaded truck; but the Woodman and the Scarecrow both pushed from behind, and they got along better. Soon they rolled the Lion out of the poppy bed to the green fields, where he could breathe the sweet, fresh air again, instead of the poisonous scent of the flowers.
passages.vernacular: 起初呢啲小生物雖然數量好多,卻幾乎拉不動重載嘅板車;但樵夫同稻草人都從後面推,佢哋走得好些喇。不久佢哋把獅子推出罌粟花床,到咗綠色嘅田野,喺嗰度佢可以再次呼吸甜美、新鮮嘅空氣,而唔係花嘅有毒氣味。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 起初這些小生物雖然數量很多,卻幾乎拉不動重載的板車;但樵夫和稻草人都從後面推,它們走得好些了。不久他們把獅子推出罌粟花床,到了綠色的田野,在那裡他可以再次呼吸甜美、新鮮的空氣,而不是花的有毒氣味。

passages.original: Dorothy came to meet them and thanked the little mice warmly for saving her companion from death. She had grown so fond of the big Lion she was glad he had been rescued.
passages.vernacular: 桃樂絲嚟迎接佢哋,熱烈地感謝小老鼠救佢嘅同伴脫離死亡。佢已經咁鍾意呢頭大獅子,好高興佢被救喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 桃樂絲來迎接他們,熱烈地感謝小老鼠救她的同伴脫離死亡。她已經那麼喜歡這頭大獅子,很高興他被救了。

passages.original: Then the mice were unharnessed from the truck and scampered away through the grass to their homes. The Queen of the Mice was the last to leave.
passages.vernacular: 然後老鼠哋從板車上卸下,飛快地穿過草地跑回家。老鼠女王最後離開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後老鼠們從板車上卸下,飛快地穿過草地跑回家。老鼠女王最後離開。

passages.original: “If ever you need us again,” she said, “come out into the field and call, and we shall hear you and come to your assistance. Good-bye!”
passages.vernacular: 「如果你哋再需要我哋,」佢講,「到田野裡嚟叫,我哋會聽到,嚟幫助你哋。再見!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果你們再需要我們,」她說,「到田野裡來叫,我們會聽到,來幫助你們。再見!」

passages.original: “Good-bye!” they all answered, and away the Queen ran, while Dorothy held Toto tightly lest he should run after her and frighten her.
passages.vernacular: 「再見!」佢哋都回答,女王跑走喇,桃樂絲緊緊抱住托托,免得佢追佢,嚇到佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「再見!」他們都回答,女王跑走了,桃樂絲緊緊抱著托托,免得他追她,嚇到她。

passages.original: After this they sat down beside the Lion until he should awaken; and the Scarecrow brought Dorothy some fruit from a tree near by, which she ate for her dinner.
passages.vernacular: 之後佢哋坐喺獅子旁邊,直到佢醒嚟;稻草人從附近嘅一棵樹上畀桃樂絲摘咗些水果,佢食咗當午飯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 之後他們坐在獅子旁邊,直到他醒來;稻草人從附近的一棵樹上給桃樂絲摘了些水果,她吃了當午飯。

chapters.title: Chapter X: The Guardian of the Gate 第十章:城門守衛

passages.original: It was some time before the Cowardly Lion awakened, for he had lain among the poppies a long while, breathing in their deadly fragrance; but when he did open his eyes and roll off the truck he was very glad to find himself still alive.
passages.vernacular: 過咗一段時間膽小嘅獅子才醒嚟,因為佢喺罌粟花中躺咗好久,吸入佢哋致命嘅芳香;但當佢真嘅睜開眼睛、從板車上滾下嚟時,佢好高興發現自己仲活住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過了一段時間膽小的獅子才醒來,因為他在罌粟花中躺了很久,吸入它們致命的芳香;但當他真的睜開眼睛、從板車上滾下來時,他很高興發現自己還活著。

passages.original: “I ran as fast as I could,” he said, sitting down and yawning, “but the flowers were too strong for me. How did you get me out?”
passages.vernacular: 「我盡我所能快地跑,」佢講,坐下嚟打呵欠,「但花對我太強喇。你哋係點樣把我弄出嚟嘅?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我盡我所能快地跑,」他說,坐下來打呵欠,「但花對我太強了。你們是怎樣把我弄出來的?」

passages.original: Then they told him of the field mice, and how they had generously saved him from death; and the Cowardly Lion laughed, and said:
passages.vernacular: 然後佢哋告訴佢關於田鼠嘅事,同牠哋點樣慷慨地救佢脫離死亡;膽小嘅獅子笑喇,講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他們告訴他關於田鼠的事,和牠們怎樣慷慨地救他脫離死亡;膽小的獅子笑了,說:

passages.original: “I have always thought myself very big and terrible; yet such little things as flowers came near to killing me, and such small animals as mice have saved my life. How strange it all is! But, comrades, what shall we do now?”
passages.vernacular: 「我一直認為自己好大、好可怕;然而像花咁樣小嘅嘢差點殺死我,像老鼠咁樣小嘅動物救咗我嘅命。呢一切幾咁奇怪!但係,同志哋,我哋而家點算?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我一直認為自己很大、很可怕;然而像花這樣小的東西差點殺死我,像老鼠這樣小的動物救了我的命。這一切多麼奇怪!但是,同志們,我們現在怎麼辦?」

passages.original: “We must journey on until we find the road of yellow brick again,” said Dorothy, “and then we can keep on to the Emerald City.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋必須繼續旅行,直到再次找到黃磚路,」桃樂絲講,「然後我哋可以繼續前往翡翠城。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們必須繼續旅行,直到再次找到黃磚路,」桃樂絲說,「然後我們可以繼續前往翡翠城。」

passages.original: So, the Lion being fully refreshed, and feeling quite himself again, they all started upon the journey, greatly enjoying the walk through the soft, fresh grass; and it was not long before they reached the road of yellow brick and turned again toward the Emerald City where the Great Oz dwelt.
passages.vernacular: 於是,獅子完全恢復,感覺又係自己喇,佢哋都出發旅行,好享受喺柔軟新鮮嘅草地上走路;不久佢哋就到咗黃磚路,再次轉向大奧茲居住嘅翡翠城。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是,獅子完全恢復,感覺又是自己了,他們都出發旅行,非常享受在柔軟新鮮的草地上走路;不久他們就到了黃磚路,再次轉向大奧茲居住的翡翠城。

passages.original: The road was smooth and well paved, now, and the country about was beautiful, so that the travelers rejoiced in leaving the forest far behind, and with it the many dangers they had met in its gloomy shades. Once more they could see fences built beside the road; but these were painted green, and when they came to a small house, in which a farmer evidently lived, that also was painted green. They passed by several of these houses during the afternoon, and sometimes people came to the doors and looked at them as if they would like to ask questions; but no one came near them nor spoke to them because of the great Lion, of which they were very much afraid. The people were all dressed in clothing of a lovely emerald-green color and wore peaked hats like those of the Munchkins.
passages.vernacular: 路而家平坦,鋪得好好,周圍嘅鄉野好美,旅行者哋好高興把森林遠遠拋喺後面,連同佢哋喺佢陰暗處遇到嘅許多危險。佢哋再次睇到路旁建嘅籬笆;但呢啲漆成綠色,佢哋嚟到一所顯然係農夫住嘅小房子,佢都漆成綠色。下午佢哋經過好幾所咁樣嘅房子,有時人哋嚟到門口睇佢哋,好像想問問題;但因為嗰頭大獅子,冇人靠近佢哋或同佢哋講話,佢哋好怕佢。人哋都穿住可愛嘅翡翠綠色衣服,戴住像芒奇金人嗰樣嘅尖帽子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 路現在平坦,鋪得很好,周圍的鄉野很美,旅行者們很高興把森林遠遠拋在後面,連同他們在它陰暗處遇到的許多危險。他們再次看到路旁建的籬笆;但這些漆成綠色,他們來到一所顯然是農夫住的小房子,它也漆成綠色。下午他們經過好幾所這樣的房子,有時人們來到門口看他們,好像想問問題;但因為那頭大獅子,沒有人靠近他們或同他們說話,他們非常怕他。人們都穿著可愛的翡翠綠色衣服,戴著像芒奇金人那樣的尖帽子。

passages.original: “This must be the Land of Oz,” said Dorothy, “and we are surely getting near the Emerald City.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢一定係奧茲國,」桃樂絲講,「我哋肯定正在接近翡翠城。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這一定是奧茲國,」桃樂絲說,「我們肯定正在接近翡翠城。」

passages.original: “Yes,” answered the Scarecrow. “Everything is green here, while in the country of the Munchkins blue was the favorite color. But the people do not seem to be as friendly as the Munchkins, and I’m afraid we shall be unable to find a place to pass the night.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,」稻草人回答。「呢度一切都係綠色嘅,而喺芒奇金人嘅國家,藍色係最喜愛嘅顏色。但呢度嘅人似乎不像芒奇金人咁友好,我恐怕我哋找唔到過夜嘅地方。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,」稻草人回答。「這裡一切都是綠色的,而在芒奇金人的國家,藍色是最喜愛的顏色。但這裡的人似乎不像芒奇金人那麼友好,我恐怕我們找不到過夜的地方。」

passages.original: “I should like something to eat besides fruit,” said the girl, “and I’m sure Toto is nearly starved. Let us stop at the next house and talk to the people.”
passages.vernacular: 「我想食水果以外嘅嘢,」女孩講,「我確信托托快餓死喇。讓我哋喺下一所房子停下,同人哋談談。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想吃水果以外的東西,」女孩說,「我確信托托快餓死了。讓我們在下一所房子停下,同人們談談。」

passages.original: So, when they came to a good-sized farmhouse, Dorothy walked boldly up to the door and knocked.
passages.vernacular: 於是,佢哋嚟到一所相當大嘅農舍,桃樂絲大膽地走到門前敲門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是,他們來到一所相當大的農舍,桃樂絲大膽地走到門前敲門。

passages.original: A woman opened it just far enough to look out, and said, “What do you want, child, and why is that great Lion with you?”
passages.vernacular: 一個女人把門開咗剛好能往外睇嘅縫,講:「細路,你要乜嘢,點解嗰頭大獅子同你喺一起?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個女人把門開了剛好能往外看的縫,說:「孩子,你要什麼,為什麼那頭大獅子同你在一起?」

passages.original: “We wish to pass the night with you, if you will allow us,” answered Dorothy; “and the Lion is my friend and comrade, and would not hurt you for the world.”
passages.vernacular: 「如果您允許,我哋想同您過夜,」桃樂絲回答;「獅子係我嘅朋友同同伴,無論如何都唔會傷害您。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果您允許,我們想同您過夜,」桃樂絲回答;「獅子是我的朋友和同伴,無論如何都不會傷害您。」

passages.original: “Is he tame?” asked the woman, opening the door a little wider.
passages.vernacular: 「佢係馴服嘅嗎?」女人問,把門開得稍寬啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他是馴服的嗎?」女人問,把門開得稍寬一些。

passages.original: “Oh, yes,” said the girl, “and he is a great coward, too. He will be more afraid of you than you are of him.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,係嘅,」女孩講,「而且佢係個大膽小鬼。佢會比您更怕您。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,是的,」女孩說,「而且他是個大膽小鬼。他會比您更怕您。」

passages.original: “Well,” said the woman, after thinking it over and taking another peep at the Lion, “if that is the case you may come in, and I will give you some supper and a place to sleep.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,」女人想咗想,又瞥咗一眼獅子後講,「如果係咁樣,你哋可以進嚟,我畀你哋啲晚飯同瞓覺嘅地方。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,」女人想了想,又瞥了一眼獅子後說,「如果是這樣,你們可以進來,我給你們一些晚飯和睡覺的地方。」
