passages.original: So they all entered the house, where there were, besides the woman, two children and a man. The man had hurt his leg, and was lying on the couch in a corner. They seemed greatly surprised to see so strange a company, and while the woman was busy laying the table the man asked:
passages.vernacular: 於是佢哋都進咗房子,嗰度除咗女人,仲有兩個細路同一個男人。男人傷咗腿,躺喺角落嘅長椅上。佢哋似乎對睇到咁奇怪嘅一群人好驚訝,女人忙住擺桌子時,男人問:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是他們都進了房子,那裡除了女人,還有兩個孩子和一個男人。男人傷了腿,躺在角落的長椅上。他們似乎對看到這麼奇怪的一群人非常驚訝,女人忙著擺桌子時,男人問:

passages.original: “Where are you all going?”
passages.vernacular: 「你哋都要去邊度?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你們都要去哪裡?」

passages.original: “To the Emerald City,” said Dorothy, “to see the Great Oz.”
passages.vernacular: 「去翡翠城,」桃樂絲講,「見大奧茲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「去翡翠城,」桃樂絲說,「見大奧茲。」

passages.original: “Oh, indeed!” exclaimed the man. “Are you sure that Oz will see you?”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,真嘅!」男人喊道。「你哋確定奧茲會見你哋嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,真的!」男人喊道。「你們確定奧茲會見你們嗎?」

passages.original: “Why not?” she replied.
passages.vernacular: 「點解唔會?」佢回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「為什麼不會?」她回答。

passages.original: “Why, it is said that he never lets anyone come into his presence. I have been to the Emerald City many times, and it is a beautiful and wonderful place; but I have never been permitted to see the Great Oz, nor do I know of any living person who has seen him.”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,據講佢從不讓任何人到佢面前。我去過翡翠城好多次,嗰個係個美麗奇妙嘅地方;但我從冇被允許見到大奧茲,我都唔知道有任何活住嘅人見過佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,據說他從不讓任何人到他面前。我去過翡翠城很多次,那是個美麗奇妙的地方;但我從沒被允許見到大奧茲,我也不知道有任何活著的人見過他。」

passages.original: “Does he never go out?” asked the Scarecrow.
passages.vernacular: 「佢從不出去嗎?」稻草人問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他從不出去嗎?」稻草人問。

passages.original: “Never. He sits day after day in the great Throne Room of his Palace, and even those who wait upon him do not see him face to face.”
passages.vernacular: 「從不。佢日復一日坐喺宮殿嘅大王座廳裡,連伺候佢嘅人都見唔到佢嘅面。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「從不。他日復一日坐在宮殿的大王座廳裡,連伺候他的人也見不到他的面。」

passages.original: “What is he like?” asked the girl.
passages.vernacular: 「佢長乜嘢樣?」女孩問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他長什麼樣?」女孩問。

passages.original: “That is hard to tell,” said the man thoughtfully. “You see, Oz is a Great Wizard, and can take on any form he wishes. So that some say he looks like a bird; and some say he looks like an elephant; and some say he looks like a cat. To others he appears as a beautiful fairy, or a brownie, or in any other form that pleases him. But who the real Oz is, when he is in his own form, no living person can tell.”
passages.vernacular: 「好難講,」男人若有所思地講。「你知道,奧茲係個大巫師,可以變成任何佢想要嘅形狀。所以有人講佢像一隻鳥;有人講佢像一頭大象;有人講佢像一隻貓。對另啲人,佢顯現為美麗嘅仙女,或小精靈,或任何佢鍾意嘅其他形狀。但真正嘅奧茲,當佢處於自己嘅形態時係邊個,冇活住嘅人能講。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很難說,」男人若有所思地說。「你知道,奧茲是個大巫師,可以變成任何他想要的形狀。所以有人說他像一隻鳥;有人說他像一頭大象;有人說他像一隻貓。對另一些人,他顯現為美麗的仙女,或小精靈,或任何他喜歡的其他形狀。但真正的奧茲,當他處於自己的形態時是誰,沒有活著的人能說。」

passages.original: “That is very strange,” said Dorothy, “but we must try, in some way, to see him, or we shall have made our journey for nothing.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰太奇怪喇,」桃樂絲講,「但我哋必須設法以某種方式見到佢,否則我哋嘅旅程就白費喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那太奇怪了,」桃樂絲說,「但我們必須設法以某種方式見到他,否則我們的旅程就白費了。」

passages.original: “Why do you wish to see the terrible Oz?” asked the man.
passages.vernacular: 「你哋點解想見可怕嘅奧茲?」男人問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你們為什麼想見可怕的奧茲?」男人問。

passages.original: “I want him to give me some brains,” said the Scarecrow eagerly.
passages.vernacular: 「我想請佢畀我啲腦子,」稻草人急切地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想請他給我一些腦子,」稻草人急切地說。

passages.original: “Oh, Oz could do that easily enough,” declared the man. “He has more brains than he needs.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,奧茲好容易做到,」男人宣稱。「佢嘅腦子比佢需要嘅仲多。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,奧茲很容易做到,」男人宣稱。「他的腦子比他需要的還多。」

passages.original: “And I want him to give me a heart,” said the Tin Woodman.
passages.vernacular: 「我想請佢畀我一顆心,」鐵皮樵夫講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想請他給我一顆心,」鐵皮樵夫說。

passages.original: “That will not trouble him,” continued the man, “for Oz has a large collection of hearts, of all sizes and shapes.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰唔會難倒佢,」男人繼續講,「因為奧茲有一大批心嘅收藏,各種大小同形狀都有。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那不會難倒他,」男人繼續說,「因為奧茲有一大批心的收藏,各種大小和形狀都有。」

passages.original: “And I want him to give me courage,” said the Cowardly Lion.
passages.vernacular: 「我想請佢畀我勇氣,」膽小嘅獅子講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想請他給我勇氣,」膽小的獅子說。

passages.original: “Oz keeps a great pot of courage in his Throne Room,” said the man, “which he has covered with a golden plate, to keep it from running over. He will be glad to give you some.”
passages.vernacular: 「奧茲喺王座廳裡有一大罐勇氣,」男人講,「佢用一個金盤蓋住,防止佢溢出嚟。佢會樂意畀你啲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「奧茲在王座廳裡有一大罐勇氣,」男人說,「他用一個金盤蓋住,防止它溢出來。他會樂意給你一些。」

passages.original: “And I want him to send me back to Kansas,” said Dorothy.
passages.vernacular: 「我想請佢送我回堪薩斯,」桃樂絲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想請他送我回堪薩斯,」桃樂絲說。

passages.original: “Where is Kansas?” asked the man, with surprise.
passages.vernacular: 「堪薩斯喺邊度?」男人驚訝地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「堪薩斯在哪裡?」男人驚訝地問。

passages.original: “I don’t know,” replied Dorothy sorrowfully, “but it is my home, and I’m sure it’s somewhere.”
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道,」桃樂絲悲傷地回答,「但佢係我嘅家,我肯定佢喺某處。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道,」桃樂絲悲傷地回答,「但它是我的家,我肯定它在某處。」

passages.original: “Very likely. Well, Oz can do anything; so I suppose he will find Kansas for you. But first you must get to see him, and that will be a hard task; for the Great Wizard does not like to see anyone, and he usually has his own way. But what do YOU want?” he continued, speaking to Toto. Toto only wagged his tail; for, strange to say, he could not speak.
passages.vernacular: 「好可能。嗯,奧茲乜嘢都能做;所以我想佢會替你找到堪薩斯。但首先你哋必須設法見到佢,嗰將係個艱難嘅任務;因為大巫師不鍾意見任何人,佢通常總是隨心所欲。但你想要乜嘢?」佢繼續講,對托托講話。托托只係搖尾巴;因為,講都奇怪,佢唔能夠講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很可能。嗯,奧茲什麼都能做;所以我想他會替你找到堪薩斯。但首先你們必須設法見到他,那將是個艱難的任務;因為大巫師不喜歡見任何人,他通常總是隨心所欲。但你想要什麼?」他繼續說,對托托說話。托托只是搖尾巴;因為,說也奇怪,他不能說話。

passages.original: The woman now called to them that supper was ready, so they gathered around the table and Dorothy ate some delicious porridge and a dish of scrambled eggs and a plate of nice white bread, and enjoyed her meal. The Lion ate some of the porridge, but did not care for it, saying it was made from oats and oats were food for horses, not for lions. The Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman ate nothing at all. Toto ate a little of everything, and was glad to get a good supper again.
passages.vernacular: 女人而家喊佢哋講晚飯好喇,於是佢哋圍住桌子坐下,桃樂絲食咗啲美味嘅粥、一盤炒蛋同一盤好嘅白麵包,享受佢嘅一餐。獅子食咗啲粥,但不鍾意,講佢係燕麥做嘅,燕麥係馬嘅食物,唔係獅子嘅。稻草人同鐵皮樵夫乜嘢都冇食。托托每樣都食咗啲,好高興又食上一頓好晚飯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 女人現在喊他們說晚飯好了,於是他們圍著桌子坐下,桃樂絲吃了一些美味的粥、一盤炒蛋和一盤好的白麵包,享受她的一餐。獅子吃了一些粥,但不喜歡,說它是燕麥做的,燕麥是馬的食物,不是獅子的。稻草人和鐵皮樵夫什麼也沒吃。托托每樣都吃了一點,很高興又吃上一頓好晚飯。

passages.original: The woman now gave Dorothy a bed to sleep in, and Toto lay down beside her, while the Lion guarded the door of her room so she might not be disturbed. The Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman stood up in a corner and kept quiet all night, although of course they could not sleep.
passages.vernacular: 女人而家畀桃樂絲一張床瞓,托托躺喺佢旁邊,獅子守住佢房間嘅門,咁樣佢唔會被打擾。稻草人同鐵皮樵夫站喺角落裡整夜安靜,雖然佢哋當然唔能夠瞓覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 女人現在給桃樂絲一張床睡,托托躺在她旁邊,獅子守著她房間的門,這樣她不會被打擾。稻草人和鐵皮樵夫站在角落裡整夜安靜,雖然他們當然不能睡覺。

passages.original: The next morning, as soon as the sun was up, they started on their way, and soon saw a beautiful green glow in the sky just before them.
passages.vernacular: 第二天早晨,太陽一升起,佢哋就上路喇,不久就睇到前面天空有一道美麗嘅綠色光芒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天早晨,太陽一升起,他們就上路了,不久就看到前面天空有一道美麗的綠色光芒。

passages.original: “That must be the Emerald City,” said Dorothy.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰一定係翡翠城,」桃樂絲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那一定是翡翠城,」桃樂絲說。

passages.original: As they walked on, the green glow became brighter and brighter, and it seemed that at last they were nearing the end of their travels. Yet it was afternoon before they came to the great wall that surrounded the City. It was high and thick and of a bright green color.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋往前走,綠色嘅光芒越嚟越亮,似乎佢哋終於接近旅程嘅盡頭喇。但到咗下午,佢哋才嚟到圍繞城市嘅大牆。佢高而厚,係鮮豔嘅綠色。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們往前走,綠色的光芒越來越亮,似乎他們終於接近旅程的盡頭了。但到了下午,他們才來到圍繞城市的大牆。它高而厚,是鮮豔的綠色。

passages.original: In front of them, and at the end of the road of yellow brick, was a big gate, all studded with emeralds that glittered so in the sun that even the painted eyes of the Scarecrow were dazzled by their brilliancy.
passages.vernacular: 喺佢哋面前,黃磚路嘅盡頭,係一扇大門,上面鑲滿翡翠,喺陽光下閃閃發光,連稻草人畫嘅眼睛都被佢哋嘅光輝閃花。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在他們面前,黃磚路的盡頭,是一扇大門,上面鑲滿翡翠,在陽光下閃閃發光,連稻草人畫的眼睛也被它們的光輝閃花。

passages.original: There was a bell beside the gate, and Dorothy pushed the button and heard a silvery tinkle sound within. Then the big gate swung slowly open, and they all passed through and found themselves in a high arched room, the walls of which glistened with countless emeralds.
passages.vernacular: 大門旁有一個鈴,桃樂絲按咗按鈕,聽到裡面傳嚟銀鈴般嘅叮噹聲。然後大門慢慢打開,佢哋都走過去,發現自己喺一個高大拱形嘅房間裡,牆壁閃耀住無數翡翠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大門旁有一個鈴,桃樂絲按了按鈕,聽到裡面傳來銀鈴般的叮噹聲。然後大門慢慢打開,他們都走過去,發現自己在一個高大拱形的房間裡,牆壁閃耀著無數翡翠。

passages.original: Before them stood a little man about the same size as the Munchkins. He was clothed all in green, from his head to his feet, and even his skin was of a greenish tint. At his side was a large green box.
passages.vernacular: 喺佢哋面前站住一個小人,同芒奇金人差不多大。佢從頭到腳穿住全綠嘅衣服,連皮膚都帶綠色。佢身旁有一個大綠箱子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在他們面前站著一個小人,同芒奇金人差不多大。他從頭到腳穿著全綠的衣服,連皮膚也帶綠色。他身旁有一個大綠箱子。

passages.original: When he saw Dorothy and her companions the man asked, “What do you wish in the Emerald City?”
passages.vernacular: 睇到桃樂絲同佢嘅同伴時,嗰人問:「你哋要喺翡翠城做乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看到桃樂絲和她的同伴時,那人問:「你們要在翡翠城做什麼?」

passages.original: “We came here to see the Great Oz,” said Dorothy.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋嚟見大奧茲,」桃樂絲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們來見大奧茲,」桃樂絲說。

passages.original: The man was so surprised at this answer that he sat down to think it over.
passages.vernacular: 嗰人聽到呢個回答咁驚訝,坐下嚟思考。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那人聽到這個回答那麼驚訝,坐下來思考。

passages.original: “It has been many years since anyone asked me to see Oz,” he said, shaking his head in perplexity. “He is powerful and terrible, and if you come on an idle or foolish errand to bother the wise reflections of the Great Wizard, he might be angry and destroy you all in an instant.”
passages.vernacular: 「已經有好多年冇人要求我見奧茲喇,」佢講,困惑地搖頭。「佢強大而可怕,如果你哋為無聊或愚蠢嘅事嚟打擾大巫師智慧嘅沉思,佢可能會生氣,瞬間毀滅你哋所有人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「已經有很多年沒有人要求我見奧茲了,」他說,困惑地搖頭。「他強大而可怕,如果你們為無聊或愚蠢的事來打擾大巫師智慧的沉思,他可能會生氣,瞬間毀滅你們所有人。」

passages.original: “But it is not a foolish errand, nor an idle one,” replied the Scarecrow; “it is important. And we have been told that Oz is a good Wizard.”
passages.vernacular: 「但呢唔係愚蠢嘅事,都唔係無聊嘅事,」稻草人回答;「呢個係重要嘅。而且我哋被告知奧茲係個好巫師。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但這不是愚蠢的事,也不是無聊的事,」稻草人回答;「這是重要的。而且我們被告知奧茲是個好巫師。」

passages.original: “So he is,” said the green man, “and he rules the Emerald City wisely and well. But to those who are not honest, or who approach him from curiosity, he is most terrible, and few have ever dared ask to see his face. I am the Guardian of the Gates, and since you demand to see the Great Oz I must take you to his Palace. But first you must put on the spectacles.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢係,」綠人講,「佢治理翡翠城聰明而良好。但對於嗰啲不誠實、或出於好奇接近佢嘅人,佢係最可怕嘅,好少人敢要求見佢嘅臉。我係城門守衛,既然你哋要求見大奧茲,我必須帶你哋去佢嘅宮殿。但首先你哋必須戴上眼鏡。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他是,」綠人說,「他治理翡翠城聰明而良好。但對於那些不誠實、或出於好奇接近他的人,他是最可怕的,很少人敢要求見他的臉。我是城門守衛,既然你們要求見大奧茲,我必須帶你們去他的宮殿。但首先你們必須戴上眼鏡。」

passages.original: “Why?” asked Dorothy.
passages.vernacular: 「點解?」桃樂絲問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「為什麼?」桃樂絲問。

passages.original: “Because if you did not wear spectacles the brightness and glory of the Emerald City would blind you. Even those who live in the City must wear spectacles night and day. They are all locked on, for Oz so ordered it when the City was first built, and I have the only key that will unlock them.”
passages.vernacular: 「因為如果你哋不戴眼鏡,翡翠城嘅光輝同榮耀會讓你哋失明。連住喺城裡嘅人都必須日夜戴眼鏡。佢哋都鎖上喇,因為城市最初建造時奧茲咁樣下令,而且我有唯一能打開佢哋嘅鑰匙。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「因為如果你們不戴眼鏡,翡翠城的光輝和榮耀會讓你們失明。連住在城裡的人也必須日夜戴眼鏡。它們都鎖上了,因為城市最初建造時奧茲這樣下令,而且我有唯一能打開它們的鑰匙。」

passages.original: He opened the big box, and Dorothy saw that it was filled with spectacles of every size and shape. All of them had green glasses in them. The Guardian of the Gates found a pair that would just fit Dorothy and put them over her eyes. There were two golden bands fastened to them that passed around the back of her head, where they were locked together by a little key that was at the end of a chain the Guardian of the Gates wore around his neck. When they were on, Dorothy could not take them off had she wished, but of course she did not wish to be blinded by the glare of the Emerald City, so she said nothing.
passages.vernacular: 佢打開大箱子,桃樂絲睇到裡面滿係各種大小同形狀嘅眼鏡。佢哋全都配有綠色鏡片。城門守衛找到一副剛好適合桃樂絲嘅,戴喺佢嘅眼睛上。上面繫住兩條金帶,繞到佢腦後,喺嗰度用一把小鑰匙鎖喺一起,鑰匙喺城門守衛掛喺脖子上嘅鏈子末端。戴上之後,桃樂絲即使想都摘不下嚟,但當然佢唔想被翡翠城嘅炫光弄瞎,所以佢乜嘢都冇講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他打開大箱子,桃樂絲看到裡面滿是各種大小和形狀的眼鏡。它們全都配有綠色鏡片。城門守衛找到一副剛好適合桃樂絲的,戴在她的眼睛上。上面繫著兩條金帶,繞到她腦後,在那裡用一把小鑰匙鎖在一起,鑰匙在城門守衛掛在脖子上的鏈子末端。戴上之後,桃樂絲即使想也摘不下來,但當然她不想被翡翠城的炫光弄瞎,所以她什麼也沒說。

passages.original: Then the green man fitted spectacles for the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman and the Lion, and even on little Toto; and all were locked fast with the key.
passages.vernacular: 然後綠人畀稻草人、鐵皮樵夫同獅子配咗眼鏡,連小托托都配喇;全部都用鑰匙鎖牢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後綠人給稻草人、鐵皮樵夫和獅子配了眼鏡,連小托托也配了;全部都用鑰匙鎖牢。

passages.original: Then the Guardian of the Gates put on his own glasses and told them he was ready to show them to the Palace. Taking a big golden key from a peg on the wall, he opened another gate, and they all followed him through the portal into the streets of the Emerald City.
passages.vernacular: 然後城門守衛戴上自己嘅眼鏡,告訴佢哋佢準備好帶佢哋去宮殿喇。佢從牆上嘅掛釘上取下一把大金鑰匙,打開另一扇門,佢哋都跟住佢穿過門道,進入翡翠城嘅街道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後城門守衛戴上自己的眼鏡,告訴他們他準備好帶他們去宮殿了。他從牆上的掛釘上取下一把大金鑰匙,打開另一扇門,他們都跟著他穿過門道,進入翡翠城的街道。

chapters.title: Chapter XI: The Wonderful City of Oz 第十一章:奧茲奇妙的城

passages.original: Even with eyes protected by the green spectacles, Dorothy and her friends were at first dazzled by the brilliancy of the wonderful City. The streets were lined with beautiful houses all built of green marble and studded everywhere with sparkling emeralds. They walked over a pavement of the same green marble, and where the blocks were joined together were rows of emeralds, set closely, and glittering in the brightness of the sun. The window panes were of green glass; even the sky above the City had a green tint, and the rays of the sun were green.
passages.vernacular: 即使眼睛戴住綠色眼鏡保護,桃樂絲同佢嘅朋友哋起初都被呢座奇妙城市嘅光輝照得眼花繚亂。街道兩旁排列住美麗嘅房子,全用綠色大理石建成,到處鑲嵌住閃閃發光嘅翡翠。佢哋走喺同樣係綠色大理石嘅路面上,石塊接縫嘅地方嵌住一排排緊密嘅翡翠,喺陽光嘅照耀下閃閃發亮。窗玻璃係綠色嘅;連城市上空嘅天空都帶住綠色,陽光都係綠色嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 即使眼睛戴著綠色眼鏡保護,桃樂絲和她的朋友們起初也被這座奇妙城市的光輝照得眼花繚亂。街道兩旁排列著美麗的房子,全用綠色大理石建成,到處鑲嵌著閃閃發光的翡翠。他們走在同樣是綠色大理石的路面上,石塊接縫的地方嵌著一排排緊密的翡翠,在陽光的照耀下閃閃發亮。窗玻璃是綠色的;連城市上空的天空也帶著綠色,陽光也是綠色的。

passages.original: There were many people—men, women, and children—walking about, and these were all dressed in green clothes and had greenish skins. They looked at Dorothy and her strangely assorted company with wondering eyes, and the children all ran away and hid behind their mothers when they saw the Lion; but no one spoke to them. Many shops stood in the street, and Dorothy saw that everything in them was green. Green candy and green pop-corn were offered for sale, as well as green shoes, green hats, and green clothes of all sorts. At one place a man was selling green lemonade, and when the children bought it Dorothy could see that they paid for it with green pennies.
passages.vernacular: 有許多人——男人、女人同小孩——喺走動,佢哋都穿住綠色嘅衣服,皮膚都帶綠色。佢哋用驚奇嘅眼光睇住桃樂絲同佢呢夥奇特嘅同伴,細路哋一睇到獅子都跑開,躲到媽媽背後;但冇人同佢哋講話。街上有許多商店,桃樂絲睇到裡面嘅嘢全係綠色嘅。有綠色嘅糖果同綠色嘅爆谷出售,仲有綠色嘅鞋子、綠色嘅帽子同各種綠色嘅衣服。有一處,一個男人喺賣綠色檸檬水,細路哋買嘅時候,桃樂絲睇到佢哋付嘅係綠色嘅便士。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有許多人——男人、女人和小孩——在走動,他們都穿著綠色的衣服,皮膚也帶綠色。他們用驚奇的眼光看著桃樂絲和她這夥奇特的同伴,孩子們一看到獅子都跑開,躲到媽媽背後;但沒有人同他們說話。街上有許多商店,桃樂絲看到裡面的東西全是綠色的。有綠色的糖果和綠色的爆谷出售,還有綠色的鞋子、綠色的帽子和各種綠色的衣服。有一處,一個男人在賣綠色檸檬水,孩子們買的時候,桃樂絲看到他們付的是綠色的便士。

passages.original: There seemed to be no horses nor animals of any kind; the men carried things around in little green carts, which they pushed before them. Everyone seemed happy and contented and prosperous.
passages.vernacular: 似乎冇馬,都冇任何動物;男人哋用小綠車子運嘢,喺前面推住走。每個人似乎都快樂、滿足、富裕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 似乎沒有馬,也沒有任何動物;男人們用小綠車子運東西,在前面推著走。每個人似乎都快樂、滿足、富裕。

passages.original: The Guardian of the Gates led them through the streets until they came to a big building, exactly in the middle of the City, which was the Palace of Oz, the Great Wizard. There was a soldier before the door, dressed in a green uniform and wearing a long green beard.
passages.vernacular: 城門守衛帶住佢哋穿過街道,嚟到城市正中嘅一座大建築物前,嗰個係偉大嘅巫師奧茲嘅宮殿。門前有一個士兵,穿住綠色制服,留住長長嘅綠鬍子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 城門守衛帶著他們穿過街道,來到城市正中的一座大建築物前,那是偉大的巫師奧茲的宮殿。門前有一個士兵,穿著綠色制服,留著長長的綠鬍子。

passages.original: “Here are strangers,” said the Guardian of the Gates to him, “and they demand to see the Great Oz.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢度有幾個陌生人,」城門守衛對佢講,「佢哋要求見大奧茲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這裡有幾個陌生人,」城門守衛對他說,「他們要求見大奧茲。」

passages.original: “Step inside,” answered the soldier, “and I will carry your message to him.”
passages.vernacular: 「請進去,」士兵回答,「我會把你哋嘅口信帶畀佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「請進去,」士兵回答,「我會把你們的口信帶給他。」

passages.original: So they passed through the Palace Gates and were led into a big room with a green carpet and lovely green furniture set with emeralds. The soldier made them all wipe their feet upon a green mat before entering this room, and when they were seated he said politely:
passages.vernacular: 於是佢哋走過宮殿嘅大門,被帶進一個大房間,房間鋪住綠地毯,擺住鑲有翡翠嘅可愛綠色家具。進呢個房間之前,士兵叫佢哋都喺一塊綠墊子上擦腳,等佢哋坐好後,佢禮貌地講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是他們走過宮殿的大門,被帶進一個大房間,房間鋪著綠地毯,擺著鑲有翡翠的可愛綠色家具。進這個房間之前,士兵叫他們都在一塊綠墊子上擦腳,等他們坐好後,他禮貌地說:

passages.original: “Please make yourselves comfortable while I go to the door of the Throne Room and tell Oz you are here.”
passages.vernacular: 「請你哋舒服地坐住,我去王座廳門口告訴奧茲你哋嚟喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「請你們舒服地坐著,我去王座廳門口告訴奧茲你們來了。」

passages.original: They had to wait a long time before the soldier returned. When, at last, he came back, Dorothy asked:
passages.vernacular: 士兵過咗好久才回嚟。最後佢回嚟時,桃樂絲問:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 士兵過了很久才回來。最後他回來時,桃樂絲問:

passages.original: “Have you seen Oz?”
passages.vernacular: 「你見到奧茲咗嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你見到奧茲了嗎?」

passages.original: “Oh, no,” returned the soldier; “I have never seen him. But I spoke to him as he sat behind his screen and gave him your message. He said he will grant you an audience, if you so desire; but each one of you must enter his presence alone, and he will admit but one each day. Therefore, as you must remain in the Palace for several days, I will have you shown to rooms where you may rest in comfort after your journey.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,冇,」士兵回答;「我從冇見過佢。但我喺佢坐喺屏風後面時同佢講咗話,把你哋嘅口信告訴咗佢。佢講如果你哋願意,佢會接見你哋;但你哋每個人必須單獨進去見佢,而且佢每天只接見一個。因此,既然你哋要喺宮殿裡待上幾天,我會叫人帶你哋去房間,讓你哋喺旅途之後舒適地休息。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,沒有,」士兵回答;「我從沒見過他。但我在他坐在屏風後面時同他說了話,把你們的口信告訴了他。他說如果你們願意,他會接見你們;但你們每個人必須單獨進去見他,而且他每天只接見一個。因此,既然你們要在宮殿裡待上幾天,我會叫人帶你們去房間,讓你們在旅途之後舒適地休息。」

passages.original: “Thank you,” replied the girl; “that is very kind of Oz.”
passages.vernacular: 「謝謝你,」女孩回答;「奧茲真係太好心喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「謝謝你,」女孩回答;「奧茲真是太好心了。」

passages.original: The soldier now blew upon a green whistle, and at once a young girl, dressed in a pretty green silk gown, entered the room. She had lovely green hair and green eyes, and she bowed low before Dorothy as she said, “Follow me and I will show you your room.”
passages.vernacular: 士兵而家吹咗一個綠色嘅哨子,即刻一個年輕女孩走進房間,佢穿住漂亮嘅綠絲綢長袍。佢有一頭可愛嘅綠頭髮同綠眼睛,佢向桃樂絲深深鞠躬,講:「跟我嚟,我帶你去你嘅房間。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 士兵現在吹了一個綠色的哨子,馬上一個年輕女孩走進房間,她穿著漂亮的綠絲綢長袍。她有一頭可愛的綠頭髮和綠眼睛,她向桃樂絲深深鞠躬,說:「跟我來,我帶你去你的房間。」

passages.original: So Dorothy said good-bye to all her friends except Toto, and taking the dog in her arms followed the green girl through seven passages and up three flights of stairs until they came to a room at the front of the Palace. It was the sweetest little room in the world, with a soft comfortable bed that had sheets of green silk and a green velvet counterpane. There was a tiny fountain in the middle of the room, that shot a spray of green perfume into the air, to fall back into a beautifully carved green marble basin. Beautiful green flowers stood in the windows, and there was a shelf with a row of little green books. When Dorothy had time to open these books she found them full of queer green pictures that made her laugh, they were so funny.
passages.vernacular: 於是桃樂絲向除咗托托以外嘅所有朋友道別,抱住狗,跟住綠衣女孩穿過七條走廊,上咗三層樓梯,嚟到宮殿前面嘅一個房間。嗰個係世界上最可愛嘅小房間,有一張柔軟舒適嘅床,床單係綠絲綢,被面係綠天鵝絨。房間中央有一個小噴泉,向空中噴出一陣綠色香水嘅水霧,再落回一個雕刻精美嘅綠色大理石水盆裡。窗台上擺住美麗嘅綠花,仲有一個架子,上面排住一排小綠書。桃樂絲有空打開呢啲書時,發現裡面滿係古怪嘅綠色圖畫,逗得佢發笑,實在太有趣喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是桃樂絲向除了托托以外的所有朋友道別,抱著狗,跟著綠衣女孩穿過七條走廊,上了三層樓梯,來到宮殿前面的一個房間。那是世界上最可愛的小房間,有一張柔軟舒適的床,床單是綠絲綢,被面是綠天鵝絨。房間中央有一個小噴泉,向空中噴出一陣綠色香水的水霧,再落回一個雕刻精美的綠色大理石水盆裡。窗台上擺著美麗的綠花,還有一個架子,上面排著一排小綠書。桃樂絲有空打開這些書時,發現裡面滿是古怪的綠色圖畫,逗得她發笑,實在太有趣了。

passages.original: In a wardrobe were many green dresses, made of silk and satin and velvet; and all of them fitted Dorothy exactly.
passages.vernacular: 衣櫃裡有許多綠色嘅衣服,用絲、緞同天鵝絨做成;每一件都剛好適合桃樂絲穿。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 衣櫃裡有許多綠色的衣服,用絲、緞和天鵝絨做成;每一件都剛好適合桃樂絲穿。

passages.original: “Make yourself perfectly at home,” said the green girl, “and if you wish for anything ring the bell. Oz will send for you tomorrow morning.”
passages.vernacular: 「請你當自己家一樣,」綠衣女孩講,「如果你需要乜嘢,就搖鈴。奧茲聽日早晨會派人叫你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「請你當自己家一樣,」綠衣女孩說,「如果你需要什麼,就搖鈴。奧茲明天早晨會派人叫你。」

passages.original: She left Dorothy alone and went back to the others. These she also led to rooms, and each one of them found himself lodged in a very pleasant part of the Palace. Of course this politeness was wasted on the Scarecrow; for when he found himself alone in his room he stood stupidly in one spot, just within the doorway, to wait till morning. It would not rest him to lie down, and he could not close his eyes; so he remained all night staring at a little spider which was weaving its web in a corner of the room, just as if it were not one of the most wonderful rooms in the world. The Tin Woodman lay down on his bed from force of habit, for he remembered when he was made of flesh; but not being able to sleep, he passed the night moving his joints up and down to make sure they kept in good working order. The Lion would have preferred a bed of dried leaves in the forest, and did not like being shut up in a room; but he had too much sense to let this worry him, so he sprang upon the bed and rolled himself up like a cat and purred himself asleep in a minute.
passages.vernacular: 佢留下桃樂絲一個人,回到其他人嗰度。佢都帶佢哋去咗房間,每一個人都發現自己住喺宮殿裡好舒適嘅一處。當然,呢番禮貌對稻草人係白費嘅;因為佢發現自己獨自在房間裡時,就呆呆地站喺門口內嘅一個地方,等到早晨。躺下對佢冇休息作用,佢都唔能夠閉上眼睛;所以佢整夜盯住一隻喺房間角落織網嘅小蜘蛛,好像呢唔係世界上最奇妙嘅房間之一似嘅。鐵皮樵夫出於習慣躺喺床上,因為佢記得自己係血肉做嘅時候;但瞓不住,佢整夜上下活動關節,確保佢哋保持良好嘅工作狀態。獅子本來寧願瞓喺森林裡嘅乾葉堆上,不鍾意被關喺房間裡;但佢好有頭腦,不讓呢個困擾佢,於是跳上床,像貓一樣蜷起身子,呼嚕呼嚕,一分鐘就瞓住喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她留下桃樂絲一個人,回到其他人那裡。她也帶他們去了房間,每一個人都發現自己住在宮殿裡很舒適的一處。當然,這番禮貌對稻草人是白費的;因為他發現自己獨自在房間裡時,就呆呆地站在門口內的一個地方,等到早晨。躺下對他沒有休息作用,他也不能閉上眼睛;所以他整夜盯著一隻在房間角落織網的小蜘蛛,好像這不是世界上最奇妙的房間之一似的。鐵皮樵夫出於習慣躺在床上,因為他記得自己是血肉做的時候;但睡不著,他整夜上下活動關節,確保它們保持良好的工作狀態。獅子本來寧願睡在森林裡的乾葉堆上,不喜歡被關在房間裡;但他很有頭腦,不讓這個困擾他,於是跳上床,像貓一樣蜷起身子,呼嚕呼嚕,一分鐘就睡著了。

passages.original: The next morning, after breakfast, the green maiden came to fetch Dorothy, and she dressed her in one of the prettiest gowns, made of green brocaded satin. Dorothy put on a green silk apron and tied a green ribbon around Toto’s neck, and they started for the Throne Room of the Great Oz.
passages.vernacular: 第二天早晨,食過早餐後,綠衣少女嚟接桃樂絲,畀佢穿上一件最漂亮嘅長袍,係綠色錦緞做嘅。桃樂絲繫上一條綠絲圍裙,喺托托脖子上繫咗一條綠絲帶,佢哋出發前往大奧茲嘅王座廳。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天早晨,吃過早餐後,綠衣少女來接桃樂絲,給她穿上一件最漂亮的長袍,是綠色錦緞做的。桃樂絲繫上一條綠絲圍裙,在托托脖子上繫了一條綠絲帶,他們出發前往大奧茲的王座廳。

passages.original: First they came to a great hall in which were many ladies and gentlemen of the court, all dressed in rich costumes. These people had nothing to do but talk to each other, but they always came to wait outside the Throne Room every morning, although they were never permitted to see Oz. As Dorothy entered they looked at her curiously, and one of them whispered:
passages.vernacular: 首先佢哋嚟到一個大廳,裡面有許多朝廷嘅男女,都穿住華麗嘅服裝。呢啲人無事可做,只係互相談話,但佢哋每天早晨總是嚟到王座廳外面等候,雖然佢哋從來不被允許見奧茲。桃樂絲進去時佢哋好奇地睇住佢,其中一個低聲講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 首先他們來到一個大廳,裡面有許多朝廷的男女,都穿著華麗的服裝。這些人無事可做,只是互相談話,但他們每天早晨總是來到王座廳外面等候,雖然他們從來不被允許見奧茲。桃樂絲進去時他們好奇地看著她,其中一個低聲說:

passages.original: “Are you really going to look upon the face of Oz the Terrible?”
passages.vernacular: 「你真嘅要去睇可怕嘅奧茲嘅臉嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你真的要去看可怕的奧茲的臉嗎?」

passages.original: “Of course,” answered the girl, “if he will see me.”
passages.vernacular: 「當然,」女孩回答,「如果佢肯見我嘅話。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然,」女孩回答,「如果他肯見我的話。」

passages.original: “Oh, he will see you,” said the soldier who had taken her message to the Wizard, “although he does not like to have people ask to see him. Indeed, at first he was angry and said I should send you back where you came from. Then he asked me what you looked like, and when I mentioned your silver shoes he was very much interested. At last I told him about the mark upon your forehead, and he decided he would admit you to his presence.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,佢會見你嘅,」嗰個把佢嘅口信帶畀巫師嘅士兵講,「雖然佢不鍾意別人要求見佢。其實,起初佢好生氣,講我應該送你哋回你哋嚟嘅地方。然後佢問我你長乜嘢樣,我提到你嘅銀鞋時,佢好有興趣。最後我告訴佢你額頭上嘅印記,佢就決定接見你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,他會見你的,」那個把她的口信帶給巫師的士兵說,「雖然他不喜歡別人要求見他。其實,起初他很生氣,說我應該送你們回你們來的地方。然後他問我你長什麼樣,我提到你的銀鞋時,他非常有興趣。最後我告訴他你額頭上的印記,他就決定接見你。」

passages.original: Just then a bell rang, and the green girl said to Dorothy, “That is the signal. You must go into the Throne Room alone.”
passages.vernacular: 就喺呢陣鈴響喇,綠衣女孩對桃樂絲講:「嗰個係信號。你必須一個人進王座廳。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在這時鈴響了,綠衣女孩對桃樂絲說:「那是信號。你必須一個人進王座廳。」

passages.original: She opened a little door and Dorothy walked boldly through and found herself in a wonderful place. It was a big, round room with a high arched roof, and the walls and ceiling and floor were covered with large emeralds set closely together. In the center of the roof was a great light, as bright as the sun, which made the emeralds sparkle in a wonderful manner.
passages.vernacular: 佢打開一扇小門,桃樂絲大膽地走過去,發現自己置身於一個奇妙嘅地方。嗰個係一個大而圓嘅房間,屋頂高高拱起,牆壁、天花板同地板都覆蓋住緊密鑲嵌嘅大翡翠。屋頂中央有一盞大燈,像太陽一樣明亮,使翡翠閃耀出奇妙嘅光彩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她打開一扇小門,桃樂絲大膽地走過去,發現自己置身於一個奇妙的地方。那是一個大而圓的房間,屋頂高高拱起,牆壁、天花板和地板都覆蓋著緊密鑲嵌的大翡翠。屋頂中央有一盞大燈,像太陽一樣明亮,使翡翠閃耀出奇妙的光彩。

passages.original: But what interested Dorothy most was the big throne of green marble that stood in the middle of the room. It was shaped like a chair and sparkled with gems, as did everything else. In the center of the chair was an enormous Head, without a body to support it or any arms or legs whatever. There was no hair upon this head, but it had eyes and a nose and mouth, and was much bigger than the head of the biggest giant.
passages.vernacular: 但最令桃樂絲感興趣嘅係立喺房間中央嘅嗰張綠色大理石大王座。佢嘅形狀像一張椅子,像其他一切一樣閃耀住寶石。椅子中央係一個巨大嘅頭,冇身體支撐佢,都冇任何手臂或腿。呢個頭上冇頭髮,卻有眼睛、鼻子同嘴巴,比最大嘅巨人嘅頭仲要大得多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但最令桃樂絲感興趣的是立在房間中央的那張綠色大理石大王座。它的形狀像一張椅子,像其他一切一樣閃耀著寶石。椅子中央是一個巨大的頭,沒有身體支撐它,也沒有任何手臂或腿。這個頭上沒有頭髮,卻有眼睛、鼻子和嘴巴,比最大的巨人的頭還要大得多。

passages.original: As Dorothy gazed upon this in wonder and fear, the eyes turned slowly and looked at her sharply and steadily. Then the mouth moved, and Dorothy heard a voice say:
passages.vernacular: 桃樂絲又驚奇又恐懼地凝視住佢時,嗰雙眼睛慢慢轉動,尖銳而穩定地睇住佢。然後嘴動喇,桃樂絲聽到一個聲音講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 桃樂絲又驚奇又恐懼地凝視著它時,那雙眼睛慢慢轉動,尖銳而穩定地看著她。然後嘴動了,桃樂絲聽到一個聲音說:

passages.original: “I am Oz, the Great and Terrible. Who are you, and why do you seek me?”
passages.vernacular: 「我係奧茲,偉大而可怕嘅。你係邊個,點解嚟找我?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我是奧茲,偉大而可怕的。你是誰,為什麼來找我?」

passages.original: It was not such an awful voice as she had expected to come from the big Head; so she took courage and answered:
passages.vernacular: 呢唔係佢預料從大頭發出嘅嗰種可怕聲音;於是佢鼓起勇氣回答:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這不是她預料從大頭發出的那種可怕聲音;於是她鼓起勇氣回答:

passages.original: “I am Dorothy, the Small and Meek. I have come to you for help.”
passages.vernacular: 「我係桃樂絲,渺小而溫順嘅。我嚟向您求助。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我是桃樂絲,渺小而溫順的。我來向您求助。」

passages.original: The eyes looked at her thoughtfully for a full minute. Then said the voice:
passages.vernacular: 嗰雙眼睛若有所思地睇咗佢足足一分鐘。然後嗰聲音講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那雙眼睛若有所思地看了她足足一分鐘。然後那聲音說:

passages.original: “Where did you get the silver shoes?”
passages.vernacular: 「你從邊度得到銀鞋?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你從哪裡得到銀鞋?」

passages.original: “I got them from the Wicked Witch of the East, when my house fell on her and killed her,” she replied.
passages.vernacular: 「我從東方惡女巫嗰度得到嘅,我嘅房子掉喺佢身上,把佢壓死喇,」佢回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我從東方惡女巫那裡得到的,我的房子掉在她身上,把她壓死了,」她回答。

passages.original: “Where did you get the mark upon your forehead?” continued the voice.
passages.vernacular: 「你額頭上嘅印記係從邊度嚟嘅?」嗰聲音繼續問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你額頭上的印記是從哪裡來的?」那聲音繼續問。

passages.original: “That is where the Good Witch of the North kissed me when she bade me good-bye and sent me to you,” said the girl.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係北方好女巫吻我嘅地方,佢同我道別,把我送嚟見您,」女孩講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是北方好女巫吻我的地方,她同我道別,把我送來見您,」女孩說。

passages.original: Again the eyes looked at her sharply, and they saw she was telling the truth. Then Oz asked, “What do you wish me to do?”
passages.vernacular: 嗰雙眼睛再次銳利地睇住佢,睇出佢講嘅係實話。然後奧茲問:「你要我做乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那雙眼睛再次銳利地看著她,看出她說的是實話。然後奧茲問:「你要我做什麼?」

passages.original: “Send me back to Kansas, where my Aunt Em and Uncle Henry are,” she answered earnestly. “I don’t like your country, although it is so beautiful. And I am sure Aunt Em will be dreadfully worried over my being away so long.”
passages.vernacular: 「送我回堪薩斯,我嘅艾姆嬸嬸同亨利叔叔喺嗰度,」佢認真地回答。「我不鍾意你哋嘅國家,雖然佢咁美麗。而且我肯定艾姆嬸嬸會為我離開咁久而擔心得要命。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「送我回堪薩斯,我的艾姆嬸嬸和亨利叔叔在那裡,」她認真地回答。「我不喜歡你們的國家,雖然它這麼美麗。而且我肯定艾姆嬸嬸會為我離開這麼久而擔心得要命。」

passages.original: The eyes winked three times, and then they turned up to the ceiling and down to the floor and rolled around so queerly that they seemed to see every part of the room. And at last they looked at Dorothy again.
passages.vernacular: 嗰雙眼睛眨咗三下,然後向上睇天花板,向下睇地板,轉得咁古怪,似乎能睇到房間嘅每一個角落。最後佢哋又睇住桃樂絲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那雙眼睛眨了三下,然後向上看天花板,向下看地板,轉得那麼古怪,似乎能看到房間的每一個角落。最後它們又看著桃樂絲。

passages.original: “Why should I do this for you?” asked Oz.
passages.vernacular: 「我點解要為你咁樣做?」奧茲問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我為什麼要為你這樣做?」奧茲問。

passages.original: “Because you are strong and I am weak; because you are a Great Wizard and I am only a little girl.”
passages.vernacular: 「因為您強大而我軟弱;因為您係偉大嘅巫師而我只係個小女孩。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「因為您強大而我軟弱;因為您是偉大的巫師而我只是個小女孩。」

passages.original: “But you were strong enough to kill the Wicked Witch of the East,” said Oz.
passages.vernacular: 「但你強大得足以殺死東方惡女巫,」奧茲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但你強大得足以殺死東方惡女巫,」奧茲說。

passages.original: “That just happened,” returned Dorothy simply; “I could not help it.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰只係碰巧發生嘅,」桃樂絲簡單地回答;「我冇辦法。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那只是碰巧發生的,」桃樂絲簡單地回答;「我沒有辦法。」

passages.original: “Well,” said the Head, “I will give you my answer. You have no right to expect me to send you back to Kansas unless you do something for me in return. In this country everyone must pay for everything he gets. If you wish me to use my magic power to send you home again you must do something for me first. Help me and I will help you.”
passages.vernacular: 「好吧,」嗰個頭講,「我畀你我嘅答覆。你冇權利期望我送你回堪薩斯,除非你為我做點事作為回報。喺呢個國家,每個人得到嘅嘢都必須付出代價。如果你想要我用我嘅魔力送你回家,你必須先為我做點事。幫助我,我就幫助你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧,」那個頭說,「我給你我的答覆。你沒有權利期望我送你回堪薩斯,除非你為我做點事作為回報。在這個國家,每個人得到的東西都必須付出代價。如果你想要我用我的魔力送你回家,你必須先為我做點事。幫助我,我就幫助你。」

passages.original: “What must I do?” asked the girl.
passages.vernacular: 「我必須做乜嘢?」女孩問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我必須做什麼?」女孩問。

passages.original: “Kill the Wicked Witch of the West,” answered Oz.
passages.vernacular: 「殺死西方惡女巫,」奧茲回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「殺死西方惡女巫,」奧茲回答。

passages.original: “But I cannot!” exclaimed Dorothy, greatly surprised.
passages.vernacular: 「但我唔能夠!」桃樂絲好驚訝地喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但我不能!」桃樂絲非常驚訝地喊道。

passages.original: “You killed the Witch of the East and you wear the silver shoes, which bear a powerful charm. There is now but one Wicked Witch left in all this land, and when you can tell me she is dead I will send you back to Kansas—but not before.”
passages.vernacular: 「你殺咗東方女巫,你穿住銀鞋,佢哋帶有強大嘅魔力。而家呢片土地上只剩下一個惡女巫,等你能告訴我佢死喇,我就送你回堪薩斯——但喺嗰之前不行。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你殺了東方女巫,你穿著銀鞋,它們帶有強大的魔力。現在這片土地上只剩下一個惡女巫,等你能告訴我她死了,我就送你回堪薩斯——但在那之前不行。」

passages.original: The little girl began to weep, she was so much disappointed; and the eyes winked again and looked upon her anxiously, as if the Great Oz felt that she could help him if she would.
passages.vernacular: 小女孩開始哭泣,佢太失望喇;嗰雙眼睛又眨咗眨,焦急地睇住佢,好像大奧茲覺得佢只要肯就能幫助佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小女孩開始哭泣,她太失望了;那雙眼睛又眨了眨,焦急地看著她,好像大奧茲覺得她只要肯就能幫助他。

passages.original: “I never killed anything, willingly,” she sobbed. “Even if I wanted to, how could I kill the Wicked Witch? If you, who are Great and Terrible, cannot kill her yourself, how do you expect me to do it?”
passages.vernacular: 「我從不曾存心殺死任何嘢,」佢哭住講。「就算我想,我點殺得咗惡女巫?如果您,偉大而可怕嘅,自己都殺不咗佢,您點期望我做到?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我從不曾存心殺死任何東西,」她哭著說。「就算我想,我怎麼殺得了惡女巫?如果您,偉大而可怕的,自己都殺不了她,您怎麼期望我做到?」

passages.original: “I do not know,” said the Head; “but that is my answer, and until the Wicked Witch dies you will not see your uncle and aunt again. Remember that the Witch is Wicked—tremendously Wicked—and ought to be killed. Now go, and do not ask to see me again until you have done your task.”
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道,」嗰個頭講;「但嗰個係我嘅答覆,惡女巫不死,你就唔會再見到你嘅叔叔嬸嬸。記住,嗰個女巫係邪惡嘅——極其邪惡——應該被殺死。而家走吧,冇完成任務,唔好再要求見我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道,」那個頭說;「但那是我的答覆,惡女巫不死,你就不會再見到你的叔叔嬸嬸。記住,那個女巫是邪惡的——極其邪惡——應該被殺死。現在走吧,沒完成任務,別再要求見我。」

passages.original: Sorrowfully Dorothy left the Throne Room and went back where the Lion and the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman were waiting to hear what Oz had said to her. “There is no hope for me,” she said sadly, “for Oz will not send me home until I have killed the Wicked Witch of the West; and that I can never do.”
passages.vernacular: 桃樂絲傷心地離開王座廳,回到獅子、稻草人同鐵皮樵夫等住聽奧茲對佢講咗乜嘢嘅地方。「我冇希望喇,」佢悲傷地講,「因為奧茲不殺死西方惡女巫就唔會送我回家;而嗰個係我永遠做唔到嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 桃樂絲傷心地離開王座廳,回到獅子、稻草人和鐵皮樵夫等著聽奧茲對她說了什麼的地方。「我沒有希望了,」她悲傷地說,「因為奧茲不殺死西方惡女巫就不會送我回家;而那是我永遠做不到的。」

passages.original: Her friends were sorry, but could do nothing to help her; so Dorothy went to her own room and lay down on the bed and cried herself to sleep.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅朋友哋好難過,但幫不咗佢;於是桃樂絲回到自己嘅房間,躺喺床上哭住瞓住喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的朋友們很難過,但幫不了她;於是桃樂絲回到自己的房間,躺在床上哭著睡著了。

passages.original: The next morning the soldier with the green whiskers came to the Scarecrow and said:
passages.vernacular: 第二天早晨,留綠鬍鬚嘅士兵嚟到稻草人嗰度,講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天早晨,留綠鬍鬚的士兵來到稻草人那裡,說:

passages.original: “Come with me, for Oz has sent for you.”
passages.vernacular: 「跟我嚟,奧茲派人叫你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「跟我來,奧茲派人叫你。」

passages.original: So the Scarecrow followed him and was admitted into the great Throne Room, where he saw, sitting in the emerald throne, a most lovely Lady. She was dressed in green silk gauze and wore upon her flowing green locks a crown of jewels. Growing from her shoulders were wings, gorgeous in color and so light that they fluttered if the slightest breath of air reached them.
passages.vernacular: 於是稻草人跟住佢,被帶進大王座廳,喺嗰度佢睇到翡翠王座上坐住一位最可愛嘅女士。佢穿住綠色絲紗,喺佢流動嘅綠色捲髮上戴住一頂寶石皇冠。佢肩上長住翅膀,色彩華麗,輕得連最輕微嘅一絲空氣吹到都會顫動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是稻草人跟著他,被帶進大王座廳,在那裡他看到翡翠王座上坐著一位最可愛的女士。她穿著綠色絲紗,在她流動的綠色捲髮上戴著一頂寶石皇冠。她肩上長著翅膀,色彩華麗,輕得連最輕微的一絲空氣吹到都會顫動。

passages.original: When the Scarecrow had bowed, as prettily as his straw stuffing would let him, before this beautiful creature, she looked upon him sweetly, and said:
passages.vernacular: 稻草人喺呢位美麗嘅人物面前盡佢稻草填塞嘅身體所能做到嘅優雅鞠咗躬,佢甜美地睇住佢,講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 稻草人在這位美麗的人物面前盡他稻草填塞的身體所能做到的優雅鞠了躬,她甜美地看著他,說:

passages.original: “I am Oz, the Great and Terrible. Who are you, and why do you seek me?”
passages.vernacular: 「我係奧茲,偉大而可怕嘅。你係邊個,點解嚟找我?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我是奧茲,偉大而可怕的。你是誰,為什麼來找我?」

passages.original: Now the Scarecrow, who had expected to see the great Head Dorothy had told him of, was much astonished; but he answered her bravely.
passages.vernacular: 而家稻草人本來預料睇到桃樂絲告訴佢嘅大頭,好驚訝;但佢勇敢地回答佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在稻草人本來預料看到桃樂絲告訴他的大頭,非常驚訝;但他勇敢地回答她。

passages.original: “I am only a Scarecrow, stuffed with straw. Therefore I have no brains, and I come to you praying that you will put brains in my head instead of straw, so that I may become as much a man as any other in your dominions.”
passages.vernacular: 「我只係個稻草人,塞滿稻草。所以我冇腦子,我嚟求您喺我頭上放腦子而唔係稻草,使我能像您領土內任何人一樣成為一個人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我只是個稻草人,塞滿稻草。所以我沒有腦子,我來求您在我頭上放腦子而不是稻草,使我能像您領土內任何人一樣成為一個人。」

passages.original: “Why should I do this for you?” asked the Lady.
passages.vernacular: 「我點解要為你咁樣做?」嗰位女士問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我為什麼要為你這樣做?」那位女士問。

passages.original: “Because you are wise and powerful, and no one else can help me,” answered the Scarecrow.
passages.vernacular: 「因為您聰明而強大,冇別人能幫我,」稻草人回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「因為您聰明而強大,沒有別人能幫我,」稻草人回答。

passages.original: “I never grant favors without some return,” said Oz; “but this much I will promise. If you will kill for me the Wicked Witch of the West, I will bestow upon you a great many brains, and such good brains that you will be the wisest man in all the Land of Oz.”
passages.vernacular: 「冇回報我從不施恩,」奧茲講;「但呢點我可以答應你。如果你為我殺死西方惡女巫,我會畀你好多腦子,而且係咁好嘅腦子,你會成為整個奧茲國最聰明嘅人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有回報我從不施恩,」奧茲說;「但這點我可以答應你。如果你為我殺死西方惡女巫,我會給你很多腦子,而且是那麼好的腦子,你會成為整個奧茲國最聰明的人。」

passages.original: “I thought you asked Dorothy to kill the Witch,” said the Scarecrow, in surprise.
passages.vernacular: 「我以為您要桃樂絲殺死女巫,」稻草人驚訝地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我以為您要桃樂絲殺死女巫,」稻草人驚訝地說。

passages.original: “So I did. I don’t care who kills her. But until she is dead I will not grant your wish. Now go, and do not seek me again until you have earned the brains you so greatly desire.”
passages.vernacular: 「我係要佢殺。我不在乎邊個殺死佢。但佢不死,我唔會答應你嘅願望。而家走吧,喺你贏得你咁渴望嘅腦子之前,唔好再嚟找我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我是要她殺。我不在乎誰殺死她。但她不死,我不會答應你的願望。現在走吧,在你贏得你那麼渴望的腦子之前,別再來找我。」

passages.original: The Scarecrow went sorrowfully back to his friends and told them what Oz had said; and Dorothy was surprised to find that the Great Wizard was not a Head, as she had seen him, but a lovely Lady.
passages.vernacular: 稻草人悲傷地回到朋友嗰度,告訴佢哋奧茲講咗乜嘢;桃樂絲驚訝地發現大巫師唔係佢睇到嘅嗰個頭,而係一位可愛嘅女士。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 稻草人悲傷地回到朋友那裡,告訴他們奧茲說了什麼;桃樂絲驚訝地發現大巫師不是她看到的那個頭,而是一位可愛的女士。

passages.original: “All the same,” said the Scarecrow, “she needs a heart as much as the Tin Woodman.”
passages.vernacular: 「儘管如此,」稻草人講,「佢同鐵皮樵夫一樣需要一顆心。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「儘管如此,」稻草人說,「她和鐵皮樵夫一樣需要一顆心。」

passages.original: On the next morning the soldier with the green whiskers came to the Tin Woodman and said:
passages.vernacular: 第二天早晨,留綠鬍鬚嘅士兵嚟到鐵皮樵夫嗰度,講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天早晨,留綠鬍鬚的士兵來到鐵皮樵夫那裡,說:

passages.original: “Oz has sent for you. Follow me.”
passages.vernacular: 「奧茲派人叫你。跟我嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「奧茲派人叫你。跟我來。」

passages.original: So the Tin Woodman followed him and came to the great Throne Room. He did not know whether he would find Oz a lovely Lady or a Head, but he hoped it would be the lovely Lady. “For,” he said to himself, “if it is the head, I am sure I shall not be given a heart, since a head has no heart of its own and therefore cannot feel for me. But if it is the lovely Lady I shall beg hard for a heart, for all ladies are themselves said to be kindly hearted.”
passages.vernacular: 於是鐵皮樵夫跟住佢,嚟到大王座廳。佢唔知道會發現奧茲係一位可愛嘅女士定係一個頭,但佢希望係嗰位可愛嘅女士。「因為,」佢對自己講,「如果係頭,我肯定得唔到心,因為頭自己冇心,因此唔能夠體恤我。但如果係嗰位可愛嘅女士,我會苦苦哀求要一顆心,因為據講所有女士自己都係好心腸嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是鐵皮樵夫跟著他,來到大王座廳。他不知道會發現奧茲是一位可愛的女士還是一個頭,但他希望是那位可愛的女士。「因為,」他對自己說,「如果是頭,我肯定得不到心,因為頭自己沒有心,因此不能體恤我。但如果是那位可愛的女士,我會苦苦哀求要一顆心,因為據說所有女士自己都是好心腸的。」

passages.original: But when the Woodman entered the great Throne Room he saw neither the Head nor the Lady, for Oz had taken the shape of a most terrible Beast. It was nearly as big as an elephant, and the green throne seemed hardly strong enough to hold its weight. The Beast had a head like that of a rhinoceros, only there were five eyes in its face. There were five long arms growing out of its body, and it also had five long, slim legs. Thick, woolly hair covered every part of it, and a more dreadful-looking monster could not be imagined. It was fortunate the Tin Woodman had no heart at that moment, for it would have beat loud and fast from terror. But being only tin, the Woodman was not at all afraid, although he was much disappointed.
passages.vernacular: 但鐵皮樵夫走進大王座廳時,既冇睇到頭都冇睇到女士,因為奧茲變成咗一頭最可怕嘅野獸。佢幾乎有大象咁大,綠色王座似乎幾乎撐不住佢嘅重量。嗰野獸嘅頭像犀牛嘅,只係臉上有五隻眼睛。佢身上長出五條長手臂,都有五條又長又細嘅腿。濃密嘅羊毛般嘅毛髮覆蓋佢全身,再都想像不出比佢更可怕嘅怪物喇。幸好鐵皮樵夫嗰時冇心,否則佢會因恐懼而劇烈快速地跳動。但鐵皮樵夫只係錫做嘅,啲都不害怕,雖然佢好失望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但鐵皮樵夫走進大王座廳時,既沒看到頭也沒看到女士,因為奧茲變成了一頭最可怕的野獸。它幾乎有大象那麼大,綠色王座似乎幾乎撐不住它的重量。那野獸的頭像犀牛的,只是臉上有五隻眼睛。它身上長出五條長手臂,也有五條又長又細的腿。濃密的羊毛般的毛髮覆蓋它全身,再也想像不出比它更可怕的怪物了。幸好鐵皮樵夫那時沒有心,否則它會因恐懼而劇烈快速地跳動。但鐵皮樵夫只是錫做的,一點也不害怕,雖然他很失望。

passages.original: “I am Oz, the Great and Terrible,” spoke the Beast, in a voice that was one great roar. “Who are you, and why do you seek me?”
passages.vernacular: 「我係奧茲,偉大而可怕嘅,」野獸用一聲巨吼般嘅聲音講。「你係邊個,點解嚟找我?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我是奧茲,偉大而可怕的,」野獸用一聲巨吼般的聲音說。「你是誰,為什麼來找我?」

passages.original: “I am a Woodman, and made of tin. Therefore I have no heart, and cannot love. I pray you to give me a heart that I may be as other men are.”
passages.vernacular: 「我係個樵夫,錫做嘅。所以我冇心,唔能夠愛。我求您畀我一顆心,使我能像別人一樣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我是個樵夫,錫做的。所以我沒有心,不能愛。我求您給我一顆心,使我能像別人一樣。」

passages.original: “Why should I do this?” demanded the Beast.
passages.vernacular: 「我點解要咁樣做?」野獸問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我為什麼要這樣做?」野獸問。

passages.original: “Because I ask it, and you alone can grant my request,” answered the Woodman.
passages.vernacular: 「因為我請求您,只有您能答應我嘅請求,」樵夫回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「因為我請求您,只有您能答應我的請求,」樵夫回答。

passages.original: Oz gave a low growl at this, but said, gruffly: “If you indeed desire a heart, you must earn it.”
passages.vernacular: 奧茲聽到呢個低低地咆哮咗一聲,但粗聲講:「如果你真嘅想要一顆心,你必須贏得佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 奧茲聽到這個低低地咆哮了一聲,但粗聲說:「如果你真的想要一顆心,你必須贏得它。」

passages.original: “How?” asked the Woodman.
passages.vernacular: 「點樣?」樵夫問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「怎樣?」樵夫問。

passages.original: “Help Dorothy to kill the Wicked Witch of the West,” replied the Beast. “When the Witch is dead, come to me, and I will then give you the biggest and kindest and most loving heart in all the Land of Oz.”
passages.vernacular: 「幫助桃樂絲殺死西方惡女巫,」野獸回答。「女巫死咗以後,嚟找我,我就畀你奧茲國裡最大、最善良、最有愛嘅心。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「幫助桃樂絲殺死西方惡女巫,」野獸回答。「女巫死了以後,來找我,我就給你奧茲國裡最大、最善良、最有愛的心。」

passages.original: So the Tin Woodman was forced to return sorrowfully to his friends and tell them of the terrible Beast he had seen. They all wondered greatly at the many forms the Great Wizard could take upon himself, and the Lion said:
passages.vernacular: 於是鐵皮樵夫只好傷心地回到朋友嗰度,告訴佢哋佢睇到嘅嗰頭可怕野獸。佢哋都對大巫師能變成咁多形態感到好驚奇,獅子講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是鐵皮樵夫只好傷心地回到朋友那裡,告訴他們他看到的那頭可怕野獸。他們都對大巫師能變成這麼多形態感到非常驚奇,獅子說:

passages.original: “If he is a Beast when I go to see him, I shall roar my loudest, and so frighten him that he will grant all I ask. And if he is the lovely Lady, I shall pretend to spring upon her, and so compel her to do my bidding. And if he is the great Head, he will be at my mercy; for I will roll this head all about the room until he promises to give us what we desire. So be of good cheer, my friends, for all will yet be well.”
passages.vernacular: 「如果我去見佢時佢係野獸,我會盡我所能大聲吼叫,把佢嚇得答應我所要求嘅一切。如果佢係嗰位可愛嘅女士,我會假裝撲向佢,逼佢照我講嘅做。如果佢係嗰個大頭,佢就任我擺布;因為我會把呢個頭喺房間裡到處滾,直到佢答應畀我哋想要嘅嘢。所以朋友哋,高興點,一切終會好嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果我去見他時他是野獸,我會盡我所能大聲吼叫,把他嚇得答應我所要求的一切。如果他是那位可愛的女士,我會假裝撲向她,逼她照我說的做。如果他是那個大頭,他就任我擺布;因為我會把這個頭在房間裡到處滾,直到他答應給我們想要的東西。所以朋友們,高興點,一切終會好的。」

passages.original: The next morning the soldier with the green whiskers led the Lion to the great Throne Room and bade him enter the presence of Oz.
passages.vernacular: 第二天早晨,留綠鬍鬚嘅士兵帶獅子到大王座廳,叫佢進去見奧茲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天早晨,留綠鬍鬚的士兵帶獅子到大王座廳,叫他進去見奧茲。

passages.original: The Lion at once passed through the door, and glancing around saw, to his surprise, that before the throne was a Ball of Fire, so fierce and glowing he could scarcely bear to gaze upon it. His first thought was that Oz had by accident caught on fire and was burning up; but when he tried to go nearer, the heat was so intense that it singed his whiskers, and he crept back tremblingly to a spot nearer the door.
passages.vernacular: 獅子即刻走過門,環顧四周,驚訝地睇到王座前有一個火球,咁猛烈咁發光,佢幾乎唔敢注視。佢嘅第一個念頭係奧茲意外住咗火,正在燒毀;但佢想走近些時,熱得咁厲害,燒焦咗佢嘅鬍鬚,佢顫抖住爬回靠近門嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 獅子立刻走過門,環顧四周,驚訝地看到王座前有一個火球,那麼猛烈那麼發光,他幾乎不敢注視。他的第一個念頭是奧茲意外著了火,正在燒毀;但他想走近些時,熱得那麼厲害,燒焦了他的鬍鬚,他顫抖著爬回靠近門的地方。

passages.original: Then a low, quiet voice came from the Ball of Fire, and these were the words it spoke:
passages.vernacular: 然後從火球裡傳嚟一個低而平靜嘅聲音,佢講嘅話係:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後從火球裡傳來一個低而平靜的聲音,它說的話是:

passages.original: “I am Oz, the Great and Terrible. Who are you, and why do you seek me?”
passages.vernacular: 「我係奧茲,偉大而可怕嘅。你係邊個,點解嚟找我?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我是奧茲,偉大而可怕的。你是誰,為什麼來找我?」

passages.original: And the Lion answered, “I am a Cowardly Lion, afraid of everything. I came to you to beg that you give me courage, so that in reality I may become the King of Beasts, as men call me.”
passages.vernacular: 獅子回答:「我係一頭膽小嘅獅子,乜嘢都怕。我嚟求您畀我勇氣,使我真嘅能成為人哋叫我嘅百獸之王。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 獅子回答:「我是一頭膽小的獅子,什麼都怕。我來求您給我勇氣,使我真的能成為人們叫我的百獸之王。」

passages.original: “Why should I give you courage?” demanded Oz.
passages.vernacular: 「我點解要畀你勇氣?」奧茲問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我為什麼要給你勇氣?」奧茲問。

passages.original: “Because of all Wizards you are the greatest, and alone have power to grant my request,” answered the Lion.
passages.vernacular: 「因為喺所有巫師中您係最偉大嘅,只有您有權力答應我嘅請求,」獅子回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「因為在所有巫師中您是最偉大的,只有您有權力答應我的請求,」獅子回答。

passages.original: The Ball of Fire burned fiercely for a time, and the voice said, “Bring me proof that the Wicked Witch is dead, and that moment I will give you courage. But as long as the Witch lives, you must remain a coward.”
passages.vernacular: 火球猛烈燃燒咗一會兒,嗰聲音講:「畀我攞證據嚟,證明惡女巫死喇,嗰一刻我就畀你勇氣。但只要女巫活住,你就必須做個膽小鬼。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 火球猛烈燃燒了一會兒,那聲音說:「給我拿證據來,證明惡女巫死了,那一刻我就給你勇氣。但只要女巫活著,你就必須做個膽小鬼。」

passages.original: The Lion was angry at this speech, but could say nothing in reply, and while he stood silently gazing at the Ball of Fire it became so furiously hot that he turned tail and rushed from the room. He was glad to find his friends waiting for him, and told them of his terrible interview with the Wizard.
passages.vernacular: 獅子對呢番話好生氣,但無話可答,佢靜靜地睇住火球時,佢變得咁猛烈地熱,佢轉身就從房間衝出去。佢好高興發現朋友哋喺等佢,把佢同巫師可怕嘅會面告訴咗佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 獅子對這番話很生氣,但無話可答,他靜靜地看著火球時,它變得那麼猛烈地熱,他轉身就從房間衝出去。他很高興發現朋友們在等他,把他同巫師可怕的會面告訴了他們。

passages.original: “What shall we do now?” asked Dorothy sadly.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋而家點算?」桃樂絲悲傷地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們現在怎麼辦?」桃樂絲悲傷地問。

passages.original: “There is only one thing we can do,” returned the Lion, “and that is to go to the land of the Winkies, seek out the Wicked Witch, and destroy her.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋只有一件事可做,」獅子回答,「就係去溫基人嘅國家,找出惡女巫,把佢消滅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們只有一件事可做,」獅子回答,「就是去溫基人的國家,找出惡女巫,把她消滅。」

passages.original: “But suppose we cannot?” said the girl.
passages.vernacular: 「但如果我哋做唔到呢?」女孩講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但如果我們做不到呢?」女孩說。

passages.original: “Then I shall never have courage,” declared the Lion.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰我永遠唔會有勇氣,」獅子宣布。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那我永遠不會有勇氣,」獅子宣布。

passages.original: “And I shall never have brains,” added the Scarecrow.
passages.vernacular: 「我永遠唔會有腦子,」稻草人補充講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我永遠不會有腦子,」稻草人補充說。

passages.original: “And I shall never have a heart,” spoke the Tin Woodman.
passages.vernacular: 「我永遠唔會有心,」鐵皮樵夫講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我永遠不會有心,」鐵皮樵夫說。

passages.original: “And I shall never see Aunt Em and Uncle Henry,” said Dorothy, beginning to cry.
passages.vernacular: 「我永遠見唔到艾姆嬸嬸同亨利叔叔,」桃樂絲講,開始哭起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我永遠見不到艾姆嬸嬸和亨利叔叔,」桃樂絲說,開始哭起來。

passages.original: “Be careful!” cried the green girl. “The tears will fall on your green silk gown and spot it.”
passages.vernacular: 「小心!」綠衣女孩喊道。「眼淚會掉喺你嘅綠絲綢長袍上,弄出污點。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「小心!」綠衣女孩喊道。「眼淚會掉在你的綠絲綢長袍上,弄出污點。」

passages.original: So Dorothy dried her eyes and said, “I suppose we must try it; but I am sure I do not want to kill anybody, even to see Aunt Em again.”
passages.vernacular: 於是桃樂絲擦乾眼睛,講:「我想我哋必須試試;但我肯定我唔想殺任何人,即使係為了再見到艾姆嬸嬸。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是桃樂絲擦乾眼睛,說:「我想我們必須試試;但我肯定我不想殺任何人,即使是為了再見到艾姆嬸嬸。」

passages.original: “I will go with you; but I’m too much of a coward to kill the Witch,” said the Lion.
passages.vernacular: 「我同你去;但我太膽小,殺不咗女巫,」獅子講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我同你去;但我太膽小,殺不了女巫,」獅子說。

passages.original: “I will go too,” declared the Scarecrow; “but I shall not be of much help to you, I am such a fool.”
passages.vernacular: 「我都去,」稻草人宣稱;「但我幫不咗你多少忙,我係咁個傻瓜。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我也去,」稻草人宣稱;「但我幫不了你多少忙,我是這麼個傻瓜。」

passages.original: “I haven’t the heart to harm even a Witch,” remarked the Tin Woodman; “but if you go I certainly shall go with you.”
passages.vernacular: 「我冇嗰個心去傷害邊怕係一個女巫,」鐵皮樵夫講;「但如果你去,我當然同你一起去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我沒有那個心去傷害哪怕是一個女巫,」鐵皮樵夫說;「但如果你去,我當然同你一起去。」

passages.original: Therefore it was decided to start upon their journey the next morning, and the Woodman sharpened his axe on a green grindstone and had all his joints properly oiled. The Scarecrow stuffed himself with fresh straw and Dorothy put new paint on his eyes that he might see better. The green girl, who was very kind to them, filled Dorothy’s basket with good things to eat, and fastened a little bell around Toto’s neck with a green ribbon.
passages.vernacular: 因此決定第二天早晨出發旅行,樵夫喺一塊綠色磨刀石上磨利咗斧頭,把所有關節都妥善上咗油。稻草人畀自己塞咗新稻草,桃樂絲喺佢眼睛上塗咗新顏料,讓佢睇得更清楚。對佢哋好好嘅綠衣女孩,把好食嘅嘢裝滿桃樂絲嘅籃子,用一條綠絲帶把一個小鈴繫喺托托嘅脖子上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因此決定第二天早晨出發旅行,樵夫在一塊綠色磨刀石上磨利了斧頭,把所有關節都妥善上了油。稻草人給自己塞了新稻草,桃樂絲在他眼睛上塗了新顏料,讓他看得更清楚。對他們非常好的綠衣女孩,把好吃的東西裝滿桃樂絲的籃子,用一條綠絲帶把一個小鈴繫在托托的脖子上。

passages.original: They went to bed quite early and slept soundly until daylight, when they were awakened by the crowing of a green cock that lived in the back yard of the Palace, and the cackling of a hen that had laid a green egg.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋好早就上床,一直瞓到天亮,被住喺宮殿後院嘅一隻綠公雞嘅啼聲,同一隻下咗綠蛋嘅母雞嘅咯咯聲吵醒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們很早就上床,一直睡到天亮,被住在宮殿後院的一隻綠公雞的啼聲,和一隻下了綠蛋的母雞的咯咯聲吵醒。

chapters.title: Chapter XII: The Search for the Wicked Witch 第十二章:尋找惡女巫

passages.original: The soldier with the green whiskers led them through the streets of the Emerald City until they reached the room where the Guardian of the Gates lived. This officer unlocked their spectacles to put them back in his great box, and then he politely opened the gate for our friends.
passages.vernacular: 留綠鬍鬚嘅士兵帶佢哋穿過翡翠城嘅街道,嚟到城門守衛住嘅房間。呢位官員打開佢哋嘅眼鏡,把佢哋放回佢嘅大箱子裡,然後禮貌地為我哋嘅朋友哋開咗城門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 留綠鬍鬚的士兵帶他們穿過翡翠城的街道,來到城門守衛住的房間。這位官員打開他們的眼鏡,把它們放回他的大箱子裡,然後禮貌地為我們的朋友們開了城門。

passages.original: “Which road leads to the Wicked Witch of the West?” asked Dorothy.
passages.vernacular: 「邊條路通往西方惡女巫嗰度?」桃樂絲問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哪條路通往西方惡女巫那裡?」桃樂絲問。

passages.original: “There is no road,” answered the Guardian of the Gates. “No one ever wishes to go that way.”
passages.vernacular: 「冇路,」城門守衛回答。「冇人會想走嗰個方向。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有路,」城門守衛回答。「沒有人會想走那個方向。」

passages.original: “How, then, are we to find her?” inquired the girl.
passages.vernacular: 「咁我哋點樣找到佢?」女孩問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼我們怎樣找到她?」女孩問。

passages.original: “That will be easy,” replied the man, “for when she knows you are in the country of the Winkies she will find you, and make you all her slaves.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰好容易,」嗰人回答,「因為當佢知道你哋喺溫基人嘅國家,佢就會找到你哋,把你哋都變成佢嘅奴隸。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那很容易,」那人回答,「因為當她知道你們在溫基人的國家,她就會找到你們,把你們都變成她的奴隸。」

passages.original: “Perhaps not,” said the Scarecrow, “for we mean to destroy her.”
passages.vernacular: 「或者唔會,」稻草人講,「因為我哋打算消滅佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「也許不會,」稻草人說,「因為我們打算消滅她。」

passages.original: “Oh, that is different,” said the Guardian of the Gates. “No one has ever destroyed her before, so I naturally thought she would make slaves of you, as she has of the rest. But take care; for she is wicked and fierce, and may not allow you to destroy her. Keep to the West, where the sun sets, and you cannot fail to find her.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,嗰就不同喇,」城門守衛講。「以前冇人消滅過佢,所以我自然以為佢會把你哋變成奴隸,像對其他人嗰樣。但要小心;因為佢邪惡又凶猛,可能不讓你哋消滅佢。一直往西走,太陽下山嘅方向,你哋一定會找到佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,那就不同了,」城門守衛說。「以前沒有人消滅過她,所以我自然以為她會把你們變成奴隸,像對其他人那樣。但要小心;因為她邪惡又凶猛,可能不讓你們消滅她。一直往西走,太陽下山的方向,你們一定會找到她。」

passages.original: They thanked him and bade him good-bye, and turned toward the West, walking over fields of soft grass dotted here and there with daisies and buttercups. Dorothy still wore the pretty silk dress she had put on in the palace, but now, to her surprise, she found it was no longer green, but pure white. The ribbon around Toto’s neck had also lost its green color and was as white as Dorothy’s dress.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋謝咗佢,向佢道別,轉向西方,走過柔軟嘅草地,草地上到處點綴住雛菊同毛茛。桃樂絲仍然穿住喺宮殿裡穿上嘅漂亮絲綢裙子,但而家,佢驚訝地發現佢唔再係綠色,而係純白色。托托脖子上嘅絲帶都失去咗綠色,同桃樂絲嘅裙子一樣白。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們謝了他,向他道別,轉向西方,走過柔軟的草地,草地上到處點綴著雛菊和毛茛。桃樂絲仍然穿著在宮殿裡穿上的漂亮絲綢裙子,但現在,她驚訝地發現它不再是綠色,而是純白色。托托脖子上的絲帶也失去了綠色,和桃樂絲的裙子一樣白。

passages.original: The Emerald City was soon left far behind. As they advanced the ground became rougher and hillier, for there were no farms nor houses in this country of the West, and the ground was untilled.
passages.vernacular: 翡翠城好快被遠遠拋喺後面。佢哋往前走,地面變得越嚟越崎嶇多山,因為喺西方呢個國家冇農場都冇房子,土地冇耕種。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 翡翠城很快被遠遠拋在後面。他們往前走,地面變得越來越崎嶇多山,因為在西方這個國家沒有農場也沒有房子,土地沒有耕種。

passages.original: In the afternoon the sun shone hot in their faces, for there were no trees to offer them shade; so that before night Dorothy and Toto and the Lion were tired, and lay down upon the grass and fell asleep, with the Woodman and the Scarecrow keeping watch.
passages.vernacular: 下午,太陽熱辣辣地照喺佢哋臉上,因為冇樹木可以遮蔭;所以仲冇到晚上,桃樂絲、托托同獅子就累喇,躺喺草地上瞓住喇,樵夫同稻草人守夜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下午,太陽熱辣辣地照在他們臉上,因為沒有樹木可以遮蔭;所以還沒到晚上,桃樂絲、托托和獅子就累了,躺在草地上睡著了,樵夫和稻草人守夜。

passages.original: Now the Wicked Witch of the West had but one eye, yet that was as powerful as a telescope, and could see everywhere. So, as she sat in the door of her castle, she happened to look around and saw Dorothy lying asleep, with her friends all about her. They were a long distance off, but the Wicked Witch was angry to find them in her country; so she blew upon a silver whistle that hung around her neck.
passages.vernacular: 而家西方惡女巫只有一隻眼睛,但嗰隻眼睛像望遠鏡一樣強大,乜嘢地方都睇得見。所以,佢坐喺城堡門口時,碰巧環顧四周,睇到桃樂絲躺住瞓覺,朋友哋都喺佢周圍。佢哋離得好遠,但惡女巫發現佢哋喺自己嘅國家,好生氣;於是佢吹響掛喺脖子上嘅銀哨子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在西方惡女巫只有一隻眼睛,但那隻眼睛像望遠鏡一樣強大,什麼地方都看得見。所以,她坐在城堡門口時,碰巧環顧四周,看到桃樂絲躺著睡覺,朋友們都在她周圍。他們離得很遠,但惡女巫發現他們在自己的國家,很生氣;於是她吹響掛在脖子上的銀哨子。

passages.original: At once there came running to her from all directions a pack of great wolves. They had long legs and fierce eyes and sharp teeth.
passages.vernacular: 即刻一群大狼從四面八方跑到佢嗰度。牠哋有長腿、凶惡嘅眼睛同鋒利嘅牙齒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬上一群大狼從四面八方跑到她那裡。牠們有長腿、凶惡的眼睛和鋒利的牙齒。

passages.original: “Go to those people,” said the Witch, “and tear them to pieces.”
passages.vernacular: 「去嗰啲人嗰度,」女巫講,「把佢哋撕成碎片。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「去那些人那裡,」女巫說,「把他們撕成碎片。」

passages.original: “Are you not going to make them your slaves?” asked the leader of the wolves.
passages.vernacular: 「你不打算把佢哋變成你嘅奴隸嗎?」狼群嘅首領問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你不打算把他們變成你的奴隸嗎?」狼群的首領問。

passages.original: “No,” she answered, “one is of tin, and one of straw; one is a girl and another a Lion. None of them is fit to work, so you may tear them into small pieces.”
passages.vernacular: 「不,」佢回答,「一個係錫做嘅,一個係稻草做嘅;一個係女孩,另一個係獅子。冇一個適合做工,所以你哋可以把佢哋撕成小塊。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,」她回答,「一個是錫做的,一個是稻草做的;一個是女孩,另一個是獅子。沒有一個適合做工,所以你們可以把他們撕成小塊。」

passages.original: “Very well,” said the wolf, and he dashed away at full speed, followed by the others.
passages.vernacular: 「好好,」狼講,全速衝出去,其他狼跟喺後面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很好,」狼說,全速衝出去,其他狼跟在後面。

passages.original: It was lucky the Scarecrow and the Woodman were wide awake and heard the wolves coming.
passages.vernacular: 幸運嘅係稻草人同樵夫完全清醒,聽到咗狼嚟嘅聲音。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幸運的是稻草人和樵夫完全清醒,聽到了狼來的聲音。

passages.original: “This is my fight,” said the Woodman, “so get behind me and I will meet them as they come.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係我嘅戰鬥,」樵夫講,「所以站到我後面,牠哋嚟一隻我迎一隻。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是我的戰鬥,」樵夫說,「所以站到我後面,牠們來一隻我迎一隻。」

passages.original: He seized his axe, which he had made very sharp, and as the leader of the wolves came on the Tin Woodman swung his arm and chopped the wolf’s head from its body, so that it immediately died. As soon as he could raise his axe another wolf came up, and he also fell under the sharp edge of the Tin Woodman’s weapon. There were forty wolves, and forty times a wolf was killed, so that at last they all lay dead in a heap before the Woodman.
passages.vernacular: 佢抓起磨得好鋒利嘅斧頭,狼群首領衝嚟時,鐵皮樵夫揮動手臂,把狼嘅頭從身體上砍下,狼即刻死喇。佢一舉起斧頭,另一隻狼又衝上嚟,都倒喺鐵皮樵夫武器嘅鋒刃下。一共有四十隻狼,殺咗四十次,最後牠哋全都死喺樵夫面前,堆成一堆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他抓起磨得很鋒利的斧頭,狼群首領衝來時,鐵皮樵夫揮動手臂,把狼的頭從身體上砍下,狼立刻死了。他一舉起斧頭,另一隻狼又衝上來,也倒在鐵皮樵夫武器的鋒刃下。一共有四十隻狼,殺了四十次,最後牠們全都死在樵夫面前,堆成一堆。

passages.original: Then he put down his axe and sat beside the Scarecrow, who said, “It was a good fight, friend.”
passages.vernacular: 然後佢放下斧頭,坐喺稻草人旁邊,稻草人講:「呢個係場好仗,朋友。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他放下斧頭,坐在稻草人旁邊,稻草人說:「這是場好仗,朋友。」

passages.original: They waited until Dorothy awoke the next morning. The little girl was quite frightened when she saw the great pile of shaggy wolves, but the Tin Woodman told her all. She thanked him for saving them and sat down to breakfast, after which they started again upon their journey.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋等到第二天早晨桃樂絲醒嚟。小女孩睇到嗰一大堆毛茸茸嘅狼時嚇壞喇,但鐵皮樵夫把一切告訴咗佢。佢謝謝佢救咗大家,坐下食早餐,之後佢哋又上路喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們等到第二天早晨桃樂絲醒來。小女孩看到那一大堆毛茸茸的狼時嚇壞了,但鐵皮樵夫把一切告訴了她。她謝謝他救了大家,坐下吃早餐,之後他們又上路了。

passages.original: Now this same morning the Wicked Witch came to the door of her castle and looked out with her one eye that could see far off. She saw all her wolves lying dead, and the strangers still traveling through her country. This made her angrier than before, and she blew her silver whistle twice.
passages.vernacular: 就喺呢同一個早晨,惡女巫嚟到城堡門口,用佢嗰隻能睇得好遠嘅眼睛向外睇。佢睇到所有嘅狼都死喺嗰度,陌生人仲喺佢嘅國家裡旅行。呢使佢比之前更生氣,佢吹咗兩下銀哨子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在這同一個早晨,惡女巫來到城堡門口,用她那隻能看得很遠的眼睛向外看。她看到所有的狼都死在那裡,陌生人還在她的國家裡旅行。這使她比之前更生氣,她吹了兩下銀哨子。

passages.original: Straightway a great flock of wild crows came flying toward her, enough to darken the sky.
passages.vernacular: 即刻一大群野烏鴉向佢飛嚟,多得遮暗咗天空。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬上一大群野烏鴉向她飛來,多得遮暗了天空。

passages.original: And the Wicked Witch said to the King Crow, “Fly at once to the strangers; peck out their eyes and tear them to pieces.”
passages.vernacular: 惡女巫對烏鴉王講:「即刻飛去嗰啲陌生人嗰度;啄出佢哋嘅眼睛,把佢哋撕成碎片。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 惡女巫對烏鴉王說:「馬上飛去那些陌生人那裡;啄出他們的眼睛,把他們撕成碎片。」

passages.original: The wild crows flew in one great flock toward Dorothy and her companions. When the little girl saw them coming she was afraid.
passages.vernacular: 野烏鴉成一大群飛向桃樂絲同佢嘅同伴。小女孩睇到牠哋嚟,好害怕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 野烏鴉成一大群飛向桃樂絲和她的同伴。小女孩看到牠們來,很害怕。

passages.original: But the Scarecrow said, “This is my battle, so lie down beside me and you will not be harmed.”
passages.vernacular: 但稻草人講:「呢個係我嘅戰鬥,所以躺喺我旁邊,你哋唔會受傷。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但稻草人說:「這是我的戰鬥,所以躺在我旁邊,你們不會受傷。」

passages.original: So they all lay upon the ground except the Scarecrow, and he stood up and stretched out his arms. And when the crows saw him they were frightened, as these birds always are by scarecrows, and did not dare to come any nearer. But the King Crow said:
passages.vernacular: 於是除咗稻草人以外,佢哋都躺喺地上,佢站起嚟,伸開雙臂。烏鴉睇到佢,就像呢啲鳥總是害怕稻草人一樣,被嚇到喇,唔敢再走近。但烏鴉王講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是除了稻草人以外,他們都躺在地上,他站起來,伸開雙臂。烏鴉看到他,就像這些鳥總是害怕稻草人一樣,被嚇到了,不敢再走近。但烏鴉王說:

passages.original: “It is only a stuffed man. I will peck his eyes out.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰只係個塞滿嘢嘅人。我嚟啄出佢嘅眼睛。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那只是個塞滿東西的人。我來啄出他的眼睛。」

passages.original: The King Crow flew at the Scarecrow, who caught it by the head and twisted its neck until it died. And then another crow flew at him, and the Scarecrow twisted its neck also. There were forty crows, and forty times the Scarecrow twisted a neck, until at last all were lying dead beside him. Then he called to his companions to rise, and again they went upon their journey.
passages.vernacular: 烏鴉王飛向稻草人,稻草人抓住牠嘅頭,擰牠嘅脖子,直到牠死喇。然後另一隻烏鴉飛向佢,稻草人都擰斷咗牠嘅脖子。一共有四十隻烏鴉,稻草人擰咗四十次脖子,直到最後牠哋全都死喺佢旁邊。然後佢叫同伴哋起嚟,佢哋又繼續旅程。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 烏鴉王飛向稻草人,稻草人抓住牠的頭,擰牠的脖子,直到牠死了。然後另一隻烏鴉飛向他,稻草人也擰斷了牠的脖子。一共有四十隻烏鴉,稻草人擰了四十次脖子,直到最後牠們全都死在他旁邊。然後他叫同伴們起來,他們又繼續旅程。

passages.original: When the Wicked Witch looked out again and saw all her crows lying in a heap, she got into a terrible rage, and blew three times upon her silver whistle.
passages.vernacular: 惡女巫再次向外睇,睇到佢所有嘅烏鴉堆喺一起死喇,佢大發雷霆,對住銀哨子吹咗三下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 惡女巫再次向外看,看到她所有的烏鴉堆在一起死了,她大發雷霆,對著銀哨子吹了三下。

passages.original: Forthwith there was heard a great buzzing in the air, and a swarm of black bees came flying toward her.
passages.vernacular: 即刻空中傳嚟一陣巨大嘅嗡嗡聲,一群黑蜜蜂向佢飛嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 立刻空中傳來一陣巨大的嗡嗡聲,一群黑蜜蜂向她飛來。

passages.original: “Go to the strangers and sting them to death!” commanded the Witch, and the bees turned and flew rapidly until they came to where Dorothy and her friends were walking. But the Woodman had seen them coming, and the Scarecrow had decided what to do.
passages.vernacular: 「去嗰啲陌生人嗰度,把佢哋螫死!」女巫命令,蜜蜂轉身快速飛去,一直飛到桃樂絲同佢朋友哋走路嘅地方。但樵夫已經睇到牠哋嚟喇,稻草人都決定咗點做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「去那些陌生人那裡,把他們螫死!」女巫命令,蜜蜂轉身快速飛去,一直飛到桃樂絲和她朋友們走路的地方。但樵夫已經看到牠們來了,稻草人也決定了怎麼做。

passages.original: “Take out my straw and scatter it over the little girl and the dog and the Lion,” he said to the Woodman, “and the bees cannot sting them.” This the Woodman did, and as Dorothy lay close beside the Lion and held Toto in her arms, the straw covered them entirely.
passages.vernacular: 「把我嘅稻草攞出嚟,撒喺小女孩、狗同獅子身上,」佢對樵夫講,「蜜蜂就螫唔到佢哋。」樵夫照做喇,桃樂絲緊靠獅子躺住,把托托抱喺懷裡,稻草把佢哋完全蓋住喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「把我的稻草拿出來,撒在小女孩、狗和獅子身上,」他對樵夫說,「蜜蜂就螫不到他們。」樵夫照做了,桃樂絲緊靠獅子躺著,把托托抱在懷裡,稻草把他們完全蓋住了。

passages.original: The bees came and found no one but the Woodman to sting, so they flew at him and broke off all their stings against the tin, without hurting the Woodman at all. And as bees cannot live when their stings are broken that was the end of the black bees, and they lay scattered thick about the Woodman, like little heaps of fine coal.
passages.vernacular: 蜜蜂嚟喇,除咗樵夫冇別人可螫,於是飛向佢,所有嘅刺都喺錫上折斷喇,卻完全冇傷到樵夫。而蜜蜂刺斷咗就活不喇,呢個就係黑蜜蜂嘅下場,牠哋厚厚地散落喺樵夫周圍,像一小堆一小堆嘅細炭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蜜蜂來了,除了樵夫沒有別人可螫,於是飛向他,所有的刺都在錫上折斷了,卻完全沒傷到樵夫。而蜜蜂刺斷了就活不了,這就是黑蜜蜂的下場,牠們厚厚地散落在樵夫周圍,像一小堆一小堆的細炭。

passages.original: Then Dorothy and the Lion got up, and the girl helped the Tin Woodman put the straw back into the Scarecrow again, until he was as good as ever. So they started upon their journey once more.
passages.vernacular: 然後桃樂絲同獅子起嚟,女孩幫鐵皮樵夫把稻草重新塞回稻草人身上,直到佢又完好如初。於是佢哋又一次上路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後桃樂絲和獅子起來,女孩幫鐵皮樵夫把稻草重新塞回稻草人身上,直到他又完好如初。於是他們又一次上路。

passages.original: The Wicked Witch was so angry when she saw her black bees in little heaps like fine coal that she stamped her foot and tore her hair and gnashed her teeth. And then she called a dozen of her slaves, who were the Winkies, and gave them sharp spears, telling them to go to the strangers and destroy them.
passages.vernacular: 惡女巫睇到佢嘅黑蜜蜂變成一小堆一小堆像細炭似嘅,氣得跺腳、扯頭髮、咬牙切齒。然後佢叫嚟十幾個奴隸,就係溫基人,畀佢哋鋒利嘅長矛,叫佢哋去陌生人嗰度消滅佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 惡女巫看到她的黑蜜蜂變成一小堆一小堆像細炭似的,氣得跺腳、扯頭髮、咬牙切齒。然後她叫來十幾個奴隸,就是溫基人,給他們鋒利的長矛,叫他們去陌生人那裡消滅他們。

passages.original: The Winkies were not a brave people, but they had to do as they were told. So they marched away until they came near to Dorothy. Then the Lion gave a great roar and sprang towards them, and the poor Winkies were so frightened that they ran back as fast as they could.
passages.vernacular: 溫基人唔係勇敢嘅民族,但佢哋必須照吩咐去做。於是佢哋前進,直到走近桃樂絲。然後獅子大吼一聲,撲向佢哋,可憐嘅溫基人嚇壞喇,拼命地跑回去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 溫基人不是勇敢的民族,但他們必須照吩咐去做。於是他們前進,直到走近桃樂絲。然後獅子大吼一聲,撲向他們,可憐的溫基人嚇壞了,拼命地跑回去。

passages.original: When they returned to the castle the Wicked Witch beat them well with a strap, and sent them back to their work, after which she sat down to think what she should do next. She could not understand how all her plans to destroy these strangers had failed; but she was a powerful Witch, as well as a wicked one, and she soon made up her mind how to act.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋回到城堡時,惡女巫用皮帶狠狠地抽咗佢哋一頓,把佢哋送回去工作,之後佢坐下嚟想下一步該點算。佢不明白佢所有消滅呢啲陌生人嘅計畫點都失敗喇;但佢係個強大嘅女巫,都係邪惡嘅,好快就想好咗點做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們回到城堡時,惡女巫用皮帶狠狠地抽了他們一頓,把他們送回去工作,之後她坐下來想下一步該怎麼辦。她不明白她所有消滅這些陌生人的計畫怎麼都失敗了;但她是個強大的女巫,也是邪惡的,很快就想好了怎麼做。

passages.original: There was, in her cupboard, a Golden Cap, with a circle of diamonds and rubies running round it. This Golden Cap had a charm. Whoever owned it could call three times upon the Winged Monkeys, who would obey any order they were given. But no person could command these strange creatures more than three times. Twice already the Wicked Witch had used the charm of the Cap. Once was when she had made the Winkies her slaves, and set herself to rule over their country. The Winged Monkeys had helped her do this. The second time was when she had fought against the Great Oz himself, and driven him out of the land of the West. The Winged Monkeys had also helped her in doing this. Only once more could she use this Golden Cap, for which reason she did not like to do so until all her other powers were exhausted. But now that her fierce wolves and her wild crows and her stinging bees were gone, and her slaves had been scared away by the Cowardly Lion, she saw there was only one way left to destroy Dorothy and her friends.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅碗櫃裡有一頂金帽子,周圍一圈鑲住鑽石同紅寶石。呢頂金帽子有魔力。邊個擁有佢,就可以三次召喚飛猴,飛猴會服從任何命令。但冇人能對呢啲奇怪嘅生物下超過三次命令。惡女巫已經用過兩次帽子嘅魔力。一次係佢把溫基人變成奴隸,並開始統治佢哋國家嘅時候。飛猴幫佢做到咗呢件事。第二次係佢同大奧茲本人作戰,把佢趕出西方國土嘅時候。飛猴都幫佢做咗呢件事。佢只能再用一次呢頂金帽子,所以佢不鍾意咁樣做,除非佢其他所有力量都用盡喇。但而家佢凶猛嘅狼、野烏鴉同螫人嘅蜜蜂都冇喇,佢嘅奴隸又被膽小嘅獅子嚇跑喇,佢睇到只剩一個辦法可以消滅桃樂絲同佢嘅朋友哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的碗櫃裡有一頂金帽子,周圍一圈鑲著鑽石和紅寶石。這頂金帽子有魔力。誰擁有它,就可以三次召喚飛猴,飛猴會服從任何命令。但沒有人能對這些奇怪的生物下超過三次命令。惡女巫已經用過兩次帽子的魔力。一次是她把溫基人變成奴隸,並開始統治他們國家的時候。飛猴幫她做到了這件事。第二次是她同大奧茲本人作戰,把他趕出西方國土的時候。飛猴也幫她做了這件事。她只能再用一次這頂金帽子,所以她不喜歡這樣做,除非她其他所有力量都用盡了。但現在她凶猛的狼、野烏鴉和螫人的蜜蜂都沒了,她的奴隸又被膽小的獅子嚇跑了,她看到只剩一個辦法可以消滅桃樂絲和她的朋友們。

passages.original: So the Wicked Witch took the Golden Cap from her cupboard and placed it upon her head. Then she stood upon her left foot and said, slowly:
passages.vernacular: 於是惡女巫從碗櫃裡攞出金帽子,戴喺頭上。然後佢用左腳站住,慢慢地講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是惡女巫從碗櫃裡拿出金帽子,戴在頭上。然後她用左腳站著,慢慢地說:

passages.original: “Ep-pe, pep-pe, kak-ke!”
passages.vernacular: 「艾-佩,佩-佩,卡-克!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「艾-佩,佩-佩,卡-克!」

passages.original: Next she stood upon her right foot and said:
passages.vernacular: 接住佢用右腳站住,講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 接著她用右腳站著,說:

passages.original: “Hil-lo, hol-lo, hel-lo!”
passages.vernacular: 「希-羅,霍-羅,赫-羅!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「希-羅,霍-羅,赫-羅!」

passages.original: After this she stood upon both feet and cried in a loud voice:
passages.vernacular: 之後佢雙腳站住,大聲喊:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 之後她雙腳站著,大聲喊:

passages.original: “Ziz-zy, zuz-zy, zik!”
passages.vernacular: 「濟-齊,祖-祖,齊克!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「濟-齊,祖-祖,齊克!」

passages.original: Now the charm began to work. The sky was darkened, and a low rumbling sound was heard in the air. There was a rushing of many wings, a great chattering and laughing, and the sun came out of the dark sky to show the Wicked Witch surrounded by a crowd of monkeys, each with a pair of immense and powerful wings on his shoulders.
passages.vernacular: 而家魔法開始起作用喇。天空變暗,空中傳嚟低沉嘅隆隆聲。傳嚟許多翅膀嘅撲打聲,一陣大聲嘅吱喳同笑聲,太陽從黑暗嘅天空露出嚟,照出惡女巫被一群猴子包圍,每隻猴子肩上都有一對巨大有力嘅翅膀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在魔法開始起作用了。天空變暗,空中傳來低沉的隆隆聲。傳來許多翅膀的撲打聲,一陣大聲的吱喳和笑聲,太陽從黑暗的天空露出來,照出惡女巫被一群猴子包圍,每隻猴子肩上都有一對巨大有力的翅膀。

passages.original: One, much bigger than the others, seemed to be their leader. He flew close to the Witch and said, “You have called us for the third and last time. What do you command?”
passages.vernacular: 其中一隻比其他嘅大得多,似乎係牠哋嘅首領。佢飛近女巫,講:「你呢個係第三次都係最後一次召喚我哋。你有乜嘢吩咐?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其中一隻比其他的大得多,似乎是牠們的首領。他飛近女巫,說:「你這是第三次也是最後一次召喚我們。你有什麼吩咐?」

passages.original: “Go to the strangers who are within my land and destroy them all except the Lion,” said the Wicked Witch. “Bring that beast to me, for I have a mind to harness him like a horse, and make him work.”
passages.vernacular: 「去我國土內嘅陌生人嗰度,把佢哋全都消滅,除咗獅子,」惡女巫講。「把嗰頭野獸帶嚟畀我,因為我打算畀佢套上馬具,像馬一樣叫佢幹活。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「去我國土內的陌生人那裡,把他們全都消滅,除了獅子,」惡女巫說。「把那頭野獸帶來給我,因為我打算給他套上馬具,像馬一樣叫他幹活。」

passages.original: “Your commands shall be obeyed,” said the leader. Then, with a great deal of chattering and noise, the Winged Monkeys flew away to the place where Dorothy and her friends were walking.
passages.vernacular: 「遵命,」首領講。然後飛猴哋伴住大量嘅吱喳聲同喧鬧,飛向桃樂絲同佢朋友哋走路嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「遵命,」首領說。然後飛猴們伴著大量的吱喳聲和喧鬧,飛向桃樂絲和她朋友們走路的地方。

passages.original: Some of the Monkeys seized the Tin Woodman and carried him through the air until they were over a country thickly covered with sharp rocks. Here they dropped the poor Woodman, who fell a great distance to the rocks, where he lay so battered and dented that he could neither move nor groan.
passages.vernacular: 啲猴子抓住鐵皮樵夫,帶住佢喺空中飛,一直飛到一片佈滿尖利岩石嘅地方上空。喺呢度牠哋把可憐嘅樵夫扔下,佢從好高嘅地方摔到岩石上,躺喺嗰度被撞得凹凸不平,動都唔能夠動,連呻吟都唔能夠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一些猴子抓住鐵皮樵夫,帶著他在空中飛,一直飛到一片佈滿尖利岩石的地方上空。在這裡牠們把可憐的樵夫扔下,他從很高的地方摔到岩石上,躺在那裡被撞得凹凸不平,動也不能動,連呻吟都不能。

passages.original: Others of the Monkeys caught the Scarecrow, and with their long fingers pulled all of the straw out of his clothes and head. They made his hat and boots and clothes into a small bundle and threw it into the top branches of a tall tree.
passages.vernacular: 另啲猴子抓住稻草人,用長長嘅手指把佢衣服同頭裡所有嘅稻草都扯出嚟。牠哋把佢嘅帽子、靴子同衣服捲成一個小包,扔到一棵高樹嘅最高枝上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 另一些猴子抓住稻草人,用長長的手指把他衣服和頭裡所有的稻草都扯出來。牠們把他的帽子、靴子和衣服捲成一個小包,扔到一棵高樹的最高枝上。

passages.original: The remaining Monkeys threw pieces of stout rope around the Lion and wound many coils about his body and head and legs, until he was unable to bite or scratch or struggle in any way. Then they lifted him up and flew away with him to the Witch’s castle, where he was placed in a small yard with a high iron fence around it, so that he could not escape.
passages.vernacular: 其餘嘅猴子把粗繩子扔到獅子身上,喺佢嘅身體、頭同腿上纏咗許多圈,直到佢唔能夠咬、唔能夠抓、唔能夠掙扎。然後牠哋把佢抬起嚟,帶住佢飛到女巫嘅城堡,喺嗰度把佢放喺一個小院子裡,周圍有高高嘅鐵柵欄,使佢唔能夠逃走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其餘的猴子把粗繩子扔到獅子身上,在他的身體、頭和腿上纏了許多圈,直到他不能咬、不能抓、不能掙扎。然後牠們把他抬起來,帶著他飛到女巫的城堡,在那裡把他放在一個小院子裡,周圍有高高的鐵柵欄,使他不能逃走。

passages.original: But Dorothy they did not harm at all. She stood, with Toto in her arms, watching the sad fate of her comrades and thinking it would soon be her turn. The leader of the Winged Monkeys flew up to her, his long, hairy arms stretched out and his ugly face grinning terribly; but he saw the mark of the Good Witch’s kiss upon her forehead and stopped short, motioning the others not to touch her.
passages.vernacular: 但桃樂絲牠哋啲都冇傷害。佢抱住托托站喺嗰度,睇住同伴哋嘅悲慘命運,想住不久就輪到佢喇。飛猴首領飛到佢面前,長長嘅毛手臂伸出嚟,醜陋嘅臉可怕地咧嘴笑住;但佢睇到佢額頭上好女巫嘅吻嘅印記,猛然停住,向其他猴子示意唔好碰佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但桃樂絲牠們一點也沒傷害。她抱著托托站在那裡,看著同伴們的悲慘命運,想著不久就輪到她了。飛猴首領飛到她面前,長長的毛手臂伸出來,醜陋的臉可怕地咧嘴笑著;但他看到她額頭上好女巫的吻的印記,猛然停住,向其他猴子示意不要碰她。

passages.original: “We dare not harm this little girl,” he said to them, “for she is protected by the Power of Good, and that is greater than the Power of Evil. All we can do is to carry her to the castle of the Wicked Witch and leave her there.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋唔敢傷害呢個小女孩,」佢對牠哋講,「因為佢受善嘅力量保護,而善嘅力量比惡嘅力量更強大。我哋只能把佢帶到惡女巫嘅城堡,把佢留喺嗰度。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們不敢傷害這個小女孩,」他對牠們說,「因為她受善的力量保護,而善的力量比惡的力量更強大。我們只能把她帶到惡女巫的城堡,把她留在那裡。」

passages.original: So, carefully and gently, they lifted Dorothy in their arms and carried her swiftly through the air until they came to the castle, where they set her down upon the front doorstep. Then the leader said to the Witch:
passages.vernacular: 於是,牠哋小心而溫柔地用手臂抱起桃樂絲,迅速地帶住佢喺空中飛,直到來到城堡,把佢放喺前門嘅台階上。然後首領對女巫講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是,牠們小心而溫柔地用手臂抱起桃樂絲,迅速地帶著她在空中飛,直到來到城堡,把她放在前門的台階上。然後首領對女巫說:

passages.original: “We have obeyed you as far as we were able. The Tin Woodman and the Scarecrow are destroyed, and the Lion is tied up in your yard. The little girl we dare not harm, nor the dog she carries in her arms. Your power over our band is now ended, and you will never see us again.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋已盡力服從咗你。鐵皮樵夫同稻草人被消滅喇,獅子綁喺你嘅院子裡。嗰個小女孩同佢抱喺懷裡嘅狗,我哋唔敢傷害。你對我哋呢一群嘅力量而家結束喇,你再都唔會見到我哋。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們已盡力服從了你。鐵皮樵夫和稻草人被消滅了,獅子綁在你的院子裡。那個小女孩和她抱在懷裡的狗,我們不敢傷害。你對我們這一群的力量現在結束了,你再也不會見到我們。」

passages.original: Then all the Winged Monkeys, with much laughing and chattering and noise, flew into the air and were soon out of sight.
passages.vernacular: 然後所有飛猴伴住大笑、吱喳同喧鬧飛到空中,好快就睇唔見喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後所有飛猴伴著大笑、吱喳和喧鬧飛到空中,很快就看不見了。

passages.original: The Wicked Witch was both surprised and worried when she saw the mark on Dorothy’s forehead, for she knew well that neither the Winged Monkeys nor she, herself, dare hurt the girl in any way. She looked down at Dorothy’s feet, and seeing the Silver Shoes, began to tremble with fear, for she knew what a powerful charm belonged to them. At first the Witch was tempted to run away from Dorothy; but she happened to look into the child’s eyes and saw how simple the soul behind them was, and that the little girl did not know of the wonderful power the Silver Shoes gave her. So the Wicked Witch laughed to herself, and thought, “I can still make her my slave, for she does not know how to use her power.” Then she said to Dorothy, harshly and severely:
passages.vernacular: 惡女巫睇到桃樂絲額頭上嘅印記,又驚訝又擔心,因為佢好清楚,飛猴同佢自己都唔敢以任何方式傷害呢個女孩。佢低頭睇桃樂絲嘅腳,睇到銀鞋,害怕得發抖,因為佢知道佢哋有幾咁強大嘅魔力。起初女巫想從桃樂絲身邊逃走;但佢碰巧睇進細路嘅眼睛,睇到眼睛後面嘅靈魂幾咁單純,而且小女孩唔知道銀鞋畀佢嘅奇妙力量。於是惡女巫自己笑喇,心想:「我定係可以把佢變成我嘅奴隸,因為佢唔知道點用佢嘅力量。」然後佢嚴厲刻薄地對桃樂絲講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 惡女巫看到桃樂絲額頭上的印記,又驚訝又擔心,因為她很清楚,飛猴和她自己都不敢以任何方式傷害這個女孩。她低頭看桃樂絲的腳,看到銀鞋,害怕得發抖,因為她知道它們有多麼強大的魔力。起初女巫想從桃樂絲身邊逃走;但她碰巧看進孩子的眼睛,看到眼睛後面的靈魂多麼單純,而且小女孩不知道銀鞋給她的奇妙力量。於是惡女巫自己笑了,心想:「我還是可以把她變成我的奴隸,因為她不知道怎麼用她的力量。」然後她嚴厲刻薄地對桃樂絲說:

passages.original: “Come with me; and see that you mind everything I tell you, for if you do not I will make an end of you, as I did of the Tin Woodman and the Scarecrow.”
passages.vernacular: 「跟我嚟;而且要留心我吩咐嘅每件事,不然我會結果你,像我結果鐵皮樵夫同稻草人嗰樣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「跟我來;而且要留心我吩咐的每件事,不然我會結果你,像我結果鐵皮樵夫和稻草人那樣。」

passages.original: Dorothy followed her through many of the beautiful rooms in her castle until they came to the kitchen, where the Witch bade her clean the pots and kettles and sweep the floor and keep the fire fed with wood.
passages.vernacular: 桃樂絲跟住佢穿過城堡裡許多漂亮嘅房間,嚟到廚房,女巫叫佢洗鍋碗瓢盆、掃地,仲要不斷添柴生火。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 桃樂絲跟著她穿過城堡裡許多漂亮的房間,來到廚房,女巫叫她洗鍋碗瓢盆、掃地,還要不斷添柴生火。

passages.original: Dorothy went to work meekly, with her mind made up to work as hard as she could; for she was glad the Wicked Witch had decided not to kill her.
passages.vernacular: 桃樂絲溫順地開始工作,決心盡力努力幹活;因為佢好高興惡女巫決定不殺佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 桃樂絲溫順地開始工作,決心盡力努力幹活;因為她很高興惡女巫決定不殺她。

passages.original: With Dorothy hard at work, the Witch thought she would go into the courtyard and harness the Cowardly Lion like a horse; it would amuse her, she was sure, to make him draw her chariot whenever she wished to go to drive. But as she opened the gate the Lion gave a loud roar and bounded at her so fiercely that the Witch was afraid, and ran out and shut the gate again.
passages.vernacular: 桃樂絲辛苦工作時,女巫想佢要去院子裡畀膽小嘅獅子套上馬具,像馬一樣;佢肯定,每當佢想出去駕車時叫佢拉佢嘅馬車,會好好玩。但佢打開門時,獅子大吼一聲,咁凶猛地向佢撲去,女巫害怕喇,跑出嚟又把門關上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 桃樂絲辛苦工作時,女巫想她要去院子裡給膽小的獅子套上馬具,像馬一樣;她肯定,每當她想出去駕車時叫他拉她的馬車,會很好玩。但她打開門時,獅子大吼一聲,那麼凶猛地向她撲去,女巫害怕了,跑出來又把門關上。

passages.original: “If I cannot harness you,” said the Witch to the Lion, speaking through the bars of the gate, “I can starve you. You shall have nothing to eat until you do as I wish.”
passages.vernacular: 「如果我唔能夠畀你套上馬具,」女巫隔住門嘅欄杆對獅子講,「我可以餓死你。你不照我嘅意思做,乜嘢食嘅都別想有。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果我不能給你套上馬具,」女巫隔著門的欄杆對獅子說,「我可以餓死你。你不照我的意思做,什麼吃的也別想有。」

passages.original: So after that she took no food to the imprisoned Lion; but every day she came to the gate at noon and asked, “Are you ready to be harnessed like a horse?”
passages.vernacular: 於是此後佢不畀被關住嘅獅子送任何食物;但每天中午佢都嚟到門口問:「你準備好像馬一樣套上馬具咗嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是此後她不給被關著的獅子送任何食物;但每天中午她都來到門口問:「你準備好像馬一樣套上馬具了嗎?」

passages.original: And the Lion would answer, “No. If you come in this yard, I will bite you.”
passages.vernacular: 獅子會回答:「不。如果你進呢個院子,我就咬你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 獅子會回答:「不。如果你進這個院子,我就咬你。」

passages.original: The reason the Lion did not have to do as the Witch wished was that every night, while the woman was asleep, Dorothy carried him food from the cupboard. After he had eaten he would lie down on his bed of straw, and Dorothy would lie beside him and put her head on his soft, shaggy mane, while they talked of their troubles and tried to plan some way to escape. But they could find no way to get out of the castle, for it was constantly guarded by the yellow Winkies, who were the slaves of the Wicked Witch and too afraid of her not to do as she told them.
passages.vernacular: 獅子唔使照女巫嘅意思做嘅原因係,每天晚上,女巫瞓住時,桃樂絲從碗櫃裡攞食物畀佢。佢食完後,會躺喺稻草床上,桃樂絲躺喺佢旁邊,頭枕住佢柔軟毛茸茸嘅鬃毛,佢哋談論自己嘅煩惱,試圖計畫某個逃走嘅辦法。但佢哋找唔到出城堡嘅辦法,因為城堡一直被黃色嘅溫基人睇守住,佢哋係惡女巫嘅奴隸,太怕佢喇,唔敢不照佢嘅吩咐做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 獅子不必照女巫的意思做的原因是,每天晚上,女巫睡著時,桃樂絲從碗櫃裡拿食物給他。他吃完後,會躺在稻草床上,桃樂絲躺在他旁邊,頭枕著他柔軟毛茸茸的鬃毛,他們談論自己的煩惱,試圖計畫某個逃走的辦法。但他們找不到出城堡的辦法,因為城堡一直被黃色的溫基人看守著,他們是惡女巫的奴隸,太怕她了,不敢不照她的吩咐做。

passages.original: The girl had to work hard during the day, and often the Witch threatened to beat her with the same old umbrella she always carried in her hand. But, in truth, she did not dare to strike Dorothy, because of the mark upon her forehead. The child did not know this, and was full of fear for herself and Toto. Once the Witch struck Toto a blow with her umbrella and the brave little dog flew at her and bit her leg in return. The Witch did not bleed where she was bitten, for she was so wicked that the blood in her had dried up many years before.
passages.vernacular: 女孩白天必須辛苦工作,女巫常常威脅要用佢手裡總是攞住嘅嗰把舊雨傘打佢。但實際上,佢唔敢打桃樂絲,因為佢額頭上嘅印記。細路唔知道呢個,為自己同托托充滿恐懼。有一次女巫用雨傘打咗托托一下,勇敢嘅小狗撲向佢,反過嚟咬咗佢嘅腿。女巫被咬嘅地方冇流血,因為佢太邪惡,體內嘅血喺多年前就乾涸喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 女孩白天必須辛苦工作,女巫常常威脅要用她手裡總是拿著的那把舊雨傘打她。但實際上,她不敢打桃樂絲,因為她額頭上的印記。孩子不知道這個,為自己和托托充滿恐懼。有一次女巫用雨傘打了托托一下,勇敢的小狗撲向她,反過來咬了她的腿。女巫被咬的地方沒有流血,因為她太邪惡,體內的血在多年前就乾涸了。

passages.original: Dorothy’s life became very sad as she grew to understand that it would be harder than ever to get back to Kansas and Aunt Em again. Sometimes she would cry bitterly for hours, with Toto sitting at her feet and looking into her face, whining dismally to show how sorry he was for his little mistress. Toto did not really care whether he was in Kansas or the Land of Oz so long as Dorothy was with him; but he knew the little girl was unhappy, and that made him unhappy too.
passages.vernacular: 桃樂絲嘅生活變得好悲慘,因為佢漸漸明白,要回堪薩斯同艾姆嬸嬸身邊,比以往更難喇。有時佢會痛哭幾個小時,托托坐喺佢腳邊,望住佢嘅臉,悲哀地嗚咽,表示佢為佢嘅小主人幾咁難過。托托其實不在乎自己喺堪薩斯定係奧茲國,只要桃樂絲跟佢喺一起;但佢知道小女孩不快樂,嗰都使佢不快樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 桃樂絲的生活變得很悲慘,因為她漸漸明白,要回堪薩斯和艾姆嬸嬸身邊,比以往更難了。有時她會痛哭幾個小時,托托坐在她腳邊,望著她的臉,悲哀地嗚咽,表示他為他的小主人多麼難過。托托其實不在乎自己在堪薩斯還是奧茲國,只要桃樂絲跟他在一起;但他知道小女孩不快樂,那也使他不快樂。

passages.original: Now the Wicked Witch had a great longing to have for her own the Silver Shoes which the girl always wore. Her bees and her crows and her wolves were lying in heaps and drying up, and she had used up all the power of the Golden Cap; but if she could only get hold of the Silver Shoes, they would give her more power than all the other things she had lost. She watched Dorothy carefully, to see if she ever took off her shoes, thinking she might steal them. But the child was so proud of her pretty shoes that she never took them off except at night and when she took her bath.
