passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我告訴你我的想法,」小個子說。「你知道,我來這個國家是乘氣球來的。你也是從空中來的,被龍捲風帶來。所以我相信穿越沙漠的最好方法就是通過空中。現在,製造龍捲風完全超出我的能力;但我一直在考慮這件事,我相信我可以做一個氣球。」

passages.original: “How?” asked Dorothy.
passages.vernacular: 「點做?」桃樂絲問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「怎麼做?」桃樂絲問。

passages.original: “A balloon,” said Oz, “is made of silk, which is coated with glue to keep the gas in it. I have plenty of silk in the Palace, so it will be no trouble to make the balloon. But in all this country there is no gas to fill the balloon with, to make it float.”
passages.vernacular: 「氣球,」奧茲講,「係用絲綢做嘅,上面塗咗膠,防止氣體漏出。我宮殿裡有好多絲綢,所以做氣球不成問題。但整個國家都冇氣體可以灌進氣球,使佢浮起嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「氣球,」奧茲說,「是用絲綢做的,上面塗了膠,防止氣體漏出。我宮殿裡有很多絲綢,所以做氣球不成問題。但整個國家都沒有氣體可以灌進氣球,使它浮起來。」

passages.original: “If it won’t float,” remarked Dorothy, “it will be of no use to us.”
passages.vernacular: 「如果佢浮不起嚟,」桃樂絲講,「對我哋就冇用。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果它浮不起來,」桃樂絲說,「對我們就沒用。」

passages.original: “True,” answered Oz. “But there is another way to make it float, which is to fill it with hot air. Hot air isn’t as good as gas, for if the air should get cold the balloon would come down in the desert, and we should be lost.”
passages.vernacular: 「冇錯,」奧茲回答。「但仲有另一個辦法使佢浮起嚟,就係灌進熱空氣。熱空氣不如氣體好,因為如果空氣變冷,氣球就會掉喺沙漠裡,我哋就完喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒錯,」奧茲回答。「但還有另一個辦法使它浮起來,就是灌進熱空氣。熱空氣不如氣體好,因為如果空氣變冷,氣球就會掉在沙漠裡,我們就完了。」

passages.original: “We!” exclaimed the girl. “Are you going with me?”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋!」女孩喊道。「你要同我一起去嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們!」女孩喊道。「你要同我一起去嗎?」

passages.original: “Yes, of course,” replied Oz. “I am tired of being such a humbug. If I should go out of this Palace my people would soon discover I am not a Wizard, and then they would be vexed with me for having deceived them. So I have to stay shut up in these rooms all day, and it gets tiresome. I’d much rather go back to Kansas with you and be in a circus again.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,當然,」奧茲回答。「我已經厭倦咗做咁樣一個騙子。如果我離開呢座宮殿,我嘅子民好快會發現我唔係巫師,然後佢哋會因為我欺騙咗佢哋而生我嘅氣。所以我整天必須關喺呢啲房間裡,變得好厭倦。我寧願同你回堪薩斯,再到馬戲團工作。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,當然,」奧茲回答。「我已經厭倦了做這樣一個騙子。如果我離開這座宮殿,我的子民很快會發現我不是巫師,然後他們會因為我欺騙了他們而生我的氣。所以我整天必須關在這些房間裡,變得很厭倦。我寧願同你回堪薩斯,再到馬戲團工作。」

passages.original: “I shall be glad to have your company,” said Dorothy.
passages.vernacular: 「我好高興有你同行,」桃樂絲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我很高興有你同行,」桃樂絲說。

passages.original: “Thank you,” he answered. “Now, if you will help me sew the silk together, we will begin to work on our balloon.”
passages.vernacular: 「謝謝,」佢回答。「而家,如果你幫我把絲綢縫喺一起,我哋就開始做我哋嘅氣球。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「謝謝,」他回答。「現在,如果你幫我把絲綢縫在一起,我們就開始做我們的氣球。」

passages.original: So Dorothy took a needle and thread, and as fast as Oz cut the strips of silk into proper shape the girl sewed them neatly together. First there was a strip of light green silk, then a strip of dark green and then a strip of emerald green; for Oz had a fancy to make the balloon in different shades of the color about them. It took three days to sew all the strips together, but when it was finished they had a big bag of green silk more than twenty feet long.
passages.vernacular: 於是桃樂絲攞起針線,奧茲把絲綢剪成合適形狀嘅條子,女孩就快速地把佢哋整齊地縫喺一起。首先係一條淺綠色絲綢,然後係一條深綠色,然後係一條翡翠綠;因為奧茲想要用佢哋周圍呢種顏色嘅不同深淺嚟做氣球。把所有嘅條子縫喺一起花咗三天,但完成時,佢哋有咗一個二十多呎長嘅綠絲綢大袋子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是桃樂絲拿起針線,奧茲把絲綢剪成合適形狀的條子,女孩就快速地把它們整齊地縫在一起。首先是一條淺綠色絲綢,然後是一條深綠色,然後是一條翡翠綠;因為奧茲想要用他們周圍這種顏色的不同深淺來做氣球。把所有的條子縫在一起花了三天,但完成時,他們有了一個二十多呎長的綠絲綢大袋子。

passages.original: Then Oz painted it on the inside with a coat of thin glue, to make it airtight, after which he announced that the balloon was ready.
passages.vernacular: 然後奧茲喺佢裡面塗咗一層薄膠,使佢不漏氣,之後佢宣布氣球準備好喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後奧茲在它裡面塗了一層薄膠,使它不漏氣,之後他宣布氣球準備好了。

passages.original: “But we must have a basket to ride in,” he said. So he sent the soldier with the green whiskers for a big clothes basket, which he fastened with many ropes to the bottom of the balloon.
passages.vernacular: 「但我哋必須有個籃子可以坐,」佢講。於是佢派留綠鬍鬚嘅士兵去攞一個大衣籃,用許多繩子把佢繫喺氣球底部。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但我們必須有個籃子可以坐,」他說。於是他派留綠鬍鬚的士兵去拿一個大衣籃,用許多繩子把它繫在氣球底部。

passages.original: When it was all ready, Oz sent word to his people that he was going to make a visit to a great brother Wizard who lived in the clouds. The news spread rapidly throughout the city and everyone came to see the wonderful sight.
passages.vernacular: 一切準備好後,奧茲傳話畀佢嘅子民,講佢要去拜訪住喺雲裡嘅一位偉大嘅巫師兄弟。消息迅速傳遍全城,每個人都嚟睇呢奇妙嘅景象。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一切準備好後,奧茲傳話給他的子民,說他要去拜訪住在雲裡的一位偉大的巫師兄弟。消息迅速傳遍全城,每個人都來看這奇妙的景象。

passages.original: Oz ordered the balloon carried out in front of the Palace, and the people gazed upon it with much curiosity. The Tin Woodman had chopped a big pile of wood, and now he made a fire of it, and Oz held the bottom of the balloon over the fire so that the hot air that arose from it would be caught in the silken bag. Gradually the balloon swelled out and rose into the air, until finally the basket just touched the ground.
passages.vernacular: 奧茲下令把氣球抬到宮殿前面,人哋好奇地凝視住佢。鐵皮樵夫砍咗一大堆柴,而家佢用佢生咗一堆火,奧茲把氣球底部攞喺火上,使上升嘅熱空氣被收進絲袋裡。氣球漸漸膨脹起嚟,升到空中,最後籃子剛好貼住地面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 奧茲下令把氣球抬到宮殿前面,人們好奇地凝視著它。鐵皮樵夫砍了一大堆柴,現在他用它生了一堆火,奧茲把氣球底部拿在火上,使上升的熱空氣被收進絲袋裡。氣球漸漸膨脹起來,升到空中,最後籃子剛好貼著地面。

passages.original: Then Oz got into the basket and said to all the people in a loud voice:
passages.vernacular: 然後奧茲走進籃子,大聲對所有人講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後奧茲走進籃子,大聲對所有人說:

passages.original: “I am now going away to make a visit. While I am gone the Scarecrow will rule over you. I command you to obey him as you would me.”
passages.vernacular: 「我而家要去拜訪喇。我不喺時稻草人將統治你哋。我命令你哋服從佢,就像服從我一樣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我現在要去拜訪了。我不在時稻草人將統治你們。我命令你們服從他,就像服從我一樣。」

passages.original: The balloon was by this time tugging hard at the rope that held it to the ground, for the air within it was hot, and this made it so much lighter in weight than the air without that it pulled hard to rise into the sky.
passages.vernacular: 呢陣氣球喺使勁拉住把佢繫喺地上嘅繩子,因為裡面嘅空氣係熱嘅,呢使佢比外面嘅空氣輕得多,所以用力要升向天空。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時氣球在使勁拉著把它繫在地上的繩子,因為裡面的空氣是熱的,這使它比外面的空氣輕得多,所以用力要升向天空。

passages.original: “Come, Dorothy!” cried the Wizard. “Hurry up, or the balloon will fly away.”
passages.vernacular: 「嚟,桃樂絲!」巫師喊道。「快點,不然氣球要飛走喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「來,桃樂絲!」巫師喊道。「快點,不然氣球要飛走了。」

passages.original: “I can’t find Toto anywhere,” replied Dorothy, who did not wish to leave her little dog behind. Toto had run into the crowd to bark at a kitten, and Dorothy at last found him. She picked him up and ran towards the balloon.
passages.vernacular: 「我到處找唔到托托,」桃樂絲回答,佢唔想把小狗丟下。托托跑進人群中,對住一隻小貓吠叫,桃樂絲終於找到咗佢。佢把佢抱起嚟,跑向氣球。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我到處找不到托托,」桃樂絲回答,她不想把小狗丟下。托托跑進人群中,對著一隻小貓吠叫,桃樂絲終於找到了他。她把他抱起來,跑向氣球。

passages.original: She was within a few steps of it, and Oz was holding out his hands to help her into the basket, when, crack! went the ropes, and the balloon rose into the air without her.
passages.vernacular: 佢離氣球只有幾步,奧茲正伸出手要幫佢進籃子,呢陣,啪嘅一聲!繩子斷喇,氣球冇佢就升到空中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她離氣球只有幾步,奧茲正伸出手要幫她進籃子,這時,啪的一聲!繩子斷了,氣球沒有她就升到空中。

passages.original: “Come back!” she screamed. “I want to go, too!”
passages.vernacular: 「回嚟!」佢尖叫。「我都要去!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「回來!」她尖叫。「我也要去!」

passages.original: “I can’t come back, my dear,” called Oz from the basket. “Good-bye!”
passages.vernacular: 「我唔能夠回嚟,親愛嘅,」奧茲喺籃子裡喊道。「再見!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不能回來,親愛的,」奧茲在籃子裡喊道。「再見!」

passages.original: “Good-bye!” shouted everyone, and all eyes were turned upward to where the Wizard was riding in the basket, rising every moment farther and farther into the sky.
passages.vernacular: 「再見!」大家喊道,所有嘅眼睛都向上望住巫師乘坐籃子嘅地方,佢每一刻都越升越遠,升向天空。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「再見!」大家喊道,所有的眼睛都向上望著巫師乘坐籃子的地方,他每一刻都越升越遠,升向天空。

passages.original: And that was the last any of them ever saw of Oz, the Wonderful Wizard, though he may have reached Omaha safely, and be there now, for all we know. But the people remembered him lovingly, and said to one another:
passages.vernacular: 呢個就係佢哋任何人最後一次睇到奧茲,呢位奇妙嘅巫師,雖然據我哋所知,佢可能已安全到達奧馬哈,而家仲喺嗰度。但人民懷住愛戴記住佢,彼此講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這就是他們任何人最後一次看到奧茲,這位奇妙的巫師,雖然據我們所知,他可能已安全到達奧馬哈,現在還在那裡。但人民懷著愛戴記著他,彼此說:

passages.original: “Oz was always our friend. When he was here he built for us this beautiful Emerald City, and now he is gone he has left the Wise Scarecrow to rule over us.”
passages.vernacular: 「奧茲一直係我哋嘅朋友。佢喺呢度時為我哋建造咗呢座美麗嘅翡翠城,而家佢走喇,留下聰明嘅稻草人統治我哋。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「奧茲一直是我們的朋友。他在這裡時為我們建造了這座美麗的翡翠城,現在他走了,留下聰明的稻草人統治我們。」

passages.original: Still, for many days they grieved over the loss of the Wonderful Wizard, and would not be comforted.
passages.vernacular: 然而,許多天嚟,佢哋為失去呢位奇妙嘅巫師而悲傷,唔肯接受安慰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而,許多天來,他們為失去這位奇妙的巫師而悲傷,不肯接受安慰。

chapters.title: Chapter XVIII: Away to the South 第十八章:前往南方

passages.original: Dorothy wept bitterly at the passing of her hope to get home to Kansas again; but when she thought it all over she was glad she had not gone up in a balloon. And she also felt sorry at losing Oz, and so did her companions.
passages.vernacular: 桃樂絲為回堪薩斯老家嘅希望破滅而痛哭;但當佢仔細想過之後,又慶幸自己冇乘氣球上去。佢都為失去奧茲而難過,佢嘅同伴哋都一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 桃樂絲為回堪薩斯老家的希望破滅而痛哭;但當她仔細想過之後,又慶幸自己沒有乘氣球上去。她也為失去奧茲而難過,她的同伴們也一樣。

passages.original: The Tin Woodman came to her and said:
passages.vernacular: 鐵皮樵夫嚟到佢面前,講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鐵皮樵夫來到她面前,說:

passages.original: “Truly I should be ungrateful if I failed to mourn for the man who gave me my lovely heart. I should like to cry a little because Oz is gone, if you will kindly wipe away my tears, so that I shall not rust.”
passages.vernacular: 「如果我不為嗰個畀咗我可愛心臟嘅人哀悼,我真係忘恩負義。我想為奧茲走咗哭一會兒,如果你肯好心替我擦掉眼淚,讓我唔會生鏽嘅話。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果我不為那個給了我可愛心臟的人哀悼,我真是忘恩負義。我想為奧茲走了哭一會兒,如果你肯好心替我擦掉眼淚,讓我不會生鏽的話。」

passages.original: “With pleasure,” she answered, and brought a towel at once. Then the Tin Woodman wept for several minutes, and she watched the tears carefully and wiped them away with the towel. When he had finished, he thanked her kindly and oiled himself thoroughly with his jeweled oil-can, to guard against mishap.
passages.vernacular: 「好樂意,」佢回答,即刻攞嚟一條毛巾。然後鐵皮樵夫哭咗幾分鐘,佢仔細地睇住眼淚,用毛巾擦去。佢哭完後,好心地謝咗佢,用佢嗰鑲寶石嘅油壺把自己徹底上咗油,以防萬一。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很樂意,」她回答,馬上拿來一條毛巾。然後鐵皮樵夫哭了幾分鐘,她仔細地看著眼淚,用毛巾擦去。他哭完後,好心地謝了她,用他那鑲寶石的油壺把自己徹底上了油,以防萬一。

passages.original: The Scarecrow was now the ruler of the Emerald City, and although he was not a Wizard the people were proud of him. “For,” they said, “there is not another city in all the world that is ruled by a stuffed man.” And, so far as they knew, they were quite right.
passages.vernacular: 稻草人而家係翡翠城嘅統治者,雖然佢唔係巫師,人民卻為佢感到自豪。「因為,」佢哋講,「全世界冇第二座城市係由一個塞滿嘢嘅人統治嘅。」而且,據佢哋所知,佢哋講得完全對。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 稻草人現在是翡翠城的統治者,雖然他不是巫師,人民卻為他感到自豪。「因為,」他們說,「全世界沒有第二座城市是由一個塞滿東西的人統治的。」而且,據他們所知,他們說得完全對。

passages.original: The morning after the balloon had gone up with Oz, the four travelers met in the Throne Room and talked matters over. The Scarecrow sat in the big throne and the others stood respectfully before him.
passages.vernacular: 氣球載住奧茲升空嘅第二天早晨,四個旅行者喺王座廳會面,商量事情。稻草人坐喺大王座上,其他人恭敬地站喺佢面前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 氣球載著奧茲升空的第二天早晨,四個旅行者在王座廳會面,商量事情。稻草人坐在大王座上,其他人恭敬地站在他面前。

passages.original: “We are not so unlucky,” said the new ruler, “for this Palace and the Emerald City belong to us, and we can do just as we please. When I remember that a short time ago I was up on a pole in a farmer’s cornfield, and that now I am the ruler of this beautiful City, I am quite satisfied with my lot.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋並不咁不幸,」新統治者講,「因為呢座宮殿同翡翠城屬於我哋,我哋可以隨心所欲。我記得不久前我仲喺農夫玉米田裡嘅一根桿子上,而而家我係呢座美麗城市嘅統治者,我對我嘅命運相當滿意。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們並不那麼不幸,」新統治者說,「因為這座宮殿和翡翠城屬於我們,我們可以隨心所欲。我記得不久前我還在農夫玉米田裡的一根桿子上,而現在我是這座美麗城市的統治者,我對我的命運相當滿意。」

passages.original: “I also,” said the Tin Woodman, “am well-pleased with my new heart; and, really, that was the only thing I wished in all the world.”
passages.vernacular: 「我都一樣,」鐵皮樵夫講,「對我嘅新心好滿意;講真嘅,嗰個係我世上唯一希望得到嘅嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我也一樣,」鐵皮樵夫說,「對我的新心很滿意;說真的,那是我世上唯一希望得到的東西。」

passages.original: “For my part, I am content in knowing I am as brave as any beast that ever lived, if not braver,” said the Lion modestly.
passages.vernacular: 「就我而言,知道自己同任何活過嘅野獸一樣勇敢,如果唔係更勇敢,我就滿足喇,」獅子謙虛地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「就我而言,知道自己同任何活過的野獸一樣勇敢,如果不是更勇敢,我就滿足了,」獅子謙虛地說。

passages.original: “If Dorothy would only be contented to live in the Emerald City,” continued the Scarecrow, “we might all be happy together.”
passages.vernacular: 「如果桃樂絲能滿足於住喺翡翠城,」稻草人繼續講,「我哋大家都可以一起快樂。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果桃樂絲能滿足於住在翡翠城,」稻草人繼續說,「我們大家都可以一起快樂。」

passages.original: “But I don’t want to live here,” cried Dorothy. “I want to go to Kansas, and live with Aunt Em and Uncle Henry.”
passages.vernacular: 「但我唔想住喺呢度,」桃樂絲喊道。「我想去堪薩斯,同艾姆嬸嬸同亨利叔叔一起生活。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但我不想住在這裡,」桃樂絲喊道。「我想去堪薩斯,同艾姆嬸嬸和亨利叔叔一起生活。」

passages.original: “Well, then, what can be done?” inquired the Woodman.
passages.vernacular: 「咁,可以點算呢?」樵夫問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼,可以怎麼辦呢?」樵夫問。

passages.original: The Scarecrow decided to think, and he thought so hard that the pins and needles began to stick out of his brains. Finally he said:
passages.vernacular: 稻草人決定思考,佢想得咁用力,以致針同別針開始從佢腦子裡戳出嚟。最後佢講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 稻草人決定思考,他想得那麼用力,以致針和別針開始從他腦子裡戳出來。最後他說:

passages.original: “Why not call the Winged Monkeys, and ask them to carry you over the desert?”
passages.vernacular: 「點解不叫飛猴,請牠哋帶你越過沙漠?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「為什麼不叫飛猴,請牠們帶你越過沙漠?」

passages.original: “I never thought of that!” said Dorothy joyfully. “It’s just the thing. I’ll go at once for the Golden Cap.”
passages.vernacular: 「我從冇想到!」桃樂絲高興地講。「就係呢個辦法。我即刻去攞金帽子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我從沒想到!」桃樂絲高興地說。「就是這個辦法。我馬上去拿金帽子。」

passages.original: When she brought it into the Throne Room she spoke the magic words, and soon the band of Winged Monkeys flew in through the open window and stood beside her.
passages.vernacular: 佢把佢攞進王座廳,講出魔咒,不久一群飛猴從敞開嘅窗子飛進嚟,站喺佢旁邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她把它拿進王座廳,說出魔咒,不久一群飛猴從敞開的窗子飛進來,站在她旁邊。

passages.original: “This is the second time you have called us,” said the Monkey King, bowing before the little girl. “What do you wish?”
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係你第二次召喚我哋,」猴王向小女孩鞠躬講。「你有乜嘢要求?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是你第二次召喚我們,」猴王向小女孩鞠躬說。「你有什麼要求?」

passages.original: “I want you to fly with me to Kansas,” said Dorothy.
passages.vernacular: 「我要你哋帶我飛去堪薩斯,」桃樂絲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我要你們帶我飛去堪薩斯,」桃樂絲說。

passages.original: But the Monkey King shook his head.
passages.vernacular: 但猴王搖咗搖頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但猴王搖了搖頭。

passages.original: “That cannot be done,” he said. “We belong to this country alone, and cannot leave it. There has never been a Winged Monkey in Kansas yet, and I suppose there never will be, for they don’t belong there. We shall be glad to serve you in any way in our power, but we cannot cross the desert. Good-bye.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰做唔到,」佢講。「我哋只屬於呢個國家,唔能夠離開。堪薩斯從來冇過飛猴,我想將來都唔會有,因為牠哋不屬於嗰度。我哋好樂意用我哋力所能及嘅任何方式為你服務,但我哋唔能夠越過沙漠。再見。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那做不到,」他說。「我們只屬於這個國家,不能離開。堪薩斯從來沒有過飛猴,我想將來也不會有,因為牠們不屬於那裡。我們很樂意用我們力所能及的任何方式為你服務,但我們不能越過沙漠。再見。」

passages.original: And with another bow, the Monkey King spread his wings and flew away through the window, followed by all his band.
passages.vernacular: 猴王又鞠咗一躬,展開翅膀飛出窗外,所有猴群跟喺後面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 猴王又鞠了一躬,展開翅膀飛出窗外,所有猴群跟在後面。

passages.original: Dorothy was ready to cry with disappointment. “I have wasted the charm of the Golden Cap to no purpose,” she said, “for the Winged Monkeys cannot help me.”
passages.vernacular: 桃樂絲失望得想哭。「我白白浪費咗金帽子嘅魔力,」佢講,「因為飛猴幫不咗我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 桃樂絲失望得想哭。「我白白浪費了金帽子的魔力,」她說,「因為飛猴幫不了我。」

passages.original: “It is certainly too bad!” said the tender-hearted Woodman.
passages.vernacular: 「真係太糟糕喇!」心地溫柔嘅樵夫講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真是太糟糕了!」心地溫柔的樵夫說。

passages.original: The Scarecrow was thinking again, and his head bulged out so horribly that Dorothy feared it would burst.
passages.vernacular: 稻草人又喺思考,佢嘅頭鼓得咁可怕,桃樂絲怕佢會爆開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 稻草人又在思考,他的頭鼓得那麼可怕,桃樂絲怕它會爆開。

passages.original: “Let us call in the soldier with the green whiskers,” he said, “and ask his advice.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋把留綠鬍鬚嘅士兵叫嚟,」佢講,「問問佢嘅意見。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們把留綠鬍鬚的士兵叫來,」他說,「問問他的意見。」

passages.original: So the soldier was summoned and entered the Throne Room timidly, for while Oz was alive he never was allowed to come farther than the door.
passages.vernacular: 於是士兵被召嚟,膽怯地走進王座廳,因為奧茲在世時,佢從來不被允許走過門口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是士兵被召來,膽怯地走進王座廳,因為奧茲在世時,他從來不被允許走過門口。

passages.original: “This little girl,” said the Scarecrow to the soldier, “wishes to cross the desert. How can she do so?”
passages.vernacular: 「呢個小女孩,」稻草人對士兵講,「想越過沙漠。佢點才能做到?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這個小女孩,」稻草人對士兵說,「想越過沙漠。她怎麼才能做到?」

passages.original: “I cannot tell,” answered the soldier, “for nobody has ever crossed the desert, unless it is Oz himself.”
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道,」士兵回答,「因為除咗奧茲本人,冇人越過沙漠。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道,」士兵回答,「因為除了奧茲本人,沒有人越過沙漠。」

passages.original: “Is there no one who can help me?” asked Dorothy earnestly.
passages.vernacular: 「冇人能幫助我嗎?」桃樂絲認真地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有人能幫助我嗎?」桃樂絲認真地問。

passages.original: “Glinda might,” he suggested.
passages.vernacular: 「格琳達或者可以,」佢建議。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「格琳達也許可以,」他建議。

passages.original: “Who is Glinda?” inquired the Scarecrow.
passages.vernacular: 「格琳達係邊個?」稻草人問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「格琳達是誰?」稻草人問。

passages.original: “The Witch of the South. She is the most powerful of all the Witches, and rules over the Quadlings. Besides, her castle stands on the edge of the desert, so she may know a way to cross it.”
passages.vernacular: 「南方嘅女巫。佢係所有女巫中最強大嘅,統治住夸德林人。而且,佢嘅城堡就喺沙漠邊上,所以佢可能知道越過沙漠嘅方法。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「南方的女巫。她是所有女巫中最強大的,統治著夸德林人。而且,她的城堡就在沙漠邊上,所以她可能知道越過沙漠的方法。」

passages.original: “Glinda is a Good Witch, isn’t she?” asked the child.
passages.vernacular: 「格琳達係個好女巫,係嗎?」細路問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「格琳達是個好女巫,是嗎?」孩子問。

passages.original: “The Quadlings think she is good,” said the soldier, “and she is kind to everyone. I have heard that Glinda is a beautiful woman, who knows how to keep young in spite of the many years she has lived.”
passages.vernacular: 「夸德林人認為佢係好嘅,」士兵講,「佢對每個人都好。我聽講格琳達係個美麗嘅女人,雖然活咗好多年,卻懂得點樣保持年輕。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「夸德林人認為她是好的,」士兵說,「她對每個人都好。我聽說格琳達是個美麗的女人,雖然活了很多年,卻懂得怎樣保持年輕。」

passages.original: “How can I get to her castle?” asked Dorothy.
passages.vernacular: 「我點樣才能到佢嘅城堡?」桃樂絲問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我怎樣才能到她的城堡?」桃樂絲問。

passages.original: “The road is straight to the South,” he answered, “but it is said to be full of dangers to travelers. There are wild beasts in the woods, and a race of queer men who do not like strangers to cross their country. For this reason none of the Quadlings ever come to the Emerald City.”
passages.vernacular: 「路一直通向南方,」佢回答,「但據講對旅行者來講到處係危險。樹林裡有野獸,仲有一種古怪嘅人,不鍾意陌生人穿過佢哋嘅國家。因為呢個原因,夸德林人從唔到翡翠城嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「路一直通向南方,」他回答,「但據說對旅行者來說到處是危險。樹林裡有野獸,還有一種古怪的人,不喜歡陌生人穿過他們的國家。因為這個原因,夸德林人從不到翡翠城來。」

passages.original: The soldier then left them and the Scarecrow said:
passages.vernacular: 士兵然後離開喇,稻草人講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 士兵然後離開了,稻草人說:

passages.original: “It seems, in spite of dangers, that the best thing Dorothy can do is to travel to the Land of the South and ask Glinda to help her. For, of course, if Dorothy stays here she will never get back to Kansas.”
passages.vernacular: 「睇來,儘管有危險,桃樂絲能做嘅最好嘅事就係前往南方國土,請格琳達幫助佢。因為,當然,如果桃樂絲留喺呢度,佢永遠回不咗堪薩斯。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「看來,儘管有危險,桃樂絲能做的最好的事就是前往南方國土,請格琳達幫助她。因為,當然,如果桃樂絲留在這裡,她永遠回不了堪薩斯。」

passages.original: “You must have been thinking again,” remarked the Tin Woodman.
passages.vernacular: 「你一定又喺思考喇,」鐵皮樵夫講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你一定又在思考了,」鐵皮樵夫說。

passages.original: “I have,” said the Scarecrow.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,」稻草人講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,」稻草人說。

passages.original: “I shall go with Dorothy,” declared the Lion, “for I am tired of your city and long for the woods and the country again. I am really a wild beast, you know. Besides, Dorothy will need someone to protect her.”
passages.vernacular: 「我要同桃樂絲一起去,」獅子宣布,「因為我厭倦咗你哋嘅城市,渴望再回到樹林同鄉間。你知道,我真嘅係頭野獸。而且,桃樂絲需要有人保護佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我要同桃樂絲一起去,」獅子宣布,「因為我厭倦了你們的城市,渴望再回到樹林和鄉間。你知道,我真的是頭野獸。而且,桃樂絲需要有人保護她。」

passages.original: “That is true,” agreed the Woodman. “My axe may be of service to her; so I also will go with her to the Land of the South.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係真嘅,」樵夫同意。「我嘅斧頭可能對佢有用;所以我都同佢去南方國土。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是真的,」樵夫同意。「我的斧頭可能對她有用;所以我也同她去南方國土。」

passages.original: “When shall we start?” asked the Scarecrow.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋乜嘢時候出發?」稻草人問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們什麼時候出發?」稻草人問。

passages.original: “Are you going?” they asked, in surprise.
passages.vernacular: 「你都去嗎?」佢哋驚訝地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你也去嗎?」他們驚訝地問。

passages.original: “Certainly. If it wasn’t for Dorothy I should never have had brains. She lifted me from the pole in the cornfield and brought me to the Emerald City. So my good luck is all due to her, and I shall never leave her until she starts back to Kansas for good and all.”
passages.vernacular: 「當然。如果唔係桃樂絲,我永遠唔會有腦子。佢把我從玉米田嘅桿子上救下嚟,帶到翡翠城。所以我嘅好運全係因為佢,我永遠唔會離開佢,直到佢永遠回到堪薩斯為止。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然。如果不是桃樂絲,我永遠不會有腦子。她把我從玉米田的桿子上救下來,帶到翡翠城。所以我的好運全是因為她,我永遠不會離開她,直到她永遠回到堪薩斯為止。」

passages.original: “Thank you,” said Dorothy gratefully. “You are all very kind to me. But I should like to start as soon as possible.”
passages.vernacular: 「謝謝你,」桃樂絲感激地講。「你哋對我都好好。但我想盡快出發。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「謝謝你,」桃樂絲感激地說。「你們對我都非常好。但我想盡快出發。」

passages.original: “We shall go tomorrow morning,” returned the Scarecrow. “So now let us all get ready, for it will be a long journey.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋聽日早晨走,」稻草人回答。「所以而家讓我哋大家都準備好,因為呢將係一段長途旅程。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們明天早晨走,」稻草人回答。「所以現在讓我們大家都準備好,因為這將是一段長途旅程。」

chapters.title: Chapter XIX: Attacked by the Fighting Trees 第十九章:被會打架的樹攻擊

passages.original: The next morning Dorothy kissed the pretty green girl good-bye, and they all shook hands with the soldier with the green whiskers, who had walked with them as far as the gate. When the Guardian of the Gate saw them again he wondered greatly that they could leave the beautiful City to get into new trouble. But he at once unlocked their spectacles, which he put back into the green box, and gave them many good wishes to carry with them.
passages.vernacular: 第二天早晨,桃樂絲吻別咗漂亮嘅綠衣女孩,佢哋都同陪佢哋走到城門嘅留綠鬍鬚嘅士兵握手。城門守衛再次見到佢哋時,好驚訝佢哋竟然離開美麗嘅城市去惹新嘅麻煩。但佢即刻打開佢哋嘅眼鏡,把佢哋放回綠箱子,畀佢哋許多好嘅祝福讓佢哋帶住上路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天早晨,桃樂絲吻別了漂亮的綠衣女孩,他們都同陪他們走到城門的留綠鬍鬚的士兵握手。城門守衛再次見到他們時,非常驚訝他們竟然離開美麗的城市去惹新的麻煩。但他馬上打開他們的眼鏡,把它們放回綠箱子,給他們許多好的祝福讓他們帶著上路。

passages.original: “You are now our ruler,” he said to the Scarecrow; “so you must come back to us as soon as possible.”
passages.vernacular: 「你而家係我哋嘅統治者,」佢對稻草人講;「所以你必須盡快回嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你現在是我們的統治者,」他對稻草人說;「所以你必須盡快回來。」

passages.original: “I certainly shall if I am able,” the Scarecrow replied; “but I must help Dorothy to get home, first.”
passages.vernacular: 「如果可以,我一定回嚟,」稻草人回答;「但我必須先幫助桃樂絲回家。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果可以,我一定回來,」稻草人回答;「但我必須先幫助桃樂絲回家。」

passages.original: As Dorothy bade the good-natured Guardian a last farewell she said:
passages.vernacular: 桃樂絲向和藹嘅城門守衛作最後嘅告別時講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 桃樂絲向和藹的城門守衛作最後的告別時說:

passages.original: “I have been very kindly treated in your lovely City, and everyone has been good to me. I cannot tell you how grateful I am.”
passages.vernacular: 「喺你哋可愛嘅城市,我受到好好嘅款待,每個人都對我好好。我講不出我有幾咁感激。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「在你們可愛的城市,我受到很好的款待,每個人都對我很好。我說不出我有多麼感激。」

passages.original: “Don’t try, my dear,” he answered. “We should like to keep you with us, but if it is your wish to return to Kansas, I hope you will find a way.” He then opened the gate of the outer wall, and they walked forth and started upon their journey.
passages.vernacular: 「別費心講喇,親愛嘅,」佢回答。「我哋想留你喺我哋身邊,但如果你想回堪薩斯,我希望你能找到辦法。」然後佢打開外牆嘅門,佢哋走咗出去,開始旅程。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「別費心說了,親愛的,」他回答。「我們想留你在我們身邊,但如果你想回堪薩斯,我希望你能找到辦法。」然後他打開外牆的門,他們走了出去,開始旅程。

passages.original: The sun shone brightly as our friends turned their faces toward the Land of the South. They were all in the best of spirits, and laughed and chatted together. Dorothy was once more filled with the hope of getting home, and the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman were glad to be of use to her. As for the Lion, he sniffed the fresh air with delight and whisked his tail from side to side in pure joy at being in the country again, while Toto ran around them and chased the moths and butterflies, barking merrily all the time.
passages.vernacular: 我哋嘅朋友哋轉向南方國土,陽光明媚。佢哋心情都極好,一起講笑聊天。桃樂絲再次充滿咗回家嘅希望,稻草人同鐵皮樵夫好高興能幫上佢嘅忙。至於獅子,佢高興地嗅住新鮮空氣,又回到鄉間,純粹嘅喜悅使佢把尾巴左右甩動,而托托喺佢哋周圍跑,追逐飛蛾同蝴蝶,一直快樂地叫住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們的朋友們轉向南方國土,陽光明媚。他們心情都極好,一起說笑聊天。桃樂絲再次充滿了回家的希望,稻草人和鐵皮樵夫很高興能幫上她的忙。至於獅子,他高興地嗅著新鮮空氣,又回到鄉間,純粹的喜悅使他把尾巴左右甩動,而托托在他們周圍跑,追逐飛蛾和蝴蝶,一直快樂地叫著。

passages.original: “City life does not agree with me at all,” remarked the Lion, as they walked along at a brisk pace. “I have lost much flesh since I lived there, and now I am anxious for a chance to show the other beasts how courageous I have grown.”
passages.vernacular: 「城市生活啲都不適合我,」獅子講,佢哋正快步走住。「自從住喺嗰度我掉咗好多肉,而家我急切地想有機會讓其他野獸睇睇我變得幾咁勇敢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「城市生活一點也不適合我,」獅子說,他們正快步走著。「自從住在那裡我掉了很多肉,現在我急切地想有機會讓其他野獸看看我變得多麼勇敢。」

passages.original: They now turned and took a last look at the Emerald City. All they could see was a mass of towers and steeples behind the green walls, and high up above everything the spires and dome of the Palace of Oz.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋而家轉身,最後睇咗一眼翡翠城。佢哋所能睇到嘅只係綠牆後面一大片塔樓同尖塔,同遠遠高於一切嘅奧茲宮殿嘅尖頂同圓頂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們現在轉身,最後看了一眼翡翠城。他們所能看到的只是綠牆後面一大片塔樓和尖塔,和遠遠高於一切的奧茲宮殿的尖頂和圓頂。

passages.original: “Oz was not such a bad Wizard, after all,” said the Tin Woodman, as he felt his heart rattling around in his breast.
passages.vernacular: 「奧茲畢竟唔係咁壞嘅巫師,」鐵皮樵夫講,感覺住佢嘅心喺胸口裡晃動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「奧茲畢竟不是那麼壞的巫師,」鐵皮樵夫說,感覺著他的心在胸口裡晃動。

passages.original: “He knew how to give me brains, and very good brains, too,” said the Scarecrow.
passages.vernacular: 「佢知道點畀我腦子,而且係好好嘅腦子,」稻草人講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他知道怎麼給我腦子,而且是很好的腦子,」稻草人說。

passages.original: “If Oz had taken a dose of the same courage he gave me,” added the Lion, “he would have been a brave man.”
passages.vernacular: 「如果奧茲自己服一劑佢畀我嘅同樣嘅勇氣,」獅子補充講,「佢會係個勇敢嘅人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果奧茲自己服一劑他給我的同樣的勇氣,」獅子補充說,「他會是個勇敢的人。」

passages.original: Dorothy said nothing. Oz had not kept the promise he made her, but he had done his best, so she forgave him. As he said, he was a good man, even if he was a bad Wizard.
passages.vernacular: 桃樂絲冇講話。奧茲冇履行對佢嘅諾言,但佢已盡咗力,所以佢原諒咗佢。正如佢講嘅,佢係個好人,即使佢係個壞巫師。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 桃樂絲沒有說話。奧茲沒有履行對她的諾言,但他已盡了力,所以她原諒了他。正如他說的,他是個好人,即使他是個壞巫師。

passages.original: The first day’s journey was through the green fields and bright flowers that stretched about the Emerald City on every side. They slept that night on the grass, with nothing but the stars over them; and they rested very well indeed.
passages.vernacular: 第一天嘅旅程穿過翡翠城四周伸展嘅綠色田野同鮮豔嘅花朵。嗰天晚上佢哋瞓喺草地上,頭上只有星星;佢哋瞓得確實好好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第一天的旅程穿過翡翠城四周伸展的綠色田野和鮮豔的花朵。那天晚上他們睡在草地上,頭上只有星星;他們睡得確實很好。

passages.original: In the morning they traveled on until they came to a thick wood. There was no way of going around it, for it seemed to extend to the right and left as far as they could see; and, besides, they did not dare change the direction of their journey for fear of getting lost. So they looked for the place where it would be easiest to get into the forest.
passages.vernacular: 早晨佢哋繼續旅行,直到來到一片茂密嘅樹林。冇辦法繞過佢,因為佢似乎向左右延伸到佢哋睇得見嘅盡頭;而且,佢哋都唔敢改變旅行嘅方向,怕迷路。於是佢哋尋找最容易進入森林嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 早晨他們繼續旅行,直到來到一片茂密的樹林。沒有辦法繞過它,因為它似乎向左右延伸到他們看得見的盡頭;而且,他們也不敢改變旅行的方向,怕迷路。於是他們尋找最容易進入森林的地方。

passages.original: The Scarecrow, who was in the lead, finally discovered a big tree with such wide-spreading branches that there was room for the party to pass underneath. So he walked forward to the tree, but just as he came under the first branches they bent down and twined around him, and the next minute he was raised from the ground and flung headlong among his fellow travelers.
passages.vernacular: 走喺最前面嘅稻草人終於發現一棵大樹,樹枝伸展得咁寬,下面有空間讓隊伍通過。於是佢向嗰棵樹走去,但佢剛走到第一根樹枝下面,佢哋就彎下嚟纏住佢,下一刻佢被提離地面,頭朝下扔到佢嘅旅伴哋中間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 走在最前面的稻草人終於發現一棵大樹,樹枝伸展得那麼寬,下面有空間讓隊伍通過。於是他向那棵樹走去,但他剛走到第一根樹枝下面,它們就彎下來纏住他,下一刻他被提離地面,頭朝下扔到他的旅伴們中間。

passages.original: This did not hurt the Scarecrow, but it surprised him, and he looked rather dizzy when Dorothy picked him up.
passages.vernacular: 呢個冇傷到稻草人,但讓佢食驚,桃樂絲把佢扶起嚟時,佢睇起嚟有點暈頭轉向。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這沒有傷到稻草人,但讓他吃驚,桃樂絲把他扶起來時,他看起來有點暈頭轉向。

passages.original: “Here is another space between the trees,” called the Lion.
passages.vernacular: 「樹同樹之間仲有另一個空隙,」獅子喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「樹與樹之間還有另一個空隙,」獅子喊道。

passages.original: “Let me try it first,” said the Scarecrow, “for it doesn’t hurt me to get thrown about.” He walked up to another tree, as he spoke, but its branches immediately seized him and tossed him back again.
passages.vernacular: 「讓我先試試,」稻草人講,「因為被扔嚟扔去對我冇傷害。」佢邊講邊走向另一棵樹,但佢嘅樹枝即刻抓住佢,又把佢扔咗回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「讓我先試試,」稻草人說,「因為被扔來扔去對我沒有傷害。」他邊說邊走向另一棵樹,但它的樹枝馬上抓住他,又把他扔了回來。

passages.original: “This is strange,” exclaimed Dorothy. “What shall we do?”
passages.vernacular: 「真奇怪,」桃樂絲喊道。「我哋點算?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真奇怪,」桃樂絲喊道。「我們怎麼辦?」

passages.original: “The trees seem to have made up their minds to fight us, and stop our journey,” remarked the Lion.
passages.vernacular: 「呢啲樹似乎下定決心要同我哋作對,阻止我哋嘅旅程,」獅子講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這些樹似乎下定決心要同我們作對,阻止我們的旅程,」獅子說。

passages.original: “I believe I will try it myself,” said the Woodman, and shouldering his axe, he marched up to the first tree that had handled the Scarecrow so roughly. When a big branch bent down to seize him the Woodman chopped at it so fiercely that he cut it in two. At once the tree began shaking all its branches as if in pain, and the Tin Woodman passed safely under it.
passages.vernacular: 「我想我自己嚟試試,」樵夫講,肩上扛起斧頭,大步走向第一棵對稻草人咁粗暴嘅樹。一根大樹枝彎下嚟要抓佢時,樵夫猛烈地砍佢,把佢砍成兩截。嗰棵樹即刻開始搖晃佢所有嘅樹枝,好像好痛,鐵皮樵夫安全地從下面走過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想我自己來試試,」樵夫說,肩上扛起斧頭,大步走向第一棵對稻草人那麼粗暴的樹。一根大樹枝彎下來要抓他時,樵夫猛烈地砍它,把它砍成兩截。那棵樹馬上開始搖晃它所有的樹枝,好像很痛,鐵皮樵夫安全地從下面走過。

passages.original: “Come on!” he shouted to the others. “Be quick!” They all ran forward and passed under the tree without injury, except Toto, who was caught by a small branch and shaken until he howled. But the Woodman promptly chopped off the branch and set the little dog free.
passages.vernacular: 「嚟吧!」佢對其他人喊。「快點!」佢哋都跑上前,從樹下通過,冇受傷,除咗托托,佢被一根小樹枝抓住,搖得嚎叫起嚟。但樵夫即刻砍斷咗嗰根樹枝,放咗小狗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「來吧!」他對其他人喊。「快點!」他們都跑上前,從樹下通過,沒受傷,除了托托,他被一根小樹枝抓住,搖得嚎叫起來。但樵夫立刻砍斷了那根樹枝,放了小狗。

passages.original: The other trees of the forest did nothing to keep them back, so they made up their minds that only the first row of trees could bend down their branches, and that probably these were the policemen of the forest, and given this wonderful power in order to keep strangers out of it.
passages.vernacular: 森林裡嘅其他樹冇做任何事阻攔佢哋,所以佢哋斷定只有第一排樹能彎下樹枝,呢啲大概係森林嘅警察,被賦予呢種奇妙嘅力量以阻止陌生人進入。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 森林裡的其他樹沒有做任何事阻攔他們,所以他們斷定只有第一排樹能彎下樹枝,這些大概是森林的警察,被賦予這種奇妙的力量以阻止陌生人進入。

passages.original: The four travelers walked with ease through the trees until they came to the farther edge of the wood. Then, to their surprise, they found before them a high wall which seemed to be made of white china. It was smooth, like the surface of a dish, and higher than their heads.
passages.vernacular: 四個旅行者輕易地穿過樹林,走到樹林嘅遠處邊緣。然後,令佢哋驚訝嘅係,佢哋面前出現咗一堵高牆,似乎係白瓷做嘅。佢光滑得像碟子嘅表面,比佢哋嘅頭仲高。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 四個旅行者輕易地穿過樹林,走到樹林的遠處邊緣。然後,令他們驚訝的是,他們面前出現了一堵高牆,似乎是白瓷做的。它光滑得像碟子的表面,比他們的頭還高。

passages.original: “What shall we do now?” asked Dorothy.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋而家點算?」桃樂絲問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們現在怎麼辦?」桃樂絲問。

passages.original: “I will make a ladder,” said the Tin Woodman, “for we certainly must climb over the wall.”
passages.vernacular: 「我嚟做一把梯子,」鐵皮樵夫講,「因為我哋肯定必須爬過呢堵牆。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我來做一把梯子,」鐵皮樵夫說,「因為我們肯定必須爬過這堵牆。」

chapters.title: Chapter XX: The Dainty China Country 第二十章:精緻的瓷器國

passages.original: While the Woodman was making a ladder from wood which he found in the forest Dorothy lay down and slept, for she was tired by the long walk. The Lion also curled himself up to sleep and Toto lay beside him.
passages.vernacular: 樵夫用喺森林裡找到嘅木頭做梯子時,桃樂絲躺下瞓覺,因為走咗好長嘅路,佢累喇。獅子都蜷起身子瞓喇,托托躺喺佢旁邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 樵夫用在森林裡找到的木頭做梯子時,桃樂絲躺下睡覺,因為走了很長的路,她累了。獅子也蜷起身子睡了,托托躺在他旁邊。

passages.original: The Scarecrow watched the Woodman while he worked, and said to him:
passages.vernacular: 稻草人睇住樵夫工作,對佢講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 稻草人看著樵夫工作,對他說:

passages.original: “I cannot think why this wall is here, nor what it is made of.”
passages.vernacular: 「我想不通呢堵牆點解喺呢度,都唔知道佢係乜嘢做嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想不通這堵牆為什麼在這裡,也不知道它是什麼做的。」

passages.original: “Rest your brains and do not worry about the wall,” replied the Woodman. “When we have climbed over it, we shall know what is on the other side.”
passages.vernacular: 「讓你嘅腦子休息一下,別為呢堵牆操心,」樵夫回答。「等我哋爬過去,就會知道另一邊有乜嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「讓你的腦子休息一下,別為這堵牆操心,」樵夫回答。「等我們爬過去,就會知道另一邊有什麼。」

passages.original: After a time the ladder was finished. It looked clumsy, but the Tin Woodman was sure it was strong and would answer their purpose. The Scarecrow waked Dorothy and the Lion and Toto, and told them that the ladder was ready. The Scarecrow climbed up the ladder first, but he was so awkward that Dorothy had to follow close behind and keep him from falling off. When he got his head over the top of the wall the Scarecrow said, “Oh, my!”
passages.vernacular: 過咗一會兒,梯子做好喇。佢睇起嚟笨重,但鐵皮樵夫肯定佢好結實,足夠派上用場。稻草人叫醒桃樂絲、獅子同托托,告訴佢哋梯子準備好喇。稻草人先爬上梯子,但佢咁笨拙,桃樂絲唔得不緊跟喺後面,免得佢掉下嚟。佢把頭伸過牆頭時,稻草人講:「哎呀!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過了一會兒,梯子做好了。它看起來笨重,但鐵皮樵夫肯定它很結實,足夠派上用場。稻草人叫醒桃樂絲、獅子和托托,告訴他們梯子準備好了。稻草人先爬上梯子,但他那麼笨拙,桃樂絲不得不緊跟在後面,免得他掉下來。他把頭伸過牆頭時,稻草人說:「哎呀!」

passages.original: “Go on,” exclaimed Dorothy.
passages.vernacular: 「繼續啊,」桃樂絲喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「繼續啊,」桃樂絲喊道。

passages.original: So the Scarecrow climbed farther up and sat down on the top of the wall, and Dorothy put her head over and cried, “Oh, my!” just as the Scarecrow had done.
passages.vernacular: 於是稻草人爬得更高,坐喺牆頭上,桃樂絲探頭過去,都像稻草人嗰樣喊:「哎呀!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是稻草人爬得更高,坐在牆頭上,桃樂絲探頭過去,也像稻草人那樣喊:「哎呀!」

passages.original: Then Toto came up, and immediately began to bark, but Dorothy made him be still.
passages.vernacular: 然後托托上嚟,即刻開始叫,但桃樂絲叫佢安靜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後托托上來,立刻開始叫,但桃樂絲叫他安靜。

passages.original: The Lion climbed the ladder next, and the Tin Woodman came last; but both of them cried, “Oh, my!” as soon as they looked over the wall. When they were all sitting in a row on the top of the wall, they looked down and saw a strange sight.
passages.vernacular: 獅子接住爬梯子,鐵皮樵夫最後;但佢哋兩個一睇過牆頭,就都喊:「哎呀!」當佢哋都排成一排坐喺牆頭上時,佢哋往下睇,睇到一幅奇怪嘅景象。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 獅子接著爬梯子,鐵皮樵夫最後;但他們兩個一看過牆頭,就都喊:「哎呀!」當他們都排成一排坐在牆頭上時,他們往下看,看到一幅奇怪的景象。

passages.original: Before them was a great stretch of country having a floor as smooth and shining and white as the bottom of a big platter. Scattered around were many houses made entirely of china and painted in the brightest colors. These houses were quite small, the biggest of them reaching only as high as Dorothy’s waist. There were also pretty little barns, with china fences around them; and many cows and sheep and horses and pigs and chickens, all made of china, were standing about in groups.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋面前係一大片土地,地面像大盤子嘅底部嗰樣光滑、發亮、潔白。周圍散落住許多完全用瓷做嘅房子,漆成最鮮豔嘅顏色。呢啲房子相當小,最大嘅都只到桃樂絲嘅腰咁高。仲有啲漂亮嘅小穀倉,周圍有瓷嘅籬笆;許多牛、羊、馬、豬同雞,全係瓷做嘅,成群站喺周圍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們面前是一大片土地,地面像大盤子的底部那樣光滑、發亮、潔白。周圍散落著許多完全用瓷做的房子,漆成最鮮豔的顏色。這些房子相當小,最大的也只到桃樂絲的腰那麼高。還有一些漂亮的小穀倉,周圍有瓷的籬笆;許多牛、羊、馬、豬和雞,全是瓷做的,成群站在周圍。

passages.original: But the strangest of all were the people who lived in this queer country. There were milkmaids and shepherdesses, with brightly colored bodices and golden spots all over their gowns; and princesses with most gorgeous frocks of silver and gold and purple; and shepherds dressed in knee breeches with pink and yellow and blue stripes down them, and golden buckles on their shoes; and princes with jeweled crowns upon their heads, wearing ermine robes and satin doublets; and funny clowns in ruffled gowns, with round red spots upon their cheeks and tall, pointed caps. And, strangest of all, these people were all made of china, even to their clothes, and were so small that the tallest of them was no higher than Dorothy’s knee.
passages.vernacular: 但最奇怪嘅係住喺呢個古怪國家嘅人。有擠奶女工同牧羊女,穿住顏色鮮豔嘅緊身上衣,長袍上到處係金色斑點;有穿住華麗至極嘅銀色、金色同紫色衣裙嘅公主哋;有穿住膝褲、褲子上有粉紅、黃色同藍色條紋、鞋上有金扣嘅牧羊人;有頭戴寶石皇冠、穿住貂皮長袍同緞面緊身上衣嘅王子哋;仲有穿住皺邊長袍、臉頰上有圓形紅斑、戴住高尖帽嘅滑稽小丑。而最奇怪嘅係,呢啲人全係瓷做嘅,連佢哋嘅衣服都係,而且小得咁厲害,最高嘅都不過到桃樂絲嘅膝蓋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但最奇怪的是住在這個古怪國家的人。有擠奶女工和牧羊女,穿著顏色鮮豔的緊身上衣,長袍上到處是金色斑點;有穿著華麗至極的銀色、金色和紫色衣裙的公主們;有穿著膝褲、褲子上有粉紅、黃色和藍色條紋、鞋上有金扣的牧羊人;有頭戴寶石皇冠、穿著貂皮長袍和緞面緊身上衣的王子們;還有穿著皺邊長袍、臉頰上有圓形紅斑、戴著高尖帽的滑稽小丑。而最奇怪的是,這些人全是瓷做的,連他們的衣服也是,而且小得那麼厲害,最高的也不過到桃樂絲的膝蓋。

passages.original: No one did so much as look at the travelers at first, except one little purple china dog with an extra-large head, which came to the wall and barked at them in a tiny voice, afterwards running away again.
passages.vernacular: 起初冇人睇旅行者一眼,只有一隻頭特別大嘅紫色小瓷狗,走到牆邊,用細小嘅聲音對佢哋叫咗幾聲,然後又跑開喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 起初沒有人看旅行者一眼,只有一隻頭特別大的紫色小瓷狗,走到牆邊,用細小的聲音對他們叫了幾聲,然後又跑開了。

passages.original: “How shall we get down?” asked Dorothy.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋點下去?」桃樂絲問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們怎麼下去?」桃樂絲問。

passages.original: They found the ladder so heavy they could not pull it up, so the Scarecrow fell off the wall and the others jumped down upon him so that the hard floor would not hurt their feet. Of course they took pains not to light on his head and get the pins in their feet. When all were safely down they picked up the Scarecrow, whose body was quite flattened out, and patted his straw into shape again.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋發現梯子太重,拉不上嚟,於是稻草人從牆上摔下去,其他人跳到佢身上,咁樣堅硬嘅地面唔會弄痛佢哋嘅腳。當然,佢哋小心不落喺佢嘅頭上,以免針扎進腳裡。大家都安全下嚟後,佢哋把身體被壓得扁平嘅稻草人扶起嚟,輕拍佢嘅稻草使佢恢復形狀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們發現梯子太重,拉不上來,於是稻草人從牆上摔下去,其他人跳到他身上,這樣堅硬的地面不會弄痛他們的腳。當然,他們小心不落在他的頭上,以免針扎進腳裡。大家都安全下來後,他們把身體被壓得扁平的稻草人扶起來,輕拍他的稻草使它恢復形狀。

passages.original: “We must cross this strange place in order to get to the other side,” said Dorothy, “for it would be unwise for us to go any other way except due South.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋必須穿過呢個奇怪嘅地方才能到另一邊,」桃樂絲講,「因為我哋除咗一直往南,走任何別嘅方向都係不明智嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們必須穿過這個奇怪的地方才能到另一邊,」桃樂絲說,「因為我們除了一直往南,走任何別的方向都是不明智的。」

passages.original: They began walking through the country of the china people, and the first thing they came to was a china milkmaid milking a china cow. As they drew near, the cow suddenly gave a kick and kicked over the stool, the pail, and even the milkmaid herself, and all fell on the china ground with a great clatter.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋開始走過瓷人嘅國家,最先遇到嘅係一個瓷擠奶女工喺擠一頭瓷母牛嘅奶。佢哋走近時,母牛突然踢咗一腳,踢翻咗凳子、桶,連擠奶女工自己都踢翻喇,全都「嘩啦」一聲倒喺瓷地上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們開始走過瓷人的國家,最先遇到的是一個瓷擠奶女工在擠一頭瓷母牛的奶。他們走近時,母牛突然踢了一腳,踢翻了凳子、桶,連擠奶女工自己也踢翻了,全都「嘩啦」一聲倒在瓷地上。

passages.original: Dorothy was shocked to see that the cow had broken her leg off, and that the pail was lying in several small pieces, while the poor milkmaid had a nick in her left elbow.
passages.vernacular: 桃樂絲驚恐地睇到母牛嘅腿斷喇,桶摔成幾片小碎片,而可憐嘅擠奶女工左手肘上有一個缺口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 桃樂絲驚恐地看到母牛的腿斷了,桶摔成幾片小碎片,而可憐的擠奶女工左手肘上有一個缺口。

passages.original: “There!” cried the milkmaid angrily. “See what you have done! My cow has broken her leg, and I must take her to the mender’s shop and have it glued on again. What do you mean by coming here and frightening my cow?”
passages.vernacular: 「睇!」擠奶女工生氣地喊道。「睇你做嘅好事!我嘅牛斷咗腿,我必須帶佢到修理店把佢黏回去。你哋跑到呢度嚇我嘅牛係乜嘢意思?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「看!」擠奶女工生氣地喊道。「看你做的好事!我的牛斷了腿,我必須帶她到修理店把它黏回去。你們跑到這裡嚇我的牛是什麼意思?」

passages.original: “I’m very sorry,” returned Dorothy. “Please forgive us.”
passages.vernacular: 「我好抱歉,」桃樂絲回答。「請原諒我哋。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我很抱歉,」桃樂絲回答。「請原諒我們。」

passages.original: But the pretty milkmaid was much too vexed to make any answer. She picked up the leg sulkily and led her cow away, the poor animal limping on three legs. As she left them the milkmaid cast many reproachful glances over her shoulder at the clumsy strangers, holding her nicked elbow close to her side.
passages.vernacular: 但漂亮嘅擠奶女工太惱火喇,冇回答。佢悶悶不樂地撿起嗰條腿,牽住佢嘅牛走喇,可憐嘅動物用三條腿一瘸一拐地走。佢離開佢哋時,擠奶女工抱住受咗缺口嘅手肘貼緊身邊,回頭向呢啲笨手笨腳嘅陌生人投去許多責備嘅目光。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但漂亮的擠奶女工太惱火了,沒有回答。她悶悶不樂地撿起那條腿,牽著她的牛走了,可憐的動物用三條腿一瘸一拐地走。她離開他們時,擠奶女工抱著受了缺口的手肘貼緊身邊,回頭向這些笨手笨腳的陌生人投去許多責備的目光。

passages.original: Dorothy was quite grieved at this mishap.
passages.vernacular: 桃樂絲為呢次意外好難過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 桃樂絲為這次意外很難過。

passages.original: “We must be very careful here,” said the kind-hearted Woodman, “or we may hurt these pretty little people so they will never get over it.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋喺呢度必須好小心,」好心腸嘅樵夫講,「否則我哋可能傷害呢啲漂亮嘅小人兒,使佢哋永遠無法恢復。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們在這裡必須非常小心,」好心腸的樵夫說,「否則我們可能傷害這些漂亮的小人兒,使他們永遠無法恢復。」

passages.original: A little farther on Dorothy met a most beautifully dressed young Princess, who stopped short as she saw the strangers and started to run away.
passages.vernacular: 再往前走啲,桃樂絲遇到一位衣住華麗至極嘅年輕公主,佢睇到陌生人,猛地停住,開始逃跑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再往前走一點,桃樂絲遇到一位衣著華麗至極的年輕公主,她看到陌生人,猛地停住,開始逃跑。

passages.original: Dorothy wanted to see more of the Princess, so she ran after her. But the china girl cried out:
passages.vernacular: 桃樂絲想多睇睇呢位公主,於是追咗上去。但瓷女孩大叫:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 桃樂絲想多看看這位公主,於是追了上去。但瓷女孩大叫:

passages.original: “Don’t chase me! Don’t chase me!”
passages.vernacular: 「別追我!別追我!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「別追我!別追我!」

passages.original: She had such a frightened little voice that Dorothy stopped and said, “Why not?”
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅聲音咁驚恐,桃樂絲停下嚟問:「點解不?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的聲音那麼驚恐,桃樂絲停下來問:「為什麼不?」

passages.original: “Because,” answered the Princess, also stopping, a safe distance away, “if I run I may fall down and break myself.”
passages.vernacular: 「因為,」公主喺安全距離外都停下嚟回答,「如果我跑,可能摔倒,把自己摔壞。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「因為,」公主在安全距離外也停下來回答,「如果我跑,可能摔倒,把自己摔壞。」

passages.original: “But could you not be mended?” asked the girl.
passages.vernacular: 「但你唔能夠被修好嗎?」女孩問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但你不能被修好嗎?」女孩問。

passages.original: “Oh, yes; but one is never so pretty after being mended, you know,” replied the Princess.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,可以;但你知道,修好之後就再都冇咁漂亮喇,」公主回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,可以;但你知道,修好之後就再也沒有那麼漂亮了,」公主回答。

passages.original: “I suppose not,” said Dorothy.
passages.vernacular: 「我想唔會喇,」桃樂絲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想不會了,」桃樂絲說。

passages.original: “Now there is Mr. Joker, one of our clowns,” continued the china lady, “who is always trying to stand upon his head. He has broken himself so often that he is mended in a hundred places, and doesn’t look at all pretty. Here he comes now, so you can see for yourself.”
passages.vernacular: 「你睇有個小丑先生,我哋嘅小丑之一,」瓷女士繼續講,「佢總是想倒立。佢把自己摔壞過咁多次,被修補咗一百多處,睇起嚟啲都不漂亮。佢而家嚟喇,你可以自己睇睇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你看有個小丑先生,我們的小丑之一,」瓷女士繼續說,「他總是想倒立。他把自己摔壞過那麼多次,被修補了一百多處,看起來一點也不漂亮。他現在來了,你可以自己看看。」

passages.original: Indeed, a jolly little clown came walking toward them, and Dorothy could see that in spite of his pretty clothes of red and yellow and green he was completely covered with cracks, running every which way and showing plainly that he had been mended in many places.
passages.vernacular: 確實,一個快活嘅小丑走咗過嚟,桃樂絲睇到,儘管佢穿住紅、黃、綠色嘅漂亮衣服,佢全身佈滿裂紋,朝各個方向延伸,清楚地表明佢被修補過好多處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 確實,一個快活的小丑走了過來,桃樂絲看到,儘管他穿著紅、黃、綠色的漂亮衣服,他全身佈滿裂紋,朝各個方向延伸,清楚地表明他被修補過很多處。

passages.original: The Clown put his hands in his pockets, and after puffing out his cheeks and nodding his head at them saucily, he said:
passages.vernacular: 小丑把雙手插進口袋,鼓起腮幫子,無禮地向佢哋點點頭,講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小丑把雙手插進口袋,鼓起腮幫子,無禮地向他們點點頭,說:

passages.original: “My lady fair, Why do you stare At poor old Mr. Joker? You’re quite as stiff And prim as if You’d eaten up a poker!”
passages.vernacular: 「美麗嘅小姐,你為何盯住可憐嘅老丑先生睇?你硬邦邦、一本正經,好像剛吞下一根火鉗!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「美麗的小姐,你為何盯著可憐的老丑先生看?你硬邦邦、一本正經,好像剛吞下一根火鉗!」

passages.original: “Be quiet, sir!” said the Princess. “Can’t you see these are strangers, and should be treated with respect?”
passages.vernacular: 「閉嘴,先生!」公主講。「你冇睇到呢啲係陌生人,應該受到尊重嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「閉嘴,先生!」公主說。「你沒看到這些是陌生人,應該受到尊重嗎?」

passages.original: “Well, that’s respect, I expect,” declared the Clown, and immediately stood upon his head.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,呢個就係尊重,我估計,」小丑宣稱,即刻倒立起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,這就是尊重,我估計,」小丑宣稱,馬上倒立起來。

passages.original: “Don’t mind Mr. Joker,” said the Princess to Dorothy. “He is considerably cracked in his head, and that makes him foolish.”
passages.vernacular: 「別理丑先生,」公主對桃樂絲講。「佢嘅頭裂得好厲害,所以佢變得愚蠢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「別理丑先生,」公主對桃樂絲說。「他的頭裂得很厲害,所以他變得愚蠢。」

passages.original: “Oh, I don’t mind him a bit,” said Dorothy. “But you are so beautiful,” she continued, “that I am sure I could love you dearly. Won’t you let me carry you back to Kansas, and stand you on Aunt Em’s mantel? I could carry you in my basket.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我啲都不介意佢,」桃樂絲講。「但你咁漂亮,」佢繼續講,「我肯定我會好鍾意你。你願意讓我帶你回堪薩斯,把你放喺艾姆嬸嬸嘅壁爐架上嗎?我可以用籃子帶你走。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我一點也不介意他,」桃樂絲說。「但你這麼漂亮,」她繼續說,「我肯定我會非常喜歡你。你願意讓我帶你回堪薩斯,把你放在艾姆嬸嬸的壁爐架上嗎?我可以用籃子帶你走。」

passages.original: “That would make me very unhappy,” answered the china Princess. “You see, here in our country we live contentedly, and can talk and move around as we please. But whenever any of us are taken away our joints at once stiffen, and we can only stand straight and look pretty. Of course that is all that is expected of us when we are on mantels and cabinets and drawing-room tables, but our lives are much pleasanter here in our own country.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰會使我好不快樂,」瓷公主回答。「你睇,喺我哋呢度嘅國家,我哋生活得好滿足,可以隨心所欲地講話同走動。但我哋任何人被帶走時,關節就即刻僵硬,只能直直站住,睇起嚟漂亮。當然,喺壁爐架、櫥櫃同客廳桌子上,對我哋嘅期望就係咁樣,但我哋喺自己嘅國家生活要愉快得多。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那會使我非常不快樂,」瓷公主回答。「你看,在我們這裡的國家,我們生活得很滿足,可以隨心所欲地說話和走動。但我們任何人被帶走時,關節就立刻僵硬,只能直直站著,看起來漂亮。當然,在壁爐架、櫥櫃和客廳桌子上,對我們的期望就是這樣,但我們在自己的國家生活要愉快得多。」

passages.original: “I would not make you unhappy for all the world!” exclaimed Dorothy. “So I’ll just say good-bye.”
passages.vernacular: 「我絕唔會為了全世界而讓你不快樂!」桃樂絲喊道。「所以我只講聲再見。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我絕不會為了全世界而讓你不快樂!」桃樂絲喊道。「所以我只說聲再見。」

passages.original: “Good-bye,” replied the Princess.
passages.vernacular: 「再見,」公主回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「再見,」公主回答。

passages.original: They walked carefully through the china country. The little animals and all the people scampered out of their way, fearing the strangers would break them, and after an hour or so the travelers reached the other side of the country and came to another china wall.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋小心地走過瓷人嘅國家。小動物同所有嘅人都跑開躲避佢哋,怕陌生人把佢哋弄破,大約一個小時後,旅行者到咗呢個國家嘅另一邊,嚟到另一堵瓷牆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們小心地走過瓷人的國家。小動物和所有的人都跑開躲避他們,怕陌生人把他們弄破,大約一個小時後,旅行者到了這個國家的另一邊,來到另一堵瓷牆。

passages.original: It was not so high as the first, however, and by standing upon the Lion’s back they all managed to scramble to the top. Then the Lion gathered his legs under him and jumped on the wall; but just as he jumped, he upset a china church with his tail and smashed it all to pieces.
passages.vernacular: 不過佢冇第一堵咁高,站喺獅子背上,佢哋都設法爬到咗牆頭。然後獅子把腿縮到身下,跳上牆;但跳嘅時候,佢嘅尾巴掃翻咗一座瓷教堂,把佢摔得粉碎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過它沒有第一堵那麼高,站在獅子背上,他們都設法爬到了牆頭。然後獅子把腿縮到身下,跳上牆;但跳的時候,他的尾巴掃翻了一座瓷教堂,把它摔得粉碎。

passages.original: “That was too bad,” said Dorothy, “but really I think we were lucky in not doing these little people more harm than breaking a cow’s leg and a church. They are all so brittle!”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰太糟糕喇,」桃樂絲講,「但講真嘅,我想我哋好幸運,對呢啲小人兒造成嘅傷害只係弄斷一頭牛嘅腿同一座教堂。佢哋都咁易碎!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那太糟糕了,」桃樂絲說,「但說真的,我想我們很幸運,對這些小人兒造成的傷害只是弄斷一頭牛的腿和一座教堂。他們都那麼易碎!」

passages.original: “They are, indeed,” said the Scarecrow, “and I am thankful I am made of straw and cannot be easily damaged. There are worse things in the world than being a Scarecrow.”
passages.vernacular: 「確實係,」稻草人講,「我慶幸我係稻草做嘅,唔容易受損。世上有比做稻草人更糟嘅事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「確實是,」稻草人說,「我慶幸我是稻草做的,不容易受損。世上有比做稻草人更糟的事。」

chapters.title: Chapter XXI: The Lion Becomes the King of Beasts 第二十一章:獅子成為百獸之王

passages.original: After climbing down from the china wall the travelers found themselves in a disagreeable country, full of bogs and marshes and covered with tall, rank grass. It was difficult to walk without falling into muddy holes, for the grass was so thick that it hid them from sight. However, by carefully picking their way, they got safely along until they reached solid ground. But here the country seemed wilder than ever, and after a long and tiresome walk through the underbrush they entered another forest, where the trees were bigger and older than any they had ever seen.
passages.vernacular: 從瓷牆爬下嚟後,旅行者哋發現自己置身於一個令人不快嘅國家,到處係沼澤同泥潭,長滿咗又高又雜嘅草。走路好難不掉進泥洞裡,因為草太濃密,把洞都遮住喇。不過,小心地選路走,佢哋安全地前進,直到走到堅實嘅地面。但呢度嘅鄉野似乎比以往更荒蕪,穿過灌木叢走咗一段漫長疲憊嘅路後,佢哋進入另一片森林,嗰度嘅樹比佢哋見過嘅任何樹都更大更老。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從瓷牆爬下來後,旅行者們發現自己置身於一個令人不快的國家,到處是沼澤和泥潭,長滿了又高又雜的草。走路很難不掉進泥洞裡,因為草太濃密,把洞都遮住了。不過,小心地選路走,他們安全地前進,直到走到堅實的地面。但這裡的鄉野似乎比以往更荒蕪,穿過灌木叢走了一段漫長疲憊的路後,他們進入另一片森林,那裡的樹比他們見過的任何樹都更大更老。

passages.original: “This forest is perfectly delightful,” declared the Lion, looking around him with joy. “Never have I seen a more beautiful place.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢片森林真係太讓人愉快喇,」獅子宣稱,高興地環顧四周。「我從冇見過更美嘅地方。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這片森林真是太讓人愉快了,」獅子宣稱,高興地環顧四周。「我從沒見過更美的地方。」

passages.original: “It seems gloomy,” said the Scarecrow.
passages.vernacular: 「佢睇起嚟陰沉,」稻草人講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「它看起來陰沉,」稻草人說。

passages.original: “Not a bit of it,” answered the Lion. “I should like to live here all my life. See how soft the dried leaves are under your feet and how rich and green the moss is that clings to these old trees. Surely no wild beast could wish a pleasanter home.”
passages.vernacular: 「啲都不,」獅子回答。「我想一輩子住喺呢度。睇睇腳下嘅枯葉幾咁柔軟,附喺呢啲老樹上嘅苔蘚幾咁豐厚翠綠。肯定冇野獸會希望有更愜意嘅家。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一點也不,」獅子回答。「我想一輩子住在這裡。看看腳下的枯葉多麼柔軟,附在這些老樹上的苔蘚多麼豐厚翠綠。肯定沒有野獸會希望有更愜意的家。」

passages.original: “Perhaps there are wild beasts in the forest now,” said Dorothy.
passages.vernacular: 「或者而家森林裡有野獸,」桃樂絲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「也許現在森林裡有野獸,」桃樂絲說。

passages.original: “I suppose there are,” returned the Lion, “but I do not see any of them about.”
passages.vernacular: 「我想有,」獅子回答,「但我冇睇到牠哋喺附近。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想有,」獅子回答,「但我沒看到牠們在附近。」

passages.original: They walked through the forest until it became too dark to go any farther. Dorothy and Toto and the Lion lay down to sleep, while the Woodman and the Scarecrow kept watch over them as usual.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋穿過森林走,直到天太黑,唔能夠再往前走。桃樂絲、托托同獅子躺下瞓覺,樵夫同稻草人像往常一樣替佢哋守夜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們穿過森林走,直到天太黑,不能再往前走。桃樂絲、托托和獅子躺下睡覺,樵夫和稻草人像往常一樣替他們守夜。

passages.original: When morning came, they started again. Before they had gone far they heard a low rumble, as of the growling of many wild animals. Toto whimpered a little, but none of the others was frightened, and they kept along the well-trodden path until they came to an opening in the wood, in which were gathered hundreds of beasts of every variety. There were tigers and elephants and bears and wolves and foxes and all the others in the natural history, and for a moment Dorothy was afraid. But the Lion explained that the animals were holding a meeting, and he judged by their snarling and growling that they were in great trouble.
passages.vernacular: 早晨來臨,佢哋又出發喇。仲冇走多遠,佢哋就聽到低沉嘅隆隆聲,像許多野獸嘅咆哮。托托輕聲嗚咽,但其他人都不害怕,佢哋沿住踩得好實嘅小路一直走,嚟到林中嘅一塊空地,嗰度聚集住成百上千各種各樣嘅野獸。有老虎、大象、熊、狼、狐狸同博物學上所有其他嘅動物,桃樂絲一時害怕喇。但獅子解釋講,呢啲動物正在開會,從牠哋嘅咆哮同吼叫判斷,牠哋遇到咗大麻煩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 早晨來臨,他們又出發了。還沒走多遠,他們就聽到低沉的隆隆聲,像許多野獸的咆哮。托托輕聲嗚咽,但其他人都不害怕,他們沿著踩得很實的小路一直走,來到林中的一塊空地,那裡聚集著成百上千各種各樣的野獸。有老虎、大象、熊、狼、狐狸和博物學上所有其他的動物,桃樂絲一時害怕了。但獅子解釋說,這些動物正在開會,從牠們的咆哮和吼叫判斷,牠們遇到了大麻煩。

passages.original: As he spoke several of the beasts caught sight of him, and at once the great assemblage hushed as if by magic. The biggest of the tigers came up to the Lion and bowed, saying:
passages.vernacular: 佢講話時,幾隻野獸睇到咗佢,頓時,龐大嘅聚集群像被施咗魔法一樣安靜下嚟。最大嘅老虎走到獅子面前,鞠躬講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說話時,幾隻野獸看到了他,頓時,龐大的聚集群像被施了魔法一樣安靜下來。最大的老虎走到獅子面前,鞠躬說:

passages.original: “Welcome, O King of Beasts! You have come in good time to fight our enemy and bring peace to all the animals of the forest once more.”
passages.vernacular: 「歡迎,噢百獸之王!你嚟得正是時候,嚟同我哋嘅敵人戰鬥,再次畀森林裡所有嘅動物帶嚟和平。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「歡迎,噢百獸之王!你來得正是時候,來與我們的敵人戰鬥,再次給森林裡所有的動物帶來和平。」

passages.original: “What is your trouble?” asked the Lion quietly.
passages.vernacular: 「你哋有乜嘢麻煩?」獅子平靜地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你們有什麼麻煩?」獅子平靜地問。

passages.original: “We are all threatened,” answered the tiger, “by a fierce enemy which has lately come into this forest. It is a most tremendous monster, like a great spider, with a body as big as an elephant and legs as long as a tree trunk. It has eight of these long legs, and as the monster crawls through the forest he seizes an animal with a leg and drags it to his mouth, where he eats it as a spider does a fly. Not one of us is safe while this fierce creature is alive, and we had called a meeting to decide how to take care of ourselves when you came among us.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋都受到威脅,」老虎回答,「有一個凶猛嘅敵人最近進咗呢片森林。嗰個係一個極其巨大嘅怪物,像一隻大蜘蛛,身體有大象咁大,腿像樹幹咁長。佢有八條咁樣嘅長腿,怪物喺森林裡爬行時,用一條腿抓住一隻動物,拖到嘴邊,像蜘蛛食蒼蠅一樣食掉。呢個凶惡嘅生物仲活住,我哋冇一個係安全嘅,我哋召開咗會議,商量如何保護自己,你就嚟到咗我哋中間。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們都受到威脅,」老虎回答,「有一個凶猛的敵人最近進了這片森林。那是一個極其巨大的怪物,像一隻大蜘蛛,身體有大象那麼大,腿像樹幹那麼長。它有八條這樣的長腿,怪物在森林裡爬行時,用一條腿抓住一隻動物,拖到嘴邊,像蜘蛛吃蒼蠅一樣吃掉。這個凶惡的生物還活著,我們沒有一個是安全的,我們召開了會議,商量如何保護自己,你就來到了我們中間。」

passages.original: The Lion thought for a moment.
passages.vernacular: 獅子想咗一會兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 獅子想了一會兒。

passages.original: “Are there any other lions in this forest?” he asked.
passages.vernacular: 「呢片森林裡有別嘅獅子嗎?」佢問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這片森林裡有別的獅子嗎?」他問。

passages.original: “No; there were some, but the monster has eaten them all. And, besides, they were none of them nearly so large and brave as you.”
passages.vernacular: 「冇;以前有啲,但怪物把牠哋全食喇。而且,牠哋冇一頭有你一半咁大、咁勇敢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有;以前有一些,但怪物把牠們全吃了。而且,牠們沒有一頭有你一半那麼大、那麼勇敢。」

passages.original: “If I put an end to your enemy, will you bow down to me and obey me as King of the Forest?” inquired the Lion.
passages.vernacular: 「如果我消滅你哋嘅敵人,你哋會向我鞠躬,服從我做森林之王嗎?」獅子問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果我消滅你們的敵人,你們會向我鞠躬,服從我做森林之王嗎?」獅子問。

passages.original: “We will do that gladly,” returned the tiger; and all the other beasts roared with a mighty roar: “We will!”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋會好樂意嗰樣做,」老虎回答;所有其他野獸發出一聲巨大嘅吼叫:「我哋願意!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們會很樂意那樣做,」老虎回答;所有其他野獸發出一聲巨大的吼叫:「我們願意!」

passages.original: “Where is this great spider of yours now?” asked the Lion.
passages.vernacular: 「你哋嗰隻大蜘蛛而家喺邊度?」獅子問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你們那隻大蜘蛛現在在哪裡?」獅子問。

passages.original: “Yonder, among the oak trees,” said the tiger, pointing with his forefoot.
passages.vernacular: 「喺嗰邊,橡樹中間,」老虎講,用前腳指住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「在那邊,橡樹中間,」老虎說,用前腳指著。

passages.original: “Take good care of these friends of mine,” said the Lion, “and I will go at once to fight the monster.”
passages.vernacular: 「好好照顧我呢幾個朋友,」獅子講,「我即刻去同怪物作戰。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好好照顧我這幾個朋友,」獅子說,「我馬上去同怪物作戰。」

passages.original: He bade his comrades good-bye and marched proudly away to do battle with the enemy.
passages.vernacular: 佢向同伴哋道別,驕傲地大步走去同敵人戰鬥。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他向同伴們道別,驕傲地大步走去同敵人戰鬥。

passages.original: The great spider was lying asleep when the Lion found him, and it looked so ugly that its foe turned up his nose in disgust. Its legs were quite as long as the tiger had said, and its body covered with coarse black hair. It had a great mouth, with a row of sharp teeth a foot long; but its head was joined to the pudgy body by a neck as slender as a wasp’s waist. This gave the Lion a hint of the best way to attack the creature, and as he knew it was easier to fight it asleep than awake, he gave a great spring and landed directly upon the monster’s back. Then, with one blow of his heavy paw, all armed with sharp claws, he knocked the spider’s head from its body. Jumping down, he watched it until the long legs stopped wiggling, when he knew it was quite dead.
passages.vernacular: 獅子找到大蜘蛛時,佢正躺住瞓覺,佢睇起嚟咁醜,佢嘅敵人厭惡地皺起鼻子。佢嘅腿確實同老虎講嘅一樣長,身體被粗糙嘅黑毛覆蓋。佢有一張大嘴,有一排一呎長嘅利齒;但佢嘅頭同矮胖嘅身體由一條像黃蜂腰嗰樣細嘅脖子連接。呢畀咗獅子一個提示,知道攻擊呢生物嘅最好方法,佢知道趁佢瞓住比醒住容易對付,於是猛地一跳,直接落喺怪物嘅背上。然後,佢用帶住鋒利爪子嘅沉重一掌,一擊把蜘蛛嘅頭從身體上打咗下嚟。佢跳下嚟,睇住佢,直到長腿唔再扭動,才知道佢完全死喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 獅子找到大蜘蛛時,它正躺著睡覺,它看起來那麼醜,他的敵人厭惡地皺起鼻子。它的腿確實和老虎說的一樣長,身體被粗糙的黑毛覆蓋。它有一張大嘴,有一排一呎長的利齒;但它的頭和矮胖的身體由一條像黃蜂腰那樣細的脖子連接。這給了獅子一個提示,知道攻擊這生物的最好方法,他知道趁它睡著比醒著容易對付,於是猛地一跳,直接落在怪物的背上。然後,他用帶著鋒利爪子的沉重一掌,一擊把蜘蛛的頭從身體上打了下來。他跳下來,看著它,直到長腿不再扭動,才知道它完全死了。

passages.original: The Lion went back to the opening where the beasts of the forest were waiting for him and said proudly:
passages.vernacular: 獅子回到林中空地,森林裡嘅野獸哋正在嗰度等佢,佢驕傲地講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 獅子回到林中空地,森林裡的野獸們正在那裡等他,他驕傲地說:

passages.original: “You need fear your enemy no longer.”
passages.vernacular: 「你哋再都唔使怕你哋嘅敵人喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你們再也不用怕你們的敵人了。」

passages.original: Then the beasts bowed down to the Lion as their King, and he promised to come back and rule over them as soon as Dorothy was safely on her way to Kansas.
passages.vernacular: 然後野獸哋向獅子鞠躬,尊佢為王,佢答應等桃樂絲安全上咗回堪薩斯嘅路,就回嚟統治牠哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後野獸們向獅子鞠躬,尊他為王,他答應等桃樂絲安全上了回堪薩斯的路,就回來統治牠們。

chapters.title: Chapter XXII: The Country of the Quadlings 第二十二章:夸德林人的國度

passages.original: The four travelers passed through the rest of the forest in safety, and when they came out from its gloom saw before them a steep hill, covered from top to bottom with great pieces of rock.
passages.vernacular: 四個旅行者安全地走過咗森林嘅其餘部分,從幽暗中走出嚟,睇到面前一座陡峭嘅山丘,從上到下覆蓋住大塊大塊嘅岩石。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 四個旅行者安全地走過了森林的其餘部分,從幽暗中走出來,看到面前一座陡峭的山丘,從上到下覆蓋著大塊大塊的岩石。

passages.original: “That will be a hard climb,” said the Scarecrow, “but we must get over the hill, nevertheless.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰將係一次艱難嘅攀爬,」稻草人講,「但我哋無論如何必須翻過呢座山。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那將是一次艱難的攀爬,」稻草人說,「但我們無論如何必須翻過這座山。」

passages.original: So he led the way and the others followed. They had nearly reached the first rock when they heard a rough voice cry out, “Keep back!”
passages.vernacular: 於是佢帶頭,其他人跟喺後面。佢哋快要走到第一塊岩石時,聽到一個粗暴嘅聲音喊道:「退後!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是他帶頭,其他人跟在後面。他們快要走到第一塊岩石時,聽到一個粗暴的聲音喊道:「退後!」

passages.original: “Who are you?” asked the Scarecrow.
passages.vernacular: 「你係邊個?」稻草人問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你是誰?」稻草人問。

passages.original: Then a head showed itself over the rock and the same voice said, “This hill belongs to us, and we don’t allow anyone to cross it.”
passages.vernacular: 然後一個頭從岩石上露咗出嚟,同一個聲音講:「呢座山屬於我哋,我哋不允許任何人越過佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後一個頭從岩石上露了出來,同一個聲音說:「這座山屬於我們,我們不允許任何人越過它。」

passages.original: “But we must cross it,” said the Scarecrow. “We’re going to the country of the Quadlings.”
passages.vernacular: 「但我哋必須越過佢,」稻草人講。「我哋要去夸德林人嘅國家。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但我們必須越過它,」稻草人說。「我們要去夸德林人的國家。」

passages.original: “But you shall not!” replied the voice, and there stepped from behind the rock the strangest man the travelers had ever seen.
passages.vernacular: 「但你哋不許!」嗰聲音回答,岩石後面走出一個旅行者哋見過嘅最奇怪嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但你們不許!」那聲音回答,岩石後面走出一個旅行者們見過的最奇怪的人。

passages.original: He was quite short and stout and had a big head, which was flat at the top and supported by a thick neck full of wrinkles. But he had no arms at all, and, seeing this, the Scarecrow did not fear that so helpless a creature could prevent them from climbing the hill. So he said, “I’m sorry not to do as you wish, but we must pass over your hill whether you like it or not,” and he walked boldly forward.
passages.vernacular: 佢相當矮而粗壯,有一個大頭,頭頂係平嘅,由一條滿係皺紋嘅粗脖子支撐住。但佢完全冇手臂,睇到呢個,稻草人不怕咁無助嘅生物能阻止佢哋爬山。所以佢講:「我好抱歉唔能夠照你嘅意思做,但無論你喜不鍾意,我哋必須越過你嘅山,」講完就大膽地向前走去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他相當矮而粗壯,有一個大頭,頭頂是平的,由一條滿是皺紋的粗脖子支撐著。但他完全沒有手臂,看到這個,稻草人不怕這麼無助的生物能阻止他們爬山。所以他說:「我很抱歉不能照你的意思做,但無論你喜不喜歡,我們必須越過你的山,」說完就大膽地向前走去。

passages.original: As quick as lightning the man’s head shot forward and his neck stretched out until the top of the head, where it was flat, struck the Scarecrow in the middle and sent him tumbling, over and over, down the hill. Almost as quickly as it came the head went back to the body, and the man laughed harshly as he said, “It isn’t as easy as you think!”
passages.vernacular: 像閃電一樣快,嗰人嘅頭向前射出,脖子伸長,頭頂嗰平嘅部分撞喺稻草人嘅中間,把佢撞得一路翻滾住滾下山去。頭幾乎同嚟時一樣快地縮回身體,嗰人粗聲笑住講:「冇你想嘅咁容易!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 像閃電一樣快,那人的頭向前射出,脖子伸長,頭頂那平的部分撞在稻草人的中間,把他撞得一路翻滾著滾下山去。頭幾乎和來時一樣快地縮回身體,那人粗聲笑著說:「沒有你想的那麼容易!」

passages.original: A chorus of boisterous laughter came from the other rocks, and Dorothy saw hundreds of the armless Hammer-Heads upon the hillside, one behind every rock.
passages.vernacular: 其他岩石嗰邊傳嚟一陣喧鬧嘅笑聲,桃樂絲睇到山坡上有上百個冇手臂嘅錘頭人,每塊岩石後面都有一個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其他岩石那邊傳來一陣喧鬧的笑聲,桃樂絲看到山坡上有上百個沒有手臂的錘頭人,每塊岩石後面都有一個。

passages.original: The Lion became quite angry at the laughter caused by the Scarecrow’s mishap, and giving a loud roar that echoed like thunder, he dashed up the hill.
passages.vernacular: 獅子對稻草人遭殃引起嘅笑聲相當生氣,佢發出一聲像雷聲般迴響嘅大吼,衝上山去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 獅子對稻草人遭殃引起的笑聲相當生氣,他發出一聲像雷聲般迴響的大吼,衝上山去。

passages.original: Again a head shot swiftly out, and the great Lion went rolling down the hill as if he had been struck by a cannon ball.
passages.vernacular: 又一個頭飛快地射出,大獅子像被炮彈擊中一樣滾下山去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 又一個頭飛快地射出,大獅子像被炮彈擊中一樣滾下山去。

passages.original: Dorothy ran down and helped the Scarecrow to his feet, and the Lion came up to her, feeling rather bruised and sore, and said, “It is useless to fight people with shooting heads; no one can withstand them.”
passages.vernacular: 桃樂絲跑下去扶稻草人站起嚟,獅子走到佢跟前,覺得相當瘀傷疼痛,講:「同會射頭嘅人戰鬥係冇用嘅;冇人能抵擋佢哋。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 桃樂絲跑下去扶稻草人站起來,獅子走到她跟前,覺得相當瘀傷疼痛,說:「同會射頭的人戰鬥是沒用的;沒有人能抵擋他們。」

passages.original: “What can we do, then?” she asked.
passages.vernacular: 「咁我哋能做乜嘢?」佢問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼我們能做什麼?」她問。

passages.original: “Call the Winged Monkeys,” suggested the Tin Woodman. “You have still the right to command them once more.”
passages.vernacular: 「叫飛猴,」鐵皮樵夫建議。「你仲有權再命令牠哋一次。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「叫飛猴,」鐵皮樵夫建議。「你還有權再命令牠們一次。」

passages.original: “Very well,” she answered, and putting on the Golden Cap she uttered the magic words. The Monkeys were as prompt as ever, and in a few moments the entire band stood before her.
passages.vernacular: 「好,」佢回答,戴上金帽子,講出魔咒。猴子哋像以前一樣迅速,幾分鐘內整群都站喺佢面前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好,」她回答,戴上金帽子,說出魔咒。猴子們像以前一樣迅速,幾分鐘內整群都站在她面前。

passages.original: “What are your commands?” inquired the King of the Monkeys, bowing low.
passages.vernacular: 「你有乜嘢吩咐?」猴王鞠躬問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你有什麼吩咐?」猴王鞠躬問。

passages.original: “Carry us over the hill to the country of the Quadlings,” answered the girl.
passages.vernacular: 「帶我哋越過呢座山到夸德林人嘅國家,」女孩回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「帶我們越過這座山到夸德林人的國家,」女孩回答。

passages.original: “It shall be done,” said the King, and at once the Winged Monkeys caught the four travelers and Toto up in their arms and flew away with them. As they passed over the hill the Hammer-Heads yelled with vexation, and shot their heads high in the air, but they could not reach the Winged Monkeys, which carried Dorothy and her comrades safely over the hill and set them down in the beautiful country of the Quadlings.
passages.vernacular: 「照辦,」猴王講,飛猴哋即刻把四個旅行者同托托抱喺懷裡,帶住佢哋飛走喇。佢哋飛過山時,錘頭人氣得大叫,把佢哋嘅頭高高射向空中,但夠不住飛猴,飛猴帶住桃樂絲同佢嘅同伴哋安全越過山丘,把佢哋放喺夸德林人美麗嘅國土上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「照辦,」猴王說,飛猴們馬上把四個旅行者和托托抱在懷裡,帶著他們飛走了。他們飛過山時,錘頭人氣得大叫,把他們的頭高高射向空中,但夠不著飛猴,飛猴帶著桃樂絲和她的同伴們安全越過山丘,把他們放在夸德林人美麗的國土上。

passages.original: “This is the last time you can summon us,” said the leader to Dorothy; “so good-bye and good luck to you.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係你最後一次能召喚我哋喇,」首領對桃樂絲講;「所以再見,祝你好運。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是你最後一次能召喚我們了,」首領對桃樂絲說;「所以再見,祝你好運。」

passages.original: “Good-bye, and thank you very much,” returned the girl; and the Monkeys rose into the air and were out of sight in a twinkling.
passages.vernacular: 「再見,好感謝你哋,」女孩回答;猴子哋升到空中,轉眼就唔見喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「再見,非常感謝你們,」女孩回答;猴子們升到空中,轉眼就不見了。

passages.original: The country of the Quadlings seemed rich and happy. There was field upon field of ripening grain, with well-paved roads running between, and pretty rippling brooks with strong bridges across them. The fences and houses and bridges were all painted bright red, just as they had been painted yellow in the country of the Winkies and blue in the country of the Munchkins. The Quadlings themselves, who were short and fat and looked chubby and good-natured, were dressed all in red, which showed bright against the green grass and the yellowing grain.
passages.vernacular: 夸德林人嘅國家睇起嚟富裕而快樂。有一塊接一塊成熟嘅穀物田,中間有鋪得好好嘅道路,仲有潺潺流動嘅漂亮小溪,上面有堅固嘅橋。籬笆、房子同橋都漆成鮮豔嘅紅色,就像溫基人國家漆成黃色、芒奇金人國家漆成藍色一樣。夸德林人自己矮而胖,睇起嚟圓滾滾、性情溫和,全身穿紅色,喺綠草同發黃嘅穀物襯托下顯得鮮豔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夸德林人的國家看起來富裕而快樂。有一塊接一塊成熟的穀物田,中間有鋪得很好的道路,還有潺潺流動的漂亮小溪,上面有堅固的橋。籬笆、房子和橋都漆成鮮豔的紅色,就像溫基人國家漆成黃色、芒奇金人國家漆成藍色一樣。夸德林人自己矮而胖,看起來圓滾滾、性情溫和,全身穿紅色,在綠草和發黃的穀物襯托下顯得鮮豔。

passages.original: The Monkeys had set them down near a farmhouse, and the four travelers walked up to it and knocked at the door. It was opened by the farmer’s wife, and when Dorothy asked for something to eat the woman gave them all a good dinner, with three kinds of cake and four kinds of cookies, and a bowl of milk for Toto.
passages.vernacular: 猴子哋把佢哋放喺一所農舍附近,四個旅行者走過去,敲咗敲門。開門嘅係農夫嘅妻子,桃樂絲向佢要點食嘅時,嗰女人畀佢哋大家做咗一頓好晚飯,有三種蛋糕同四種餅乾,還畀托托一碗牛奶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 猴子們把他們放在一所農舍附近,四個旅行者走過去,敲了敲門。開門的是農夫的妻子,桃樂絲向她要點吃的時,那女人給他們大家做了一頓好晚飯,有三種蛋糕和四種餅乾,還給托托一碗牛奶。

passages.original: “How far is it to the Castle of Glinda?” asked the child.
passages.vernacular: 「到格琳達嘅城堡有多遠?」細路問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「到格琳達的城堡有多遠?」孩子問。

passages.original: “It is not a great way,” answered the farmer’s wife. “Take the road to the South and you will soon reach it.”
passages.vernacular: 「不太遠,」農夫嘅妻子回答。「走南邊嗰條路,你哋好快就到喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不太遠,」農夫的妻子回答。「走南邊那條路,你們很快就到了。」

passages.original: Thanking the good woman, they started afresh and walked by the fields and across the pretty bridges until they saw before them a very beautiful Castle. Before the gates were three young girls, dressed in handsome red uniforms trimmed with gold braid; and as Dorothy approached, one of them said to her:
passages.vernacular: 謝過呢位好心嘅女人,佢哋重新出發,沿住田野走,過咗漂亮嘅橋,直到睇到面前一座好美麗嘅城堡。門前有三個年輕女孩,穿住鑲有金色穗帶嘅漂亮紅制服;桃樂絲走近時,其中一個對佢講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 謝過這位好心的女人,他們重新出發,沿著田野走,過了漂亮的橋,直到看到面前一座非常美麗的城堡。門前有三個年輕女孩,穿著鑲有金色穗帶的漂亮紅制服;桃樂絲走近時,其中一個對她說:

passages.original: “Why have you come to the South Country?”
passages.vernacular: 「你點解嚟南方國土?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你為什麼來南方國土?」

passages.original: “To see the Good Witch who rules here,” she answered. “Will you take me to her?”
passages.vernacular: 「嚟見統治呢度嘅好女巫,」佢回答。「你能帶我去見佢嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「來見統治這裡的好女巫,」她回答。「你能帶我去見她嗎?」

passages.original: “Let me have your name, and I will ask Glinda if she will receive you.” They told who they were, and the girl soldier went into the Castle. After a few moments she came back to say that Dorothy and the others were to be admitted at once.
passages.vernacular: 「告訴我你嘅名字,我去問格琳達願唔願意接見你。」佢哋講出咗自己係邊個,女兵走進城堡。過咗一會兒,佢回來講桃樂絲同其他人可以即刻進去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「告訴我你的名字,我去問格琳達願不願意接見你。」他們說出了自己是誰,女兵走進城堡。過了一會兒,她回來說桃樂絲和其他人可以馬上進去。

chapters.title: Chapter XXIII: Glinda the Good Witch Grants Dorothy's Wish 第二十三章:好女巫格琳達實現桃樂絲的願望

passages.original: Before they went to see Glinda, however, they were taken to a room of the Castle, where Dorothy washed her face and combed her hair, and the Lion shook the dust out of his mane, and the Scarecrow patted himself into his best shape, and the Woodman polished his tin and oiled his joints.
passages.vernacular: 不過,喺去見格琳達之前,佢哋被帶到城堡嘅一個房間,桃樂絲喺嗰度洗咗臉,梳咗頭髮,獅子抖掉鬃毛上嘅灰塵,稻草人把自己拍成最好嘅形狀,樵夫擦亮佢嘅錫,畀關節上咗油。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,在去見格琳達之前,他們被帶到城堡的一個房間,桃樂絲在那裡洗了臉,梳了頭髮,獅子抖掉鬃毛上的灰塵,稻草人把自己拍成最好的形狀,樵夫擦亮他的錫,給關節上了油。

passages.original: When they were all quite presentable they followed the soldier girl into a big room where the Witch Glinda sat upon a throne of rubies.
passages.vernacular: 當佢哋都整整齊齊喇,就跟住女兵走進一個大房間,女巫格琳達坐喺一個紅寶石王座上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當他們都整整齊齊了,就跟著女兵走進一個大房間,女巫格琳達坐在一個紅寶石王座上。

passages.original: She was both beautiful and young to their eyes. Her hair was a rich red in color and fell in flowing ringlets over her shoulders. Her dress was pure white but her eyes were blue, and they looked kindly upon the little girl.
passages.vernacular: 喺佢哋眼裡,佢既美麗又年輕。佢嘅頭髮係濃郁嘅紅色,流動嘅捲髮垂喺肩上。佢嘅裙子係純白色,但眼睛係藍色嘅,慈愛地睇住小女孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在他們眼裡,她既美麗又年輕。她的頭髮是濃郁的紅色,流動的捲髮垂在肩上。她的裙子是純白色,但眼睛是藍色的,慈愛地看著小女孩。

passages.original: “What can I do for you, my child?” she asked.
passages.vernacular: 「我嘅細路,我能為你做乜嘢?」佢問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我的孩子,我能為你做什麼?」她問。

passages.original: Dorothy told the Witch all her story: how the cyclone had brought her to the Land of Oz, how she had found her companions, and of the wonderful adventures they had met with.
passages.vernacular: 桃樂絲把佢嘅全部故事告訴咗女巫:龍捲風點樣把佢帶到奧茲國,佢點樣找到咗同伴,同佢哋所遇到嘅奇妙冒險。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 桃樂絲把她的全部故事告訴了女巫:龍捲風怎樣把她帶到奧茲國,她怎樣找到了同伴,和他們所遇到的奇妙冒險。

passages.original: “My greatest wish now,” she added, “is to get back to Kansas, for Aunt Em will surely think something dreadful has happened to me, and that will make her put on mourning; and unless the crops are better this year than they were last, I am sure Uncle Henry cannot afford it.”
passages.vernacular: 「我而家最大嘅願望,」佢補充講,「係回到堪薩斯,因為艾姆嬸嬸一定以為我出咗乜嘢可怕嘅事,嗰會使佢穿上喪服;除非今年嘅收成比去年好,我肯定亨利叔叔負擔不起。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我現在最大的願望,」她補充說,「是回到堪薩斯,因為艾姆嬸嬸一定以為我出了什麼可怕的事,那會使她穿上喪服;除非今年的收成比去年好,我肯定亨利叔叔負擔不起。」

passages.original: Glinda leaned forward and kissed the sweet, upturned face of the loving little girl.
passages.vernacular: 格琳達俯身吻咗呢個充滿愛心嘅小女孩嗰張甜美嘅仰起嘅臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 格琳達俯身吻了這個充滿愛心的小女孩那張甜美的仰起的臉。

passages.original: “Bless your dear heart,” she said, “I am sure I can tell you of a way to get back to Kansas.” Then she added, “But, if I do, you must give me the Golden Cap.”
passages.vernacular: 「願祝福臨到你親愛嘅心,」佢講,「我肯定我能告訴你回堪薩斯嘅方法。」然後佢補充講:「但係,如果我告訴你,你必須把金帽子畀我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「願祝福臨到你親愛的心,」她說,「我肯定我能告訴你回堪薩斯的方法。」然後她補充說:「但是,如果我告訴你,你必須把金帽子給我。」

passages.original: “Willingly!” exclaimed Dorothy; “indeed, it is of no use to me now, and when you have it you can command the Winged Monkeys three times.”
passages.vernacular: 「樂意!」桃樂絲喊道;「確實,佢而家對我冇用喇,你得到佢之後,可以三次命令飛猴。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「樂意!」桃樂絲喊道;「確實,它現在對我沒用了,你得到它之後,可以三次命令飛猴。」

passages.original: “And I think I shall need their service just those three times,” answered Glinda, smiling.
passages.vernacular: 「我想我正好需要牠哋服務呢三次,」格琳達微笑住回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想我正好需要牠們服務這三次,」格琳達微笑著回答。

passages.original: Dorothy then gave her the Golden Cap, and the Witch said to the Scarecrow, “What will you do when Dorothy has left us?”
passages.vernacular: 桃樂絲於是把金帽子畀咗佢,女巫對稻草人講:「桃樂絲離開我哋之後,你會做乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 桃樂絲於是把金帽子給了她,女巫對稻草人說:「桃樂絲離開我們之後,你會做什麼?」

passages.original: “I will return to the Emerald City,” he replied, “for Oz has made me its ruler and the people like me. The only thing that worries me is how to cross the hill of the Hammer-Heads.”
passages.vernacular: 「我會回翡翠城,」佢回答,「因為奧茲讓我做咗佢嘅統治者,人民都鍾意我。唯一讓我擔心嘅係點樣越過錘頭人嘅山丘。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我會回翡翠城,」他回答,「因為奧茲讓我做了它的統治者,人民也喜歡我。唯一讓我擔心的是怎樣越過錘頭人的山丘。」

passages.original: “By means of the Golden Cap I shall command the Winged Monkeys to carry you to the gates of the Emerald City,” said Glinda, “for it would be a shame to deprive the people of so wonderful a ruler.”
passages.vernacular: 「藉住金帽子,我會命令飛猴帶你到翡翠城嘅城門,」格琳達講,「因為剝奪人民咁樣一位奇妙嘅統治者係可惜嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「藉著金帽子,我會命令飛猴帶你到翡翠城的城門,」格琳達說,「因為剝奪人民這樣一位奇妙的統治者是可惜的。」

passages.original: “Am I really wonderful?” asked the Scarecrow.
passages.vernacular: 「我真嘅好奇妙嗎?」稻草人問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我真的很奇妙嗎?」稻草人問。

passages.original: “You are unusual,” replied Glinda.
passages.vernacular: 「你係同眾不同嘅,」格琳達回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你是與眾不同的,」格琳達回答。

passages.original: Turning to the Tin Woodman, she asked, “What will become of you when Dorothy leaves this country?”
passages.vernacular: 佢轉向鐵皮樵夫,問:「桃樂絲離開呢個國家之後,你會點樣?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她轉向鐵皮樵夫,問:「桃樂絲離開這個國家之後,你會怎樣?」

passages.original: He leaned on his axe and thought a moment. Then he said, “The Winkies were very kind to me, and wanted me to rule over them after the Wicked Witch died. I am fond of the Winkies, and if I could get back again to the Country of the West, I should like nothing better than to rule over them forever.”
passages.vernacular: 佢倚住斧頭,想咗一會兒。然後佢講:「溫基人對我好好,惡女巫死後,佢哋想要我統治佢哋。我鍾意溫基人,如果我能回到西方國土,我最想要嘅就係永遠統治佢哋。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他倚著斧頭,想了一會兒。然後他說:「溫基人對我非常好,惡女巫死後,他們想要我統治他們。我喜歡溫基人,如果我能回到西方國土,我最想要的就是永遠統治他們。」

passages.original: “My second command to the Winged Monkeys,” said Glinda “will be that they carry you safely to the land of the Winkies. Your brain may not be so large to look at as those of the Scarecrow, but you are really brighter than he is—when you are well polished—and I am sure you will rule the Winkies wisely and well.”
passages.vernacular: 「我畀飛猴嘅第二個命令,」格琳達講,「將係帶你安全到溫基人嘅土地。你嘅腦子睇起嚟可能不如稻草人嘅大,但你其實比佢更聰明——當你被擦亮嘅時候——我肯定你會明智而良好地統治溫基人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我給飛猴的第二個命令,」格琳達說,「將是帶你安全到溫基人的土地。你的腦子看起來可能不如稻草人的大,但你其實比他更聰明——當你被擦亮的時候——我肯定你會明智而良好地統治溫基人。」

passages.original: Then the Witch looked at the big, shaggy Lion and asked, “When Dorothy has returned to her own home, what will become of you?”
passages.vernacular: 然後女巫睇住嗰頭大而毛茸茸嘅獅子,問:「桃樂絲回到佢自己嘅家之後,你會點樣?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後女巫看著那頭大而毛茸茸的獅子,問:「桃樂絲回到她自己的家之後,你會怎樣?」

passages.original: “Over the hill of the Hammer-Heads,” he answered, “lies a grand old forest, and all the beasts that live there have made me their King. If I could only get back to this forest, I would pass my life very happily there.”
passages.vernacular: 「喺錘頭人嘅山丘嗰邊,」佢回答,「有一片宏偉嘅古老森林,住喺嗰度嘅所有野獸都擁立我做牠哋嘅王。如果我能回到呢片森林,我會喺嗰度好快樂地度過一生。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「在錘頭人的山丘那邊,」他回答,「有一片宏偉的古老森林,住在那裡的所有野獸都擁立我做牠們的王。如果我能回到這片森林,我會在那裡非常快樂地度過一生。」

passages.original: “My third command to the Winged Monkeys,” said Glinda, “shall be to carry you to your forest. Then, having used up the powers of the Golden Cap, I shall give it to the King of the Monkeys, that he and his band may thereafter be free for evermore.”
passages.vernacular: 「我畀飛猴嘅第三個命令,」格琳達講,「將係帶你到你嘅森林。然後,金帽子嘅力量用盡喇,我會把佢畀猴王,讓佢同佢嘅族群從此永遠自由。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我給飛猴的第三個命令,」格琳達說,「將是帶你到你的森林。然後,金帽子的力量用盡了,我會把它給猴王,讓他和他的族群從此永遠自由。」

passages.original: The Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman and the Lion now thanked the Good Witch earnestly for her kindness; and Dorothy exclaimed:
passages.vernacular: 稻草人、鐵皮樵夫同獅子而家誠懇地感謝好女巫嘅好意;桃樂絲喊道:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 稻草人、鐵皮樵夫和獅子現在誠懇地感謝好女巫的好意;桃樂絲喊道:

passages.original: “You are certainly as good as you are beautiful! But you have not yet told me how to get back to Kansas.”
passages.vernacular: 「你確實既善良又美麗!但你仲冇告訴我點回堪薩斯。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你確實既善良又美麗!但你還沒告訴我怎麼回堪薩斯。」

passages.original: “Your Silver Shoes will carry you over the desert,” replied Glinda. “If you had known their power you could have gone back to your Aunt Em the very first day you came to this country.”
passages.vernacular: 「你嘅銀鞋會帶你越過沙漠,」格琳達回答。「如果你早知道佢哋嘅力量,你到呢個國家嘅第一天就可以回到你嘅艾姆嬸嬸身邊喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你的銀鞋會帶你越過沙漠,」格琳達回答。「如果你早知道它們的力量,你到這個國家的第一天就可以回到你的艾姆嬸嬸身邊了。」

passages.original: “But then I should not have had my wonderful brains!” cried the Scarecrow. “I might have passed my whole life in the farmer’s cornfield.”
passages.vernacular: 「但嗰樣我就得唔到我奇妙嘅腦子喇!」稻草人喊道。「我可能一輩子待喺農夫嘅玉米田裡。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但那樣我就得不到我奇妙的腦子了!」稻草人喊道。「我可能一輩子待在農夫的玉米田裡。」

passages.original: “And I should not have had my lovely heart,” said the Tin Woodman. “I might have stood and rusted in the forest till the end of the world.”
passages.vernacular: 「我都得唔到我可愛嘅心喇,」鐵皮樵夫講。「我可能一直站喺森林裡生鏽,直到世界末日。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我也得不到我可愛的心了,」鐵皮樵夫說。「我可能一直站在森林裡生鏽,直到世界末日。」

passages.original: “And I should have lived a coward forever,” declared the Lion, “and no beast in all the forest would have had a good word to say to me.”
passages.vernacular: 「我會永遠做個膽小鬼,」獅子宣稱,「森林裡冇一頭野獸會對我講一句好話。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我會永遠做個膽小鬼,」獅子宣稱,「森林裡沒有一頭野獸會對我說一句好話。」

passages.original: “This is all true,” said Dorothy, “and I am glad I was of use to these good friends. But now that each of them has had what he most desired, and each is happy in having a kingdom to rule besides, I think I should like to go back to Kansas.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢都係真嘅,」桃樂絲講,「我好高興我對呢啲好朋友有用。但而家佢哋每個人都得到咗最想要嘅,而且每個人仲有一個王國可以統治而快樂,我想我想回堪薩斯喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這都是真的,」桃樂絲說,「我很高興我對這些好朋友有用。但現在他們每個人都得到了最想要的,而且每個人還有一個王國可以統治而快樂,我想我想回堪薩斯了。」

passages.original: “The Silver Shoes,” said the Good Witch, “have wonderful powers. And one of the most curious things about them is that they can carry you to any place in the world in three steps, and each step will be made in the wink of an eye. All you have to do is to knock the heels together three times and command the shoes to carry you wherever you wish to go.”
passages.vernacular: 「銀鞋,」好女巫講,「有奇妙嘅力量。其中一件最奇特嘅事係,佢哋能三步把你帶到世界上任何地方,每一步都喺眨眼之間完成。你要做嘅只係把鞋跟敲喺一起三次,命令鞋子把你帶到你想去嘅任何地方。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「銀鞋,」好女巫說,「有奇妙的力量。其中一件最奇特的事是,它們能三步把你帶到世界上任何地方,每一步都在眨眼之間完成。你要做的只是把鞋跟敲在一起三次,命令鞋子把你帶到你想去的任何地方。」

passages.original: “If that is so,” said the child joyfully, “I will ask them to carry me back to Kansas at once.”
passages.vernacular: 「如果係咁樣,」細路高興地講,「我要請佢哋即刻把我帶回堪薩斯。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果是這樣,」孩子高興地說,「我要請它們馬上把我帶回堪薩斯。」

passages.original: She threw her arms around the Lion’s neck and kissed him, patting his big head tenderly. Then she kissed the Tin Woodman, who was weeping in a way most dangerous to his joints. But she hugged the soft, stuffed body of the Scarecrow in her arms instead of kissing his painted face, and found she was crying herself at this sorrowful parting from her loving comrades.
passages.vernacular: 佢用雙臂摟住獅子嘅脖子,吻咗佢,溫柔地輕拍佢嘅大頭。然後佢吻咗鐵皮樵夫,佢哭嘅樣子對佢嘅關節好危險。但佢係用手臂抱住稻草人柔軟、塞滿嘢嘅身體,而唔係吻佢畫嘅臉,發現自己都因為同親愛嘅同伴哋傷心離別而哭喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她用雙臂摟住獅子的脖子,吻了他,溫柔地輕拍他的大頭。然後她吻了鐵皮樵夫,他哭的樣子對他的關節非常危險。但她是用手臂抱住稻草人柔軟、塞滿東西的身體,而不是吻他畫的臉,發現自己也因為與親愛的同伴們傷心離別而哭了。

passages.original: Glinda the Good stepped down from her ruby throne to give the little girl a good-bye kiss, and Dorothy thanked her for all the kindness she had shown to her friends and herself.
passages.vernacular: 好女巫格琳達從佢嘅紅寶石王座走下嚟,畀小女孩一個告別嘅吻,桃樂絲感謝佢對佢嘅朋友哋同自己所顯示嘅一切好意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好女巫格琳達從她的紅寶石王座走下來,給小女孩一個告別的吻,桃樂絲感謝她對她的朋友們和自己所顯示的一切好意。

passages.original: Dorothy now took Toto up solemnly in her arms, and having said one last good-bye she clapped the heels of her shoes together three times, saying:
passages.vernacular: 桃樂絲而家莊重地把托托抱喺懷裡,講咗最後一次再見,佢把鞋跟敲喺一起三次,講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 桃樂絲現在莊重地把托托抱在懷裡,說了最後一次再見,她把鞋跟敲在一起三次,說:

passages.original: “Take me home to Aunt Em!”
passages.vernacular: 「帶我回艾姆嬸嬸嗰度!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「帶我回艾姆嬸嬸那裡!」

passages.original: Instantly she was whirling through the air, so swiftly that all she could see or feel was the wind whistling past her ears.
passages.vernacular: 即刻佢喺空中旋轉,快得佢所能睇到或感覺到嘅只有風從耳邊呼嘯而過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 立刻她在空中旋轉,快得她所能看到或感覺到的只有風從耳邊呼嘯而過。

passages.original: The Silver Shoes took but three steps, and then she stopped so suddenly that she rolled over upon the grass several times before she knew where she was.
passages.vernacular: 銀鞋只走咗三步,然後佢突然停住,喺草地上滾咗好幾圈,才知道自己喺邊度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 銀鞋只走了三步,然後她突然停住,在草地上滾了好幾圈,才知道自己在哪裡。

passages.original: At length, however, she sat up and looked about her.
passages.vernacular: 不過,最後佢坐起嚟,環顧四周。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,最後她坐起來,環顧四周。

passages.original: “Good gracious!” she cried.
passages.vernacular: 「天呀!」佢喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天哪!」她喊道。

passages.original: For she was sitting on the broad Kansas prairie, and just before her was the new farmhouse Uncle Henry built after the cyclone had carried away the old one. Uncle Henry was milking the cows in the barnyard, and Toto had jumped out of her arms and was running toward the barn, barking furiously.
passages.vernacular: 因為佢坐喺堪薩斯寬闊嘅大草原上,佢面前就係龍捲風吹走舊房子後亨利叔叔建嘅新農舍。亨利叔叔正在穀倉院子裡擠牛奶,托托從佢懷裡跳出去,狂叫住跑向穀倉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為她坐在堪薩斯寬闊的大草原上,她面前就是龍捲風吹走舊房子後亨利叔叔建的新農舍。亨利叔叔正在穀倉院子裡擠牛奶,托托從她懷裡跳出去,狂叫著跑向穀倉。

passages.original: Dorothy stood up and found she was in her stocking-feet. For the Silver Shoes had fallen off in her flight through the air, and were lost forever in the desert.
passages.vernacular: 桃樂絲站起嚟,發現自己只穿住襪子。因為銀鞋喺佢空中飛行時掉喇,永遠失落喺沙漠裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 桃樂絲站起來,發現自己只穿著襪子。因為銀鞋在她空中飛行時掉了,永遠失落在沙漠裡。

chapters.title: Chapter XXIV: Home Again 第二十四章:回家

passages.original: Aunt Em had just come out of the house to water the cabbages when she looked up and saw Dorothy running toward her.
passages.vernacular: 艾姆嬸嬸剛從屋裡出嚟畀甘藍菜澆水,抬頭睇到桃樂絲向佢跑嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 艾姆嬸嬸剛從屋裡出來給甘藍菜澆水,抬頭看到桃樂絲向她跑來。

passages.original: “My darling child!” she cried, folding the little girl in her arms and covering her face with kisses. “Where in the world did you come from?”
passages.vernacular: 「我親愛嘅細路!」佢喊道,把小女孩摟喺懷裡,用吻蓋滿佢嘅臉。「你到底係從邊度嚟嘅?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我親愛的孩子!」她喊道,把小女孩摟在懷裡,用吻蓋滿她的臉。「你到底是從哪裡來的?」

passages.original: “From the Land of Oz,” said Dorothy gravely. “And here is Toto, too. And oh, Aunt Em! I’m so glad to be at home again!”
passages.vernacular: 「從奧茲國嚟嘅,」桃樂絲莊重地講。「托托都喺呢度。哦,艾姆嬸嬸!我又回到家喇,真高興!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「從奧茲國來的,」桃樂絲莊重地說。「托托也在這裡。哦,艾姆嬸嬸!我又回到家了,真高興!」
